manuals.title: Role and Powers of the BHA

entries.doc: Role and Powers of the BHA
entries.title: Scope and application of the Rules
path: Scope and application of the Rules
entries.html: (A)1These Rules incorporate the Codes, General Instructions, Safeguarding Regulations, Regulations for Point-to-Point Steeple Chases, Regulations for Arabian Horse Racing and published DBS Policy.

entries.doc: Role and Powers of the BHA
entries.title: Scope and application of the Rules
path: Scope and application of the Rules
entries.html:
(A)2The following are bound by these Rules:

2.1Persons; and

2.2anyone falling within Rule (A)3 below.

entries.doc: Role and Powers of the BHA
entries.title: Scope and application of the Rules
path: Scope and application of the Rules
entries.html:
(A)3Once bound, a Person will always remain subject to the Rules:

3.1to allow the BHA to investigate, and to take disciplinary action in relation to a breach of these Rules that took place whilst they were bound; and

3.2for so long as they owe a Debt.

entries.doc: Role and Powers of the BHA
entries.title: Scope and application of the Rules
path: Scope and application of the Rules
entries.html: (A)4The Rules do not create or confer any rights or other benefits under the Contracts (Rights of Third Parties) Act 1999.

entries.doc: Role and Powers of the BHA
entries.title: Objectives
path: Functions and powers of the BHA
entries.html: (A)5The BHA shall exercise all functions relating to the regulation and governance of horseracing in Great Britain and other matters as may be specified in these Rules from time to time in accordance with the BHA Objectives.

entries.doc: Role and Powers of the BHA
entries.title: Delegation of functions
path: Functions and powers of the BHA
entries.html:
(A)6The BHA may:

6.1delegate any of its powers or functions; or

6.2ratify the exercise of any power of the BHA by a person.

entries.doc: Role and Powers of the BHA
entries.title: Rules
path: Functions and powers of the BHA
entries.html:
(A)7The BHA may from time to time:

7.1implement new Rules;

7.2waive, amend or delete existing Rules;

7.3issue guidance in relation to the Rules; and/or

7.4waive, amend or delete existing guidance.

entries.doc: Role and Powers of the BHA
entries.title: Rules
path: Functions and powers of the BHA
entries.html:
(A)8To discharge its functions and to give effect to the operation of these Rules, the BHA may from time to time:

8.1take any action necessary for these purposes; and / or

8.2issue any directions or instructions.

entries.doc: Role and Powers of the BHA
entries.title: Fixtures
path: Functions and powers of the BHA
entries.html: (A)9The BHA shall fix the dates on which all Race Meetings are to be held.

entries.doc: Role and Powers of the BHA
entries.title: Fixtures
path: Functions and powers of the BHA
entries.html:
(A)10The BHA may:

10.1cancel any meeting, fixture or Race;

10.2alter the date of any meeting, fixture or Race;

10.3supervise or make such alterations to the programme of any meeting or conditions of any Race;

10.4order the transfer of any Race Meeting or Race to another Racecourse with or without existing engagements; or

10.5elect to divide Races.

entries.doc: Role and Powers of the BHA
entries.title: Fixtures
path: Functions and powers of the BHA
entries.html: (A)11The BHA may authorise, cancel or alter fixture fees, fixtures and races run under the Regulations for Point-to-Point Steeple Chases or the Regulations for Arabian Horse Racing.

entries.doc: Role and Powers of the BHA
entries.title: Applications
path: Functions and powers of the BHA
entries.html:
(A)12Where these Rules provide that a person must:

12.1seek or apply for consent, permission or approval from the BHA;

12.2complete a registration with the BHA; or

12.3request that the BHA take an administrative step, such as renewing a name in a register or entering a horse in a Race,

the BHA may:

12.4require the person to:

12.4.1use and comply with the relevant application form;

12.4.2pay the fee set out in the Fee Code; and / or

12.4.3provide any supporting documentation or information.

12.5refuse or grant the application; or

12.6grant the application subject to conditions or restrictions.

entries.doc: Role and Powers of the BHA
entries.title: Applications
path: Functions and powers of the BHA
entries.html: (A)13The BHA may withdraw, cancel or suspend the consent, permission, approval, registration or other administrative step if it considers it appropriate to do so.

entries.doc: Role and Powers of the BHA
entries.title: Forfeit List
path: Functions and powers of the BHA
entries.html: (A)14The BHA may keep and publish a record of any Debt on the Forfeit List.

entries.doc: Role and Powers of the BHA
entries.title: Forfeit List
path: Functions and powers of the BHA
entries.html:
(A)15The Forfeit List may include details of:

15.1the amounts due;

15.2the name(s) of the debtor(s); and

15.3such other information as the BHA may consider appropriate.

entries.doc: Role and Powers of the BHA
entries.title: Forfeit List
path: Functions and powers of the BHA
entries.html: (A)16Anyone named on the Forfeit List, or any equivalent list published by another Recognised Racing Authority, shall be a Disqualified Person for as long as their name appears on the list.

entries.doc: Role and Powers of the BHA
entries.title: Publication
path: Functions and powers of the BHA
entries.html: (A)17The BHA may from time to time publish any information relating to horseracing where it is in the interests of horseracing to do so.

entries.doc: Role and Powers of the BHA
entries.title: Exclusion of liability
path: Functions and powers of the BHA
entries.html: (A)18To the fullest extent permitted by the laws of England, Wales and Scotland, the BHA, its employees, any member of the licensing, disciplinary or appeal boards or panels, agents or those carrying out functions on its behalf shall not be liable to anyone bound by these Rules for any representation, statement, act or omission given, made or carried out relating to the discharge or operation of these Rules or the governance of horse racing.

entries.doc: Role and Powers of the BHA
entries.title: Exclusion of liability
path: Functions and powers of the BHA
entries.html: (A)19Nothing in Rule (A)18 shall exclude liability for fraud, or death or personal injury resulting from negligence.

entries.doc: Role and Powers of the BHA
entries.title: Notices
path: Functions and powers of the BHA
entries.html:
(A)20Any notice given to the BHA under these Rules must be given by one of the following methods:

20.1by sending by first class post or other service that provides for next day delivery to the BHA’s office at British Horseracing Authority, Holborn Gate, 26 Southampton Buildings, London, WC2A 1AN;

20.2by delivering the notice by hand to the BHA’s office at Holborn Gate, 26 Southampton Buildings, London, WC2A 1AN;

20.3by emailing to an email address as provided by the BHA; or

20.4any other method where directed to do so by the BHA.

entries.doc: Role and Powers of the BHA
entries.title: Deadlines
path: Functions and powers of the BHA
entries.html: (A)21For the purposes of complying with deadlines under these Rules, a notice shall be given or a document served on a given day provided that one of the steps set out in Rule (A)20 is completed before 5 p.m. that day.

entries.doc: Role and Powers of the BHA
entries.title: Deadlines
path: Functions and powers of the BHA
entries.html: (A)22Except where specified otherwise, where a deadline falls on a Saturday, Sunday or Bank Holiday it shall be extended to the next business day.

entries.doc: Role and Powers of the BHA
entries.title: Deemed Service
path: Functions and powers of the BHA
entries.html:
(A)23A notice given or document served under these Rules shall be deemed given or served as follows:

Method of ServiceDeemed Day of Service
First class post (or other service which provides for next- day delivery)The second day after it was posted, left with, delivered to or collected by the relevant service provider. If that day falls on a Saturday, Sunday or Bank Holiday, it shall be treated as being received on the next business day.
Delivering the document by handIf delivered by 4pm on a business day, that day;  otherwise, on the next business day after the day  on which it was delivered.
 EmailIf transmitted by 4pm on a business day, that day; otherwise, on the next business day after the day  on which it was transmitted.

entries.doc: Role and Powers of the BHA
entries.title: Deemed Service
path: Functions and powers of the BHA
entries.html: (A)24Where the BHA is the sending party, it may determine the form in which the notice, direction or other document is sent.

entries.doc: Role and Powers of the BHA
entries.title: Deemed Service
path: Functions and powers of the BHA
entries.html: (A)25The BHA may send any notice, communication or document using the last known contact details for the person in question.

entries.doc: Role and Powers of the BHA
entries.title: Deemed Service
path: Functions and powers of the BHA
entries.html: (A)26Persons must ensure that the BHA is informed of any change in contact details.

entries.title: Licensing Requirements
entries.html: (B)1A person cannot be a Trainer, a Jockey, a Valet or a Jockey’s Agent without having a Licence permitting them to do so issued by the BHA, or equivalent licence issued by another Recognised Racing Authority.

entries.title: Licensing Requirements
entries.html: (B)2No Person may operate an equine swimming pool without a Licence.

entries.title: Licensing Requirements
entries.html: (B)3A racecourse cannot stage a Race without having a Licence permitting it to do so issued by the BHA.

entries.title: Licence Applications
entries.html: (B)4The BHA may grant, refuse, withdraw and suspend Licences under these Rules.

entries.title: Licence Applications
entries.html: (B)5The BHA may grant a temporary Licence where there is good reason for one to be issued.

entries.title: Licence Applications
entries.html:
(B)6To obtain, vary or renew a Licence, a person or racecourse must:

6.1apply to the BHA within the stated notice period;

6.2use the relevant application form;

6.3meet all the criteria set out in, or accompanying, the relevant application form; and

6.4pay the fee set out in the Fee Code, if applicable.

entries.title: Licence Applications
entries.html:
(B)7If a Licence application is submitted electronically, the BHA must receive originals of all required documents within seven days of the electronic submission. Where the originals are not received by the deadline, the BHA may cancel:

7.1any Licence application; or

7.2any registration or other step taken in reliance on the information contained in the electronic submission.

entries.title: Licence Applications
entries.html: (B)8A person applying to be a Jockey must pass a medical examination.

entries.title: Licence Applications
entries.html: (B)9An application by a racecourse for a Licence shall identify the Racecourse Managing Executive who shall be responsible for ensuring compliance with the terms, restrictions and conditions of the Licence.

entries.title: Licence Applications
entries.html:
(B)10The BHA may require an applicant, or any other relevant person, to:

10.1provide further information or documentation; and / or

10.2attend an interview.

entries.title: Licence Applications
entries.html: (B)11The BHA may inspect any premises relevant to a Licence or Licence application at any time.

entries.title: Deciding a Licence Application
entries.html: (B)12The BHA shall decide each Licence application on its merits.

entries.title: Deciding a Licence Application
entries.html:
(B)13The BHA may:

13.1grant or refuse a Licence;

13.2grant a Licence with any conditions and / or restrictions attached; or

13.3refer a Licence application to the Licensing Committee for determination.

entries.title: Deciding a Licence Application
entries.html: (B)14The BHA shall give written notice of the outcome of a Licence application to the applicant.

entries.title: Referrals for determination of a Licence application
path: Referrals for determination of a Licence application
entries.html:
(B)15Except in relation to a Racecourse Licence application, the BHA shall refer a Licence application to the Licensing Committee for determination if it:

15.1does not consider the applicant to be a suitable person; or

15.2believes that it would be in the interests of racing, pending the outcome of an ongoing investigation or process, to refuse the Licence.

entries.title: Referrals for determination of a Licence application
path: Referrals for determination of a Licence application
entries.html:
(B)16If a Licence application is referred to the Licensing Committee, the BHA shall inform the applicant of:

16.1any facts relied upon by the BHA; and

16.2the reasons why the BHA made the referral.

entries.title: Referrals for determination of a Licence application
path: Referrals for determination of a Licence application
entries.html: (B)17The Licensing Committee shall determine a Licence application referred to it by the BHA in accordance with the Judicial Panel Code.

entries.title: Temporary Licences
entries.html: (B)18The Licensing Committee may grant a temporary Licence to an applicant whilst Licensing Committee proceedings involving that person are ongoing.

entries.title: Appeals
entries.html:
(B)19An applicant may, in accordance with the Judicial Panel Code, appeal a decision of the BHA in relation to a Licence to the Licensing Committee if the BHA:

19.1refuses the Licence for reasons other than that the absolute requirements on the application form were not met;

19.2grants the Licence subject to any conditions or restrictions;

19.3imposes any restrictions or conditions during the term of a Racecourse Licence; 

19.4withdraws or suspends a Licence at any time during its term; or

19.5consents to the appeal.

entries.title: Withdrawal and suspension of Licences
entries.html:
(B)20The BHA may withdraw a Licence if the following are not complied with at any time:

20.1the criteria set out in, or accompanying, the application form used to apply for the Licence; or

20.2anything upon which the issuance and / or continuation of the Licence was conditional.

entries.title: Withdrawal and suspension of Licences
entries.html:
(B)21Except in relation to a Racecourse Licence, the BHA may apply to the Licensing Committee to withdraw or suspend a Licence if it considers that:

21.1the Licence holder is no longer a suitable person to hold a Licence;

21.2it is in the best interests of horse racing pending the outcome of an ongoing investigation or process; or

21.3it is appropriate to do so.

entries.title: Withdrawal and suspension of Licences
entries.html:
(B)22A Licence shall cease to be valid if:

22.1it expires;

22.2it is withdrawn by the BHA or a Judicial Panel;

22.3it is suspended by the BHA, the Disciplinary Officer, or a Judicial Panel (for the period of suspension);

22.4it is relinquished by a holder; or

22.5subject to Rule (B)23, a holder of the Licence becomes a Disqualified Person.

entries.title: Withdrawal and suspension of Licences
entries.html: (B)23Rule (B)22.5 will apply to a Licensed Trainer whose name has been published on the Forfeit List from 14 days after the date of publication.

entries.title: Other referrals to the Licensing Committee
path: Other referrals to the Licensing Committee
entries.html: (B)24The BHA may refer any other matter concerning a Licence or registration to the Licensing Committee which shall deal with the matter in such manner as it considers appropriate, in accordance with the Judicial Panel Code so far as possible.

entries.title: APPEALING DECISIONS of the Licensing Committee
path: APPEALING DECISIONS of the Licensing Committee
entries.html: (B)25An applicant may appeal a decision of the Licensing Committee to the Appeal Board in accordance with the Judicial Panel Code, except where the decision was made by the Licensing Committee acting as an appellate body.

entries.title: Licensed Trainers
entries.html:
(B)26To train a horse for a Race, other than for a Hunters’ Steeple Chase or a Military Race, a person must:

26.1where the horse is trained in Great Britain, hold a Licence permitting them to train horses for the Race in question; or

26.2where the horse is trained outside of Great Britain, have an equivalent licence issued by a Recognised Racing Authority.

entries.title: Licensed Trainers
entries.html: (B)27A Licence held by a Trainer shall cease to be valid if the Trainer changes stables or their employment status without first obtaining the BHA’s consent.

entries.title: Licensed Trainers
entries.html: (B)28Each person in a Training Partnership shall be jointly and severally responsible for the obligations imposed on a Trainer under these Rules.

entries.title: Mandatory Licence conditions for Licensed Trainers
path: Mandatory Licence conditions for Licensed Trainers
entries.html:
(B)29Every Trainer as a condition of their Licence must:

29.1make sure that their training establishment is suitable and secure;

29.2only train horses at the premises named on the Licence;

29.3ensure that any persons who work for or with them in the training of racehorses are employed on terms that are no less favourable than those set out by the National Joint Council for Racing Staff from time to time; and

29.4comply with the Stable Employees Code.

entries.title: Restrictions for Trainers with a Jockey’s Licence
path: Restrictions for Trainers with a Jockey’s Licence
entries.html:
(B)30Any Trainer who is also a Jockey or authorised to ride in a race by another Recognised Racing Authority, may only ride in a Race if:

30.1they are riding a horse trained by them and that is the only horse in the Race trained by them, or

30.2they do not train any of the horses in the Race

entries.title: Jockeys
entries.html:
(B)31To ride a horse in a Race, a person must:

31.1be at least 16 years of age;

31.2be

31.2.1a Jockey and hold a Licence permitting them to ride in the Race in question; or

31.2.2an Overseas Jockey and permitted to ride in the Race in question.

entries.title: Jockeys
entries.html:
(B)32Any Jockey who, since last riding under these Rules, has sustained a:

32.1head injury or concussion;

32.2severe back injury;

32.3fracture or dislocation involving a limb bone or joints;

32.4fracture of the pelvis or spine; or

32.5any other significant injury or significant illness,

must inform the Chief Medical Adviser as soon as possible, or within 48 hours of their return to Great Britain if the injury was sustained abroad.

entries.title: Certificate Of Clearance
entries.html: (B)33Where required by another country’s racing authority, a Jockey may apply to the Racing Calendar Office for a certificate of clearance.

entries.title: Apprentice Jockeys and Conditional Jockeys
entries.html:
(B)34A person applying to be an Apprentice Jockey or Conditional Jockey must:

34.1be at least 16 years of age and less than 26 years of age;

34.2be in the full-time, paid employment of a Trainer who holds a Licence to train horses for:

34.2.1Flat Races (in the case of Apprentice Jockeys); or

34.2.2Jump Races (in the case of Conditional Jockeys);

34.3have entered into an Apprentice Jockey’s Agreement or a Conditional Jockey’s Agreement with that Trainer;

34.4make the application jointly with that Trainer; and

34.5be entitled to claim a weight allowance pursuant to the Weights and Handicapping Code.

entries.title: Apprentice Jockeys and Conditional Jockeys
entries.html:
(B)35A Licence held by an Apprentice Jockey or a Conditional Jockey shall cease to be valid if:

35.1they reach the age of 26 years;

35.2they leave the employment referred to on their Licence;

35.3Deleted

35.4the relevant Apprentice Jockey’s Agreement or Conditional Jockey’s Agreement is terminated; or

35.5they have not been entitled to claim a Jockey’s Allowance for six months.

entries.title: Apprentice Jockeys and Conditional Jockeys
entries.html: (B)36A Trainer must immediately inform the BHA if an Apprentice Jockey's Agreement or a Conditional Jockey's Agreement is terminated.

entries.title: Apprentice Jockeys and Conditional Jockeys
entries.html: (B)37If a Trainer who employs an Apprentice Jockey or Conditional Jockey ceases to hold a Licence then the Licence of any Apprentice Jockey or Conditional Jockey employed by that Trainer shall be valid for seven days thereafter on BHA approval.

entries.title: Amateur Jockey’s Licence
entries.html: (B)38A person applying to be an Amateur Jockey must have ridden no more than 25 winners in total under the rules of Recognised Racing Authorities, other than as an Amateur Jockey.

entries.title: Amateur Jockey’s Licence
entries.html:
(B)39A person is not eligible to be an Amateur Jockey if they have been paid directly or indirectly for riding in a race, other than as allowed by Rule (B)37, but the following are disregarded for the purpose of this Rule:

39.1any trophy that was advertised in the race conditions

39.2any expenses distributed by F.E.G.E.N.T.R.I.

39.3any assisted or free travel or accommodation in connection with participation in invitation races abroad, and approved by the relevant Recognised Racing Authority,

39.4any other payments, expenses or benefits approved by the BHA.

entries.title: Overseas Jockeys
entries.html:
(B)40An Overseas Jockey may be required to provide:

40.1an Official with evidence that they have a valid licence from a Recognised Racing Authority and any Medical Record Book issued by that Recognised Racing Authority; and/or

40.2any other relevant documentation.

entries.title: Overseas Jockeys
entries.html:
(B)41The BHA may:

41.1impose restrictions or conditions on an Overseas Jockey; or

41.2prohibit an Overseas Jockey from riding in a Race if:

41.2.1they have been resident in Great Britain for more than 30 consecutive days leading up to the Race; or

41.2.2it is appropriate to do so.

entries.title: Overseas Jockeys
entries.html:
(B)42Where a Race is confined to Apprentice Jockeys and Conditional Jockeys, an Overseas Jockey may ride in the Race if:

42.1they are entitled to claim a weight allowance pursuant to the Weights and Handicapping Code, or have been entitled to claim such an allowance within the past six months; and

42.2are less than 26 years of age.

entries.title: Jockeys' Agents
entries.html:
(B)43A Jockey's Agent may not act for a Jockey unless the appointment has been authorised by:

43.1the Jockey; and

43.2where the Jockey is an Apprentice Jockey or a Conditional Jockey, the Jockey's employing Trainer.

entries.title: Authority to Act
entries.html: (B)44The BHA must approve any Authorised Agent appointed to act on behalf of a Person.

entries.title: Racecourses
entries.html:
(B)45A Licence held by a Racecourse may be subject to such restrictions or conditions imposed by the BHA: 

45.1during the term of the Licence; and/or

45.2on renewal, 

and these may differ from those previously imposed.

entries.title: Racecourses
entries.html: (B)46The Racecourse Managing Executive must ensure that the Racecourse and all employees, representatives, and agents comply with the General Instructions.

entries.title: Racecourses
entries.html:
(B)47The Racecourse Managing Executive may, in accordance with the General Instructions, abandon a day’s racing or any Race where:

47.1there are exceptional circumstances;

47.2there is adverse weather; or

47.3the ground conditions are such that any part of the course is unsafe.

entries.title: Racecourses
entries.html:
(B)48Where a Racecourse Managing Executive proposes to abandon a day’s racing or any Race on the day of a meeting, as a result of:

48.1an emergency situation involving crowd safety or public order; or

48.2any direction given by the police or emergency services,

they must inform the Stewards before the decision to abandon is announced.

entries.title: Syndicator / Racing CLub Manager
entries.html: (B)49Any Syndicator or Racing Club Manager must have an approved licence to manage Syndicates or Racing Clubs

entries.title: Registration of Ownership
entries.html: (C)1A person must make an application to the BHA in order to be registered as an Owner.

entries.title: Registration of Ownership
entries.html:
(C)2The BHA shall only register the following ownership types:

2.1a Sole Owner;

2.2a Company;

2.3a Partnership;

2.4a Syndicate; or

2.5a Racing Club.

entries.title: Registration of Ownership
entries.html:
(C)3The BHA may refuse an application if:

3.1any of the following are or become a Disqualified Person or subject to any form of insolvency proceedings:

3.1.1the applicant;

3.1.2a director or company secretary of a company making the application;

3.1.3anyone with a legal, beneficial or equitable interest in any horses owned by the applicant; or

3.1.4any representative of the applicant;

3.2appropriate financial arrangements are not in place;

3.3information about the applicant is not provided on request; or

3.4it is appropriate to do so.

Cancellation

entries.title: Registration of Ownership
entries.html:
(C)4The BHA may cancel an Owner’s registration if:

4.1they do not have a horse registered with the BHA for a period of two consecutive years;

4.2any of the following are or become a Disqualified Person or subject to any form of insolvency proceedings:

4.2.1the Owner;

4.2.2a director or company secretary of a Company;

4.2.3anyone with a legal, beneficial or equitable interest in any horses owned by the Owner; or

4.2.4any representative of the Owner;

4.3information is not provided on request, or is false, inaccurate or incomplete;

4.4the criteria for the ownership type is not met;

4.5appropriate financial arrangements are not in place;

4.6a participant in a Syndicate does not have any interest in a horse owned by the Syndicate;

4.7there is a breach of the Syndicate Code; or

4.8it is appropriate to do so.

entries.title: Prohibitions on Ownership
entries.html:
(C)5A Professional Jockey must not own or part-own, or hold any equitable or beneficial interest in, any horse which is entered into or run in a Race:

5.1in Great Britain; or

5.2under the rules of any other Recognised Racing Authority, unless the Jockey is an Overseas Jockey,

entries.title: Prohibitions on Ownership
entries.html: (C)6Rule (C)5 shall not apply to horses that only run in Hunters’ Steeple Chases and/or Military Races.

entries.title: Owner’s Representatives
entries.html:
(C)7At least one person, who must also be an Owner, must be appointed to act on behalf of the following Owners:

7.1a Syndicate, such person(s) being called a Syndicator;

7.2a Racing Club, such person(s) being called a Racing Club Manager;

7.3a Stud Company, such person(s) being called a Stud Company Nominee.

entries.title: Owner’s Representatives
entries.html: (C)8At least one Registered Agent must be appointed to act on behalf of a Company.

entries.title: Owner’s Representatives
entries.html: (C)9The BHA may refuse an application to register an individual as an Owner’s Representative, or cancel an individual’s registration as an Owner’s Representative, if that individual is or becomes a Disqualified Person or subject to any form of insolvency proceedings, or if it is otherwise appropriate to do so.

entries.title: Owner’s Responsibilities
entries.html:
(C)10The following shall be responsible for the obligations imposed by the Rules on an Owner:

10.1a Sole Owner;

10.2a Company;

10.3an Owner’s Representative;

10.4each Partner in a Partnership;

10.5each Business Partner in a Business Partnership; or

10.6for horses subject to a Registered Lease, the lessee.

entries.title: Notification Obligations
entries.html:
(C)11The Owner or the Owner’s Representative must inform the BHA, within 21 days or, if sooner, before a relevant horse is next entered or runs in a Race, of:

11.1any change to the ownership interest in a horse;

11.2any changes to the company secretary or directors of a Company;

11.3any changes to the composition of a Syndicate;

11.4any changes to the Partners or Business Partners in a Partnership or Business Partnership;

11.5the names of all the members of a Racing Club on a given date;

11.6such other details as the BHA may request.

entries.title: Partnerships
entries.html: (C)12Each Partner in a Partnership must be an Owner.

entries.title: Syndicates
entries.html:
(C)13A Syndicator must be licensed and comply with the Syndicate Code if:

13.1the Syndicator is paid for that role; or

13.2the Syndicate is one that invites members of the public to join.

entries.title: Racing Clubs
entries.html:
13A. A Racing Club Manager must be licensed and comply with the Racing Club Code.

13A.1 Deleted

13A.2 Deleted

entries.title: Leases of horses
entries.html: (C)14Where an Owner is a lessee of a horse, the Owner must register the lease with the BHA.

entries.title: Leases of horses
entries.html: (C)15A Lease shall only be valid for up to 12 months.

entries.title: Leases of horses
entries.html: (C)16The BHA may publish the details of a Lease.

entries.title: Leases of horses
entries.html: (C)17A Lease shall cease to be registered if the lessee ceases to be an Owner.

entries.title: Transfer of engagements
entries.html:
(C)18Where ownership of a horse passes from one Owner to another, its engagements may be transferred provided that:

18.1the new Owner is registered in the country in which the horse is trained; and

18.2both parties confirm the transfer to the Racing Calendar Office.

entries.title: Racing colours
entries.html: (C)19An Owner must, prior to making a Declaration to Run for a horse, register racing colours with the Racing Calendar Office.

entries.title: Racing colours
entries.html: (C)20Registration of racing colours shall not be permitted where they are too similar to colours already registered.

entries.title: Racing colours
entries.html:
(C)21The BHA may cancel the registration of racing colours if it considers it appropriate.

Use of Racing Colours

entries.title: Racing colours
entries.html:
(C)22A horse must run in the racing colours registered by its Owner:

22.1in Great Britain, where the horse is trained in Great Britain, or

22.2otherwise, in a Recognised Racing Authority.

entries.title: Racing colours
entries.html: (C)23An Owner who has more than one set of registered racing colours must nominate which are their first colours.

entries.title: Racing colours
entries.html: (C)24Where two or more horses in a Race have similar racing colours, the BHA may require that one or more horses use alternative colours and shall determine what colours are suitable.

entries.title: Racing colours
entries.html: (C)25Where an Owner has more than one horse running in the same Race, or where the Owner’s horse shall not be carrying their first colours in a Race, the Owner or the Trainer must declare alternative colours to the Racing Calendar Office by 1pm on the day for making Declarations to Run.

entries.title: Racing colours
entries.html:
(C)26The BHA may permit the joint use of racing colours if there is sufficient connection between those who shall jointly use them.

Transfer of racing colours

entries.title: Racing colours
entries.html: (C)27The BHA shall permit a transfer of racing colours from an Owner to any of their Family Members.

entries.title: Racing colours
entries.html: (C)28The BHA may permit a transfer of racing colours from one Owner to another.

entries.title: Notification to the Stud Book Authority
path: Notification to the Stud Book Authority
entries.html: (C)29The legal owner must ensure that notification of the birth of a horse is provided to the Stud Book Authority (in such form as may be required from time to time) within 30 days of the horse’s birth.

entries.title: Naming horses
entries.html:
(C)30All horses’ names must be registered in accordance with the Horse Naming Code.

Reserving a name

entries.title: Naming horses
entries.html:
(C)31A person may apply to the Racing Calendar Office to reserve a name for a horse.

Changing a name

entries.title: Naming horses
entries.html:
(C)32A horse’s name may not be changed if:

32.1the horse has already raced under that name;

32.2the name is registered with a Recognised Racing Authority which has not consented to the name change; or

32.3the horse has been registered either as a broodmare or a stallion in:

32.3.1the Stud Book or the Non-Thoroughbred Register; or

32.3.2a stud book or non-thoroughbred register published by another Recognised Racing Authority.

entries.title: Reckoning the age of a horse
path: Reckoning the age of a horse
entries.html: (C)33For the purposes of these Rules, a horse’s date of birth is deemed to be 1 January in the year in which it is foaled.

entries.title: Registration of Non-Racing Agreements
entries.html: Deleted - see Rules (D)12 - (D)15

entries.title: Duty to promote welfare of horses
path: Duty to promote welfare of horses
entries.html: (D)1The Responsible Person must take all reasonable steps to ensure the safety and welfare of every horse in their care at all times.

entries.title: Duty to promote welfare of horses
path: Duty to promote welfare of horses
entries.html: (D)2A Person, whether mounted or dismounted, must not kick, strike or otherwise act improperly towards a horse, except for proper use of the whip whilst riding.

entries.title: Veterinary treatment and medication
entries.html:
(D)3The Responsible Person must ensure that:

3.1all treatment and medication administered to a horse in their care is:

3.1.1given in the best interests of the horse’s health and welfare; and

3.1.2justified by the horse’s medical condition, and

3.2they obtain and follow advice from a Veterinary Surgeon as to the appropriate treatment and level of training for a horse affected by injury or disease.

3.3the sensory hairs around the horse’s mouth, nose and eyes have not been clipped, shaven or in any other way removed, except for:

3.3.1hairs removed by a veterinarian on welfare grounds; or

3.3.2hairs removed by a veterinarian to allow veterinary treatment.

3.4no horse in their care is euthanised at an abattoir or slaughterhouse.

entries.title: Duty to report communicable diseases
entries.html:
(D)4If the Responsible Person has been informed by a Veterinary Surgeon, or should otherwise be aware, that a horse in their care is infected or is likely to be infected with a Communicable Disease, the Responsible Person must:

4.1observe any statutory requirements;

4.2immediately notify the BHA; and

4.3not remove, or allow to be removed, any horse in their care from the premises without the BHA’s consent.

entries.title: Security of horses
entries.html:
(D)5The Responsible Person must:

5.1maintain adequate security measures for horses at all times; and

5.2ensure that any staff are properly briefed and trained about these measures.

entries.title: Horse Passports
entries.html:
(D)6The Responsible Person must ensure that:

6.1each horse in their care has a valid Passport; and

6.2the Passport accompanies the horse and is always available for inspection; and

6.3if the horse is trained in Great Britain, the Passport and Vaccination App must declare that the horse is not intended for human consumption:

6.3.1in Section IX or any equivalent section; or

6.3.2if no such section exists, through an appropriate endorsement elsewhere in the Passport.

entries.title: Duty to check identity of a horse
path: Duty to check identity of a horse
entries.html:
(D)7A Responsible Person must:

7.1promptly check the identity of any horse that comes into their care against its Passport; and

7.2immediately report any discrepancies in the markings or microchip in a Passport to the Racing Calendar Office.

entries.title: Duty to check identity of a horse
path: Duty to check identity of a horse
entries.html: (D)8The BHA may check the identity of a horse at any time, and the Responsible Person must ensure that the correct horse is presented on each occasion.

entries.title: Neurectomy operations
entries.html: (D)9A horse which has undergone a Neurectomy cannot run in a Race.

entries.title: Neurectomy operations
entries.html:
(D)10If a horse has undergone a Neurectomy, the Responsible Person must:

10.1notify the Racing Calendar Office within seven days of the horse undergoing the procedure; and

10.2ensure that the Veterinary Surgeon carrying out the procedure endorses the horse’s Passport.

entries.title: Raceday restrictions and examinations
entries.html:
(D)11From 12.01 a.m. on the day of a Race in which a horse is declared to run:

11.1no substance may be administered to a horse except for normal feed and water offered by mouth, or water administered in small quantities using a bulb syringe; and

11.2the horse must not receive Manipulative Therapy,

until it has run in the Race or been withdrawn.

11A The BHA may order:

11A .1   the examination of any horse prior to a race

11A .2   that the medical records of any horse are provided.

Note: Failure to be comply with Rule 11A will result in the horse being Withdrawn

entries.title: Non-Racing Declaration
entries.html:
(D)12The following may notify the BHA of the permanent retirement of a horse from racing, by lodging a Non-Racing Declaration:

12.1the Owner;

12.2the legal owner;

12.3the Trainer, acting on behalf of the Owner (in which case there will be a 14-day period before the restriction is imposed).

entries.title: Non-Racing Declaration
entries.html:
(D)13A horse that is the subject of a Non-Racing Declaration is ineligible to race under:

13.1the Rules of Racing; and

13.2unless otherwise specified on the Non-Racing Declaration, the BHA Regulations for Point-to-Point Steeple Chases,

and the BHA shall seek reciprocation of this from other Recognised Racing Authorities where applicable.

entries.title: Non-Racing Declaration
entries.html: (D)14The BHA shall recognise and enforce a non-racing restriction registered with another Recognised Racing Authority, other than in exceptional circumstances.

entries.title: Non-Racing Declaration
entries.html: (D)15A Non-Racing Declaration shall not be revoked without the approval of the BHA.

entries.title: Horses injured on Racecourse Property
entries.html:
(D)16A Veterinary Surgeon on the Racecourse may direct that:

16.1an injured horse, or horse with a spread plate, is transported to the Racecourse Stables or the veterinary treatment box in the horse ambulance;

16.2a severely injured horse is humanely euthanised to prevent undue suffering to the horse.

entries.title: Horses injured on Racecourse Property
entries.html: (D)17If a Veterinary Surgeon on the Racecourse directs that a horse is to be humanely euthanised, they will obtain a second opinion from another Veterinary Surgeon and contact the Trainer or Owner if it is practicable to do so.

entries.title: Horses injured on Racecourse Property
entries.html: (D)18If it is not practicable to contact the Trainer or Owner, the Veterinary Surgeon may proceed with humane euthanasia without reference to them.

entries.title: Death of a horse
entries.html: (D)19A Veterinary Officer may order a post-mortem examination of any horse that dies on Racecourse Property.

entries.title: Death of a horse
entries.html: (D)20The Responsible Person must immediately notify the BHA of the death of a horse under their care.

entries.title: Duties of care and skill
entries.html:
(D)21A Trainer must train racehorses:

21.1with reasonable care and skill; and

21.2with due regard to:

21.2.1the interests of the Owners of horses in their care; and

21.2.2the safety of their employees and agents.

entries.title: Duties of care and skill
entries.html: (D)22A Trainer must ensure that any person mounted on a horse under their care and control is wearing a helmet and body protector which complies with the Equipment Code, and must carry out risk assessments regarding wearing body protectors at other times.

entries.title: Vaccinations
entries.html: (D)23Trainers must comply with the Vaccinations Code.

entries.title: Duty to keep Medication Records
entries.html: (D)24A Trainer is responsible for keeping a clear and accurate record of any Treatment administered to each horse in their care for at least 12 months in an Equine Medication Record Book.

entries.title: Duty to keep Medication Records
entries.html:
(D)25Each entry in an Equine Medication Record Book must:

25.1be made within 48 hours of administration of any Treatment or, if administration did not take place at the yard, as soon as the horse returns;

25.2contain the following information:

25.2.1registered name of the horse or, if it is unnamed, the registered name of the dam and the year of foaling;

25.2.2brand name or active ingredient of the Treatment used;

25.2.3start and end date of the Treatment;

25.2.4method of administration;

25.2.5quantifiable dosage of Treatment, to include any changes to dosage during the Treatment;

25.2.6frequency of administration, to include any changes in frequency during the Treatment; and

25.2.7name of the person administering the Treatment and whether that person is a Veterinary Surgeon.

entries.title: Duty to keep Medication Records
entries.html: (D)26Veterinary practice records that contain the information required for an Equine Medication Record Book entry shall be sufficient if they are available in the yard and cross-referenced in the Equine Medication Record Book.

entries.title: Duty to keep Medication Records
entries.html: (D)27Equine Medication Record Books must be made available for inspection when required by the BHA.

entries.title: Information about gelding a horse
entries.html:
(D)28A Trainer must notify the Racing Calendar Office if a horse in their care has been gelded:

28.1by no later than Closing for the horse’s next Race; or

28.2by the next Scratching Deadline or deadline for Confirmation of Entry, if the horse has an entry for an Early Closer.

entries.title: Horses of Ambiguous Sex
entries.html: (D)29A Responsible Person must, as soon as possible, notify the Racing Calendar Office when a horse under their care and control is found to be of Ambiguous Sex.

entries.title: Information about Wind Surgery
entries.html: (D)30A Trainer must notify the Racing Calendar Office on each occasion a horse in their care has had Wind Surgery. Notification must be made before the horse is declared to run, but is not necessary if the horse has never previously raced.

entries.title: Information about suprachoroidal cyclosporine implants
entries.html:
(D)31A Trainer must notify the BHA if a horse in their care has a suprachoroidal cyclosporine implant:

31.1if in training within seven days of the surgery; or

31.2whenever the horse enters training,

by sending a certificate signed by a Veterinary Surgeon.

entries.title: Notification Of Pregnant Horses
entries.html:
(D)32A Trainer must notify the BHA if a horse in their care is pregnant: 

32.1within 25 days of the last covering, or 

32.2as soon as the horse enters training 

whichever is the later, and the notification must include the last covering date.

entries.title: Notification Of Pregnant Horses
entries.html: (D)33If, after notification, the pregnancy is lost the Trainer must notify the BHA as soon as reasonably practicable.

entries.title: Information about new horses
entries.html:
(D)34A Trainer must inform the Racing Calendar Office of any:

34.1horse that enters or leaves their care; and

34.2change in ownership of a horse in their care,

within three days or, if earlier, before any Transaction Notice is made for the horse.

entries.title: Information about new horses
entries.html: (D)35Where a horse was foaled outside Great Britain, Ireland or the Channel Islands and enters Great Britain for the first time, the Trainer must apply for the horse’s name to be registered before any Transaction Notice is made for the horse.

entries.title: Information about new horses
entries.html: (D)36Where a horse arrives from outside Great Britain or Ireland the Trainer must provide the Racing Calendar Office with details of the horse’s racecourse performances before any Transaction Notice is made for the horse.

entries.title: Racing Outside Great Britain
entries.html:
Information about a horse running in a race outside Great Britain and Ireland 

(D)37Rule (D)37 and Rule (D)38 apply where a horse travels to another country to race run under the rules of another country’s racing authority.

entries.title: Racing Outside Great Britain
entries.html:
(D)38A Trainer must give details of a horse’s performance in any race run outside of Great Britain and Ireland to the  Racing Calendar Office:

38.1within 48 hours of the horse’s return to Great Britain; or

38.2if the horse has an Entry, as soon as the horse returns to Great Britain.

entries.title: Racing Clearance Notification
entries.html: (D)39Where a Recognised Racing Authority requires a Racing Clearance Notification, a request must be made to the Racing Calendar Office no later than the day prior to the deadline for the pre-race day declaration for the relevant race..

entries.title: Entering a Horse for a Race
path: Entering a Horse for a Race
entries.html:
(E)1To run in a Race a horse must be:

1.1qualified in accordance with the Running Requirements Code; and

1.2entered in accordance with the Race Entry Code.

entries.title: Overnight Accomodation
entries.html: (E)2If a Trainer requires overnight accommodation at a racecourse for a stable employee and/or a horse, the Trainer must submit a written application to the racecourse by 1pm on the day before they are due to arrive.

entries.title: Equipment
entries.html: (E)3A horse’s equipment must comply with and be used in accordance with the requirements of the Equipment Code when the horse is on Racecourse Property.

entries.title: Advertising
entries.html: (E)4Jockeys and Trainers must comply with, and Trainers must ensure their Stable Employees comply with, the Sponsorship Codes of Conduct.

entries.title: Advertising
entries.html: (E)5Any form of advertising carried by a horse on a Racecourse must first be approved by the BHA.

entries.title: Advertising
entries.html:
(E)6The BHA may:

6.1prohibit the advertisement in the Racing Calendar of any Race or Race Meeting;

6.2determine the circumstances in which sponsorship is permitted for or in connection with horseracing; and

6.3approve any sponsorship agreements, subject to such restrictions or conditions as it may determine.

entries.title: On Course Declarations
entries.html:
(E)7A Trainer must ensure that:

7.1a raceday Privileges request is submitted via the designated platform for each horse for which they want to request Privileges no later than 1pm on the day before the Race;

7.2they have checked the weights and colours for their horse in the racecard and that the Clerk of the Scales is informed if any is incorrect.

entries.title: Requirement to use official racecourse stables
path: Requirement to use official racecourse stables
entries.html: (E)8A Trainer must ensure that their horse is in the Racecourse Stables at least 45 minutes before the advertised start time for the Race in which the horse is to run.

entries.title: Restrictions on a horse whilst on Racecourse Property
path: Restrictions on a horse whilst on Racecourse Property
entries.html:
(E)9Once the Equine Welfare Integrity Officers have commenced their duties on Racecourse Property:

9.1a horse cannot leave Racecourse Property, unless:

9.1.1to move  between the Racecourse Stables and the Racecourse; or

9.1.2to go to or from any gallops which are not on Racecourse Property; or

9.1.345 minutes has elapsed since the horses Race, except where permission has been granted by a Veterinary Officer or Equine Welfare Integrity Officer. 

9.2the horse must not be stood in ice or iced water, or have a cooling device (including ice boots or bandages, or ice bags) applied to any part of the horse, unless approved by the Veterinary Officer,

until the horse has either run in the Race or been withdrawn.

9A   Once the Equine Welfare Integrity Officers have commenced their duties on Racecourse Property no equipment, save for equipment expressly permitted under the Rules of Racing, that is designed or advertised to have an effect on any mammalian body system, including but not limited to, magnetic boots, magnetic rugs, and massage pads may be used or brought onto Racecourse Property, unless approved by the Veterinary Officer.

entries.title: Restrictions on a horse whilst on Racecourse Property
path: Restrictions on a horse whilst on Racecourse Property
entries.html: (E)10Once the Equine Welfare and Integrity Officers have commenced their duties on Racecourse Property, no substance may be administered to a horse except for normal feed and water offered by mouth, or water administered in small quantities using a bulb syringe, unless otherwise approved by a Veterinary Officer.

entries.title: Restrictions on a horse whilst on Racecourse Property
path: Restrictions on a horse whilst on Racecourse Property
entries.html: (E)11Any medical treatment given to a horse on Racecourse Property must first be authorised by the Veterinary Officer, except where a horse needs to be humanely euthanised and it is not possible to consult the Veterinary Officer first.

entries.title: Prohibition on bringing horses affected with ringworm to a Racecourse
path: Prohibition on bringing horses affected with ringworm to a Racecourse
entries.html: (E)12A Trainer must not bring a horse infected with ringworm onto Racecourse Property.

entries.title: Prohibition on bringing horses affected with ringworm to a Racecourse
path: Prohibition on bringing horses affected with ringworm to a Racecourse
entries.html: (E)13If a horse is showing signs of ringworm, the Trainer of the horse must have a Certificate of Non-Contagiousness before they take the horse onto Racecourse Property.

entries.title: Equipment requirements
entries.html:
(E)14Trainers must ensure, in relation to the equipment of any horse in their care on Racecourse Property, that:

14.1horses are shod in accordance with the Equipment Code;

14.2all reins are attached to the bridle in an approved manner; and

14.3all other equipment worn by the horse is in a serviceable condition and properly fitted.

entries.title: General
entries.html: (E)15A Jockey must weigh out for each Race in which they are declared to ride, except that they shall not be permitted to do so if they are 4lbs or more over weight.

entries.title: General
entries.html: (E)16An Amateur Jockey must present their Medical Record Book if requested by a Racecourse Medical Officer or an Official.

entries.title: General
entries.html: (E)17Weighing out must be completed 15 minutes before the start of the Race.

entries.title: General
entries.html:
(E)18A Jockey must:

18.1weigh out wearing the correct colours, and present their colours cap and number cloth to the Clerk of the Scales; and

18.2place on the scales all equipment to be worn or carried in the Race, except for Excluded Equipment.

entries.title: General
entries.html: (E)19All weights shall be rounded down to the nearest 1lb unit.

entries.title: General
entries.html: (E)20Jockeys will be given a 4lb safety allowance.

entries.title: General
entries.html:
(E)21After weighing out for a Race both the Jockey and the Trainer are responsible for ensuring that:

21.1the Jockey’s saddle is not left unattended or taken back into the Jockey’s changing room;

21.2the clothing and equipment a Jockey wore when weighing out is not changed except that the girth or surcingle can be changed if they do not fit;

21.3the Jockey does not accept anything from, or give anything to, another person which may affect the Jockey’s weight; and

21.4no lead is added to or removed from the Jockey’s weight cloth.

entries.title: General
entries.html: (E)22A Jockey must ride the horse for which they have been weighed out.

entries.title: General
entries.html: (E)23The Trainer, or representative of the Trainer, of a horse to be ridden by an Apprentice Jockey or Conditional Jockey must be present when the Apprentice Jockey or Conditional Jockey is weighed out.

entries.title: Declaration of unfitness to ride
entries.html:
(E)24If a Jockey has sustained an injury listed in Rule (B)32, and/or has been declared unfit to ride, they must not ride in a Race unless they are declared fit by:

24.1a Racecourse Medical Officer; or

24.2where required by the BHA, the Chief Medical Adviser.

entries.title: The course
path: Requirements before proceeding to the start
entries.html:
(E)25Before riding in a Race, Jockeys must:

25.1familiarise themselves with the course they are to ride; and

25.2for Races started from starting stalls, know the draw number for their horse and ensure they are loaded into and start from the correct stall.

entries.title: Requirements before mounting
path: Requirements before proceeding to the start
entries.html: (E)26A horse being led on Racecourse Property must be fitted with a bridle, or a chifney attached to a headcollar.

entries.title: Requirements before mounting
path: Requirements before proceeding to the start
entries.html: (E)27When on Racecourse Property, a person may only lead one horse at a time.

entries.title: Requirements before mounting
path: Requirements before proceeding to the start
entries.html:
(E)28A Trainer must ensure that each of their horses:

28.1carries the correct number cloth and it is clearly visible;

28.2carries at least the correct weight; 

28.3is led by an attendant wearing the correct number armband; and

28.4where applicable, carries a BHA approved speed sensing device in the number cloth.

entries.title: Requirements before mounting
path: Requirements before proceeding to the start
entries.html: (E)29A Trainer must ensure that their horse is in the parade ring by the time displayed in the weighing room.

entries.title: Requirements before mounting
path: Requirements before proceeding to the start
entries.html: (E)30A Trainer must ensure that their horse is properly saddled, and any sheets or rugs are removed, before the horse goes to the start.

entries.title: Mounting, Parades and proceeding to the start
path: Requirements before proceeding to the start
Mounting, Parades and proceeding to the start
entries.html: (E)31All persons in the pre-parade ring, the parade ring or that are involved in a parade must obey the instructions of BHA Officials and racecourse officials.

entries.title: Mounting, Parades and proceeding to the start
path: Requirements before proceeding to the start
Mounting, Parades and proceeding to the start
entries.html:
(E)32Subject to any additional requirements imposed by the Racecourse, the following may enter the parade ring:

32.1an Owner, Trainer, horse attendant or Jockey of a horse which is to run in the next Race;

32.2a horse that has been Declared to Run; and

32.3a horse for which permission has been given by the Stewards.

entries.title: Mounting, Parades and proceeding to the start
path: Requirements before proceeding to the start
Mounting, Parades and proceeding to the start
entries.html: (E)33Jockeys shall mount their horse and proceed to the start as directed by BHA Officials or racecourse officials.

entries.title: Trainers’ responsibilities for Apprentice Jockeys and Conditional Jockeys before the start
path: Requirements before proceeding to the start
Trainers’ responsibilities for Apprentice Jockeys and Conditional Jockeys before the start
entries.html:
(E)34A Trainer that employs an Apprentice Jockey or Conditional Jockey must ensure:

34.1the fit condition of any saddle used by them;

34.2that they:

34.2.1arrive at any Racecourse at which they are declared to ride on time;

34.2.2acquaint themselves with every course, to include walking the course on the first occasion they ride there.

34.2.3are aware that they must have their girths checked at the start;

34.2.4are aware that they must report any concerns to the Starter or assistant Starter;

34.2.5comply with all requirements of the Equipment Code; and

34.2.6are aware that they must remove the blindfold from the horse before the start of the Race, where applicable.

entries.title: Trainers’ Representatives
entries.html:
(E)35A Trainer must appoint a representative to undertake all of their responsibilities if the Trainer is unable to attend a Racecourse where they have a horse running, including:

35.1attending any Stewards’ Enquiry on the Trainer’s behalf;

35.2knowing the instructions given to the Jockey by the Trainer; and

35.3being able to inform the Stewards whether the Jockey has complied with such instructions,

but only a representative that is a Trainer or a Stable Employee shall be permitted to enter the Racecourse Stables.

entries.title: Trainers’ Representatives
entries.html: (E)36A Trainer is responsible for the acts and omissions of their representatives.

entries.title: Access on the Racecourse
entries.html:
Weighing room and Jockeys’ changing room

(E)37No Person except those authorised by the BHA may enter the weighing room.

entries.title: Access on the Racecourse
entries.html:
(E)38No Person other than Jockeys or Valets may enter the Jockey’s changing room except where permission has been obtained from the BHA.

Racecourse Stables

entries.title: Access on the Racecourse
entries.html:
(E)39To enter the Racecourse Stables:

39.1all persons must obtain consent from the Equine Welfare Integrity Officer;

39.2Licensed Trainers and Stable Employees must show a valid BHA Identity Card; and

39.3attendants for Hunters’ Steeple Chase and Military Race runners and horses trained outside Great Britain must show photo identification.

entries.title: Access on the Racecourse
entries.html: (E)40A Trainer who enters Racecourse Stables must comply, and must ensure that their Stable Employees comply, with any directions given to them by BHA Officials.

entries.title: Access on the Racecourse
entries.html: (E)41No more than 3 people per horse shall be given access to Racecourse Stables.

entries.title: Remaining on Racecourse Property
entries.html: (E)42During the Restricted Period a Restricted Person must not leave and return to Racecourse Property without the permission of a BHA Official.

entries.title: Communication Devices
entries.html:
(E)43Deleted

43.1Deleted

43.2Deleted

entries.title: Communication Devices
entries.html: (E)44Deleted

entries.title: Getting to the start
entries.html: (F)1Trainers and Jockeys must ensure that their horses are ready to start on time.

entries.title: Getting to the start
entries.html: (F)2Horses must be ridden to the start.

entries.title: Getting to the start
entries.html:
(F)3Horses may not be led on the course on the way to the start, except:

3.1when in a Parade; or

3.2with the prior permission of the Stewards.

entries.title: Getting to the start
entries.html: (F)4Jockeys are not permitted to jump a fence or hurdle before the start of a Race.

entries.title: Getting to the start
entries.html:
(F)5If a Jockey remounts after leaving the parade ring they must:

5.1be assessed by a Racecourse Medical Officer or ambulance paramedic; or

5.2inform the Starter that they remounted,

before riding in the Race.

entries.title: At the start
entries.html:
(F)6All Persons at the start must:

6.1obey the Starter; and

6.2comply with the Starting Procedures Code.

entries.title: At the start
entries.html: (F)7No person shall be allowed on the course at the start without the permission of the Starter.

entries.title: At the start
entries.html: (F)8An Apprentice Jockey or Conditional Jockey (or an equivalent Overseas Jockey) must ensure their girths are checked at the start.

entries.title: Withdrawal of horses at the start
path: Withdrawal of horses at the start
entries.html:
(F)9In a Race started from starting stalls, a horse will be withdrawn if it:

9.1refuses to enter the stalls; or

9.2is not mounted at the ‘Off’.

entries.title: Withdrawal of horses at the start
path: Withdrawal of horses at the start
entries.html:
(F)10A horse may be withdrawn if it:

10.1will be unable to start on time;

10.2is unruly; or

10.3there is another good reason.

entries.title: False starts
entries.html: (F)11The signal for a false start is the waving of the Starting Flag.

entries.title: False starts
entries.html:
(F)12A Starter shall declare a false start:

12.1if any faulty action of the starting gate or starting stalls has meant that there has not been a fair start;

12.2when a horse has broken away before the Race has been declared ‘Off’; 

12.3if the Starter releases the starting gate or starting stalls for safety reasons but does not intend to start the Race; or

12.4if the recall procedures have been initiated.

entries.title: False starts
entries.html: (F)13Where a false start has been declared the Jockeys must return to the start.

entries.title: False starts
entries.html:
(F)14A horse shall be withdrawn if, following a false start and before the Race has restarted:

14.1in a Flat Race, it completes the course; or

14.2in a Jump Race, it either completes a circuit of the course, unseats its Jockey other than at the start, or falls.

entries.title: Stalls Tests
entries.html: (F)15All Persons must comply with the Stalls Test Code.

entries.title: Stalls Tests
entries.html: (F)16Any horse reported by a Starter for a Stalls Test cannot run in a Race started from starting stalls until the day after it has passed a Stalls Test, or gained an equivalent certificate from a Recognised Racing Authority.

entries.title: Stalls Tests
entries.html:
(F)17A Starter may report a horse for a Stalls Test if the horse:

17.1failed to enter the starting stalls;

17.2unnecessarily delayed the start; or

17.3was unruly.

entries.title: Stalls Tests
entries.html:
(F)18A Starter may give a Trainer a warning in respect of a horse if:

18.0.1the horse was unruly; or

18.0.2a Late Load Request was requested for the horse.

18.1Subject to paragraph 18.2 below, Late Load Request(s) are restricted to horses that have had a demonstrative behaviour reason inside of the starting stalls as identified in a previous race in Great Britain.

18.2A horse having its debut run will be ineligible for a Late Load Request unless it has undertaken a pre-race assessment showing a demonstrative behaviour concern inside of the starting stalls.

entries.title: Stalls Tests
entries.html: (F)19If a Trainer is given three warnings in respect of the same horse within a 12 month period, the horse must complete a Stalls Test.

entries.title: Stalls Tests
entries.html: (F)20Where a horse has completed a Stalls Tests as a result of behaviour inside the starting stalls, any further Late Load Request(s) for that horse will not result in additional warnings for a 12-month period commencing from the date of the Starters Report

entries.title: Stalls Tests
entries.html: (F)21Where a horse is subject to a third Starter’s report, it may not attempt a Stalls Test for six months.

entries.title: Walk Overs
entries.html:
(F)22A Race shall be a walk over if:

22.1only one horse is declared a runner; 

22.2only one horse is ready to start; or

22.3only one horse returns to the start following a false start.

entries.title: Walk Overs
entries.html: (F)23Deleted.

entries.title: Remounting
entries.html: (F)24Any Jockey that has remounted after a Race has been declared ‘Off’ may not continue in the Race.

entries.title: Remounting
entries.html:
(F)25After a Race has been declared ‘Off’, a Jockey must not remount a horse unless:

25.1they have been assessed by a Racecourse Medical Officer; and

25.2their horse has been examined by a Veterinary Surgeon.

entries.title: Pulling up a horse
entries.html:
(F)26A Jockey must pull up their horse whenever:

26.1it is lame or injured;

26.2it has no more to give or has tailed off through fatigue; or

26.3has a problem which is materially affecting its performance.

entries.title: Pulling up a horse
entries.html: (F)27A Jockey must dismount as soon as reasonably possible to do so from any lame or injured horse.

entries.title: Pulling up a horse
entries.html:
(F)28Where a Jockey pulls up their horse:

28.1they cannot re-join the Race or jump any further fence or hurdle; and

28.2they must wait in the area where they pulled up until all horses still in the Race have passed.

entries.title: Riding the course
entries.html: (F)29A Jockey must ride the correct course and comply with all direction markers.

entries.title: Riding the course
entries.html:
(F)30Where a horse:

30.1runs the wrong side of a running rail or a direction marker; or

30.2misses a fence or hurdle,

the Jockey must pull up, or turn back and ride the course correctly if continuing in the Race.

entries.title: Riding the course
entries.html: (F)31In a Race with Marker Poles located after the start, a Jockey must ride in a straight line from their draw position until they reach the Marker Poles, unless the horse is at the rear of the field.

entries.title: Emergency procedures
entries.html:
(F)32Except where it is used to indicate a false start, if a Stop Race Flag is deployed during a Race:

32.1each Jockey must pull up; and

32.2the Race shall be void.

entries.title: Reporting accidents occurring in a Race
path: Reporting accidents occurring in a Race
entries.html: (F)33If a Jockey falls or is injured in a Race, they must report it immediately to the Racecourse Medical Officer upon returning to the weighing room.

entries.title: Dangerous, Careless and Improper Riding
entries.html: (F)34A Jockey must take reasonable care for the safety of all Jockeys and horses.

entries.title: Dangerous, Careless and Improper Riding
entries.html: (F)35Jockey must not interfere with or make contact with another horse or Jockey during a Race.

entries.title: Dangerous, Careless and Improper Riding
entries.html: (F)36There shall be no breach of Rule (F)35 where the interference or contact is accidental.

entries.title: Riding a horse in a Race
path: Riding a horse in a Race
entries.html:
(F)37Subject to Rule (F)26, a Jockey must, and must be seen to:

37.1ask their horse for timely, real and substantial efforts to achieve the best possible position; and

37.2take all other reasonable and permissible measures throughout the Race to ensure the horse is given a full opportunity to achieve the best possible position.

entries.title: Riding a horse in a Race
path: Riding a horse in a Race
entries.html: (F)38A Person must not prevent or try to prevent a horse from obtaining the best possible position.

entries.title: Instructions
entries.html: (F)39A Trainer is responsible for ensuring that a Jockey who rides a horse trained by them in a Race is given instructions that shall allow the Jockey to ensure that the horse is given a full opportunity to achieve the best possible position.

entries.title: Instructions
entries.html: (F)40If a Jockey deliberately does not ensure that the horse runs the Race to achieve its best possible position, or if a Race is used to school or condition a horse, a Trainer shall be responsible unless the Trainer can demonstrate that the Jockey was given the necessary instructions.

entries.title: Instructions
entries.html: (F)41A Person must not give instructions to a Jockey which would, if obeyed, lead to a breach of Rule (F)37.

entries.title: Whip Instructions
entries.html: (F)42A Trainer must give Apprentice Jockeys, Conditional Jockeys and equivalent Overseas Jockeys instructions regarding their use of the whip.

entries.title: Whip Instructions
entries.html: (F)43A Person must not give any instructions to a Jockey which could lead to a breach of Rule (F)45.

entries.title: Whip
entries.html: (F)44A Jockey must carry, but is not obliged to use, a whip that complies with the Equipment Code.

entries.title: Whip
entries.html:
(F)45A Jockey must use a whip only:

45.1In a Flat Race a maximum of 6 times

45.2In a Jump Race a maximum of 7 times

45.3In accordance with the Whip Guidance

45A Any potential breach of (F)45 identified by the Stewards will be referred to the Whip Review Committee, unless meeting the exemption specified within the Whip Guidance whereupon a Jockey may elect for the breach to be dealt with by the Stewards.

       45A.1 Where a Jockey elects for the matter to be dealt with by the Stewards they will forfeit any right of appeal against the decision.

entries.title: Assisting another horse in a Race
path: Assisting another horse in a Race
entries.html:
(F)46A Jockey must not ride in such a way which is intended to, or does, give an advantage to or is in the interests of a horse which:

46.1shares one or more Owners in common with; or

46.2is from the same stable or team as the horse they are riding in the Race.

entries.title: Assisting another horse in a Race
path: Assisting another horse in a Race
entries.html: (F)47A Trainer is also responsible for any breach of Rule (F)46 by a Jockey riding one of their horses, except where they can demonstrate that they instructed the Jockey to treat every other horse in the Race equally.

entries.title: Assisting another horse in a Race
path: Assisting another horse in a Race
entries.html: (F)48Nothing in these Rules prohibits pure pace making.

entries.title: Determining the result
entries.html: (G)1The winner and the remaining placings in a Race shall be determined by the order in which the leading point of each horse’s head (excluding the ears and tongue) crosses the finish line.

entries.title: Determining the result
entries.html:
(G)2Subject to subsequent correction or appeal, the result and the placings shall be determined:

2.1by the Judge; or

2.2if the Judge is unable to do so, by the Stewards.

entries.title: Determining the result
entries.html: (G)3A Race shall be void if the Judge or the Stewards are unable to determine the result.

entries.title: Determining the result
entries.html: (G)4If a horse is disqualified or has its placing altered, other than as a result of analysis of a stored sample, the placings of the other horses in the Race shall be altered accordingly.

entries.title: Decision where there is a dead-heat
path: Decision where there is a dead-heat
entries.html: (G)5In the event of a dead-heat for a given placing, the horses in question shall each be regarded as having that placing.

entries.title: Correction of original decision
entries.html:
By the Judge

(G)6A Judge may correct their decision within 5 days of the Race, which shall be subject to confirmation by the BHA.

By the BHA

entries.title: Correction of original decision
entries.html: (G)7If an incorrect result has been declared, the BHA may correct the decision within 14 days of the Race and declare any changes to the winner and placed horses.

entries.title: Dismounting
entries.html: (G)8Jockeys must dismount within a reasonable distance of the place appointed for unsaddling.

entries.title: Weighing In
entries.html: (G)9After dismounting, a Jockey must remove and keep their saddle and present themselves to the Clerk of the Scales with the saddle to be weighed in.

entries.title: Weighing In
entries.html: (G)10If a Jockey is unable to remove the saddle or carry it to the weighing room, a Trainer may do so, provided that it is handed back to the Jockey unchanged before weighing in.

entries.title: Weighing In
entries.html:
(G)11When weighing in, Jockeys must:

11.1be wearing the same clothes and equipment that they wore when weighing out; and

11.2put onto the scales everything that was on the scales when weighing out, except for any Excluded Equipment.

entries.title: Weighing In
entries.html: (G)12All weights shall be rounded down to the nearest whole 1lb unit.

entries.title: Weighing In
entries.html:
(G)13A Jockey’s weight at weighing in must not be:

13.1more than 1lb less than their weight at weighing out; or

13.22lb or more heavier than their Declared Weight at weighing out.

13A  The Stewards shall sanction the Jockey or Trainer, or both of them, when a breach of Rule (G)13.1 or 13.2 has occurred, unless the reason for the breach can be explained to the satisfaction of the Stewards.

13B  The Jockey and Trainer will both be sanctioned for a breach of (G)13.1 if no cause is established.

entries.title: Weighing In
entries.html:
(G)14The Stewards may authorise the announcement of ‘Weighed In’ once:

14.1the weighing in process has completed;

14.2the Judge has confirmed the placings; and

14.3any Objections have been determined.

entries.title: Weighing In
entries.html: (G)15A Jockey must remain in the vicinity of the weighing room for five minutes after the ‘Weighed In’ announcement.

entries.title: Weighing In
entries.html: (G)16A Jockey who has failed to complete the course must report that fact to the Clerk of the Scales.

entries.title: Post-Race Reports of matters materially affecting a horse’s performance
path: Post-Race Reports of matters materially affecting a horse’s performance
entries.html: (G)17Jockeys and Trainers must without delay make a Post Race Report if applicable.

entries.title: Post-Race Reports of matters materially affecting a horse’s performance
path: Post-Race Reports of matters materially affecting a horse’s performance
entries.html:
(G)18A Post Race Report must be made as soon as possible to:

18.1a Steward, or where a Steward is not available,

18.2a Veterinary Officer; or

18.3the Clerk of the Scales.

entries.title: Post-Race Reports of matters materially affecting a horse’s performance
path: Post-Race Reports of matters materially affecting a horse’s performance
entries.html: (G)19The obligation on a Trainer to make a Post Race Report applies at any time after the Race, including after the horse has left the Racecourse. Once the horse has left the Racecourse, the Post Race Report must be made without delay to the BHA.

entries.title: Post-Race Reports of matters materially affecting a horse’s performance
path: Post-Race Reports of matters materially affecting a horse’s performance
entries.html: (G)20A Jockey may make a Post Race Report on behalf of a Trainer. In such circumstances, the Trainer remains responsible for ensuring that the Post Race Report is made.

entries.title: Post-Race Reports of matters materially affecting a horse’s performance
path: Post-Race Reports of matters materially affecting a horse’s performance
entries.html: (G)21If a horse loses its tongue strap during a Race, the Trainer must report this to a Steward.

entries.title: Post-Race Reports of matters materially affecting a horse’s performance
path: Post-Race Reports of matters materially affecting a horse’s performance
entries.html: (G)22A Post Race Report may be published by the BHA.

entries.title: General Powers
entries.html: (H)1A Person must comply with instructions given by BHA Officials.

entries.title: General Powers
entries.html: (H)2BHA Officials must have unrestricted access to every part of Racecourse Property.

entries.title: General Powers
entries.html:
(H)3The Stewards may:

3.1make or vary any arrangements in place for a Race Meeting;

3.2omit or alter any fence or hurdle in a Race, provided that the advertised distance of the Race is not decreased;

3.3abandon a Race; or

3.4abandon a Race Meeting.

entries.title: Voiding Races
entries.html:
(H)4The Stewards shall declare a Race void where:

4.1no horses returned to the start after a false start;

4.2a Stop Race Flag was raised;

4.3no horse finished; or

4.4the result cannot be determined.

entries.title: Voiding Races
entries.html:
(H)5The Stewards may declare a Race void where:

5.1a false start should have been declared;

5.2a fault with the starting stalls has materially prejudiced more than one-third of the horses starting the Race.

5.3no horse covers the course in accordance with these Rules;

5.4all the horses in the Race ran at the wrong weights; or

5.5all the horses ran over the wrong course or started from the wrong place.

entries.title: Non-Runners
entries.html:
(H)6The Stewards may declare a horse a non-runner where:

6.1In a Race started from starting stalls, a horse is denied a fair start, and its chances are materially affected, including but not limited to where:

6.1.1a horse is prevented from starting on equal terms due to a faulty action of the starting stalls

6.2In a race started by any method other than starting stalls, a horse is denied a fair start, and its chances are materially affected, including but not limited to where:

6.2.1a horse is prevented from starting on equal terms due to a faulty action of a starting mechanism; or

6.2.2when the race is started, a horse is in such a position as to be denied the opportunity of starting on equal terms.

6.3that horse is riderless at the ‘Off’.

6.4that horse has gained an unfair advantage at the start of the Race.

entries.title: Horses
entries.html:
(H)7The Stewards may:

7.1direct that any horse be examined;

7.2direct that a Sample is taken from any horse for analysis;

7.3direct that a horse stays in the Racecourse Stables for examination for up to 24 hours after the Race in which it was declared to run;

7.4withdraw a horse from a Race:

7.4.1if they are not satisfied that it is qualified for that Race;

7.4.2where there are welfare concerns;

7.4.3where any person prevents or seeks to prevent access to the horse;

7.4.4if it is unruly;

7.4.5if it may delay the start of the Race;

7.4.6where the Jockey is not in control of the horse on the way to the start; or

7.4.7where there has been a breach of the Rules.

entries.title: Horses
entries.html:
(H)8The Stewards will disqualify a horse where:

8.1the Jockey causes interference which is Dangerous Riding; 

8.2the Jockey remounts and continues in the Race;

8.3subject to Rule (G)13, the horse did not carry at least the correct weight throughout the Race; or

8.4the horse was led over a hurdle or steeple chase fence.

entries.title: Horses
entries.html:
(H)9The Stewards may disqualify a horse where:

9.1the horse did not cover the correct course; or

9.2the Jockey did not present themselves to be weighed in.

entries.title: Horses
entries.html: (H)10The Stewards will, where a horse or Jockey causes interference, which is not Dangerous Riding, and the Stewards are satisfied that the interference improved the placing of the horse in relation to the horse or horses with which it interfered, place the horse that caused the interference behind the horse or horses with which it has interfered.

entries.title: Jockeys
entries.html: (H)11The Stewards may direct that any Jockey be examined by a Racecourse Medical Officer.

entries.title: Objections
entries.html:
(H)12A Qualified Person may make an Objection to:

12.1the Stewards; or

12.2the BHA, if there was no reasonable opportunity to make it to the Stewards.

entries.title: Objections made to the Stewards
entries.html: (H)13An Objection made to the Stewards must be brought to their attention as soon as reasonably practicable and in any event before the announcement of ‘Weighed In’.

entries.title: Objections made to the Stewards
entries.html:
(H)14The Stewards shall hold a Stewards Enquiry if:

14.1a valid Objection is made to them; or

14.2they believe that there are grounds for an Objection.

entries.title: Objections made to the Stewards
entries.html: (H)15A Qualified Person may review a replay of the Race before making an Objection. If they do so, they must notify the Stewards and the Clerk of the Scales of the review and any subsequent Objection.

entries.title: Objections made to the Stewards
entries.html:
(H)16A Qualified Person must not:

16.1raise an Objection without reasonable grounds for doing so; or

16.2withdraw an Objection without the permission of the Stewards.
