entries.title: Objections made to the Stewards
entries.html: (H)17The Stewards may announce or publish details of an Objection.

entries.title: Objections made to the BHA
entries.html:
(H)18An Objection made to the BHA must be made in accordance with the Judicial Panel Code and:

18.1within 14 days of the Race; or

18.2where the grounds for the Objection are discovered after 14 days, as soon as reasonably practicable after they are discovered.

entries.title: Objections made to the BHA
entries.html: (H)19A valid Objection made to the BHA shall be determined by the Disciplinary Panel in accordance with the Judicial Panel Code.

entries.title: Objections yet to be determined
entries.html:
(H)20Pending the final determination of an Objection or a matter falling within Rule (H)10

20.1prizes shall be withheld; and

20.2any stake shall be held by the Stakeholder.

entries.title: General
entries.html: (H)21The Stewards may enquire into any matter.

entries.title: General
entries.html:
(H)22The Stewards:

22.1may refer any matter to the BHA; and

22.2shall refer a matter to the BHA where they consider that a penalty, order or sanction ought to be imposed which exceeds their powers.

22.3shall refer any potential breach of Rule (F)45 to the Whip Review Committee in accordance with the Whip Guidance

entries.title: General
entries.html: (H)23A Stewards’ Enquiry shall be held by three Stewards where possible

entries.title: General
entries.html: (H)24Any decision taken at a Stewards’ Enquiry shall be taken by simple majority.

entries.title: Sanction
entries.html:
(H)25The Stewards may impose one or more of the following in accordance with the Penalty Guidelines:

25.1a financial penalty not exceeding £15,000;

25.2a caution;

25.3suspend a Jockey from riding for up to 40 days;

25.4remove a Jockey’s riding fee;

25.5disqualify a horse;

25.6change the placings; and / or

25.7suspend a horse.

entries.title: Sanction
entries.html: (H)26A penalty, or part of it, may be deferred, suspended or be contingent on an event.

entries.title: Jockeys
entries.html:
(H)27A riding suspension imposed on a Jockey by Stewards shall start on the later of:

27.114 days after the date of the Stewards’ decision;

27.2the day after an appeal of the Stewards’ decision has been determined; or

27.3the day after an existing suspension ends.

27A   A riding suspension imposed on a Jockey by the Whip Review Committee will start the later of:

        27A.1 14 days after the date of the written decision of the Whip Review Committee; or

        27A.2 the day after an appeal of the Whip Review Committee’s decision has been determined; or

        27A.3 the day after an existing suspension ends.

27B   If accepting a penalty from the Whip Review Committee, a Jockey may request that any suspension is issued in accordance with the timeline outlined in Rule (H)27, providing that the request is made before the deadline for Jockey Declarations for the first Race affected by the change.

Days on which a riding suspension shall apply

entries.title: Jockeys
entries.html:
(H)28A period of suspension may:

28.1apply only to days:

28.1.1on which Flat Races are programmed to take place, if the Jockey is licensed to ride in Flat Races;

28.1.2on which Jump Races are programmed to take place, if the Jockey is licensed to ride in Jump Races; or

28.1.3as determined by the Stewards, if the Jockey is licensed to ride in both Flat and Jump Races or is an Amateur Jockey; and

28.2include any day on which a Jockey is required to attend remedial training.

entries.title: Jockeys
entries.html: (H)29The days on which a suspension applies shall not change if any meetings are subsequently moved or abandoned, unless otherwise directed by the BHA.

entries.title: Riding suspensions of four days or less
path: Riding suspensions of four days or less
entries.html:
(H)30If a suspension is for four days or less:

30.1it shall not take effect on days on which a Group 1 or Grade 1 Race is programmed to take place, as applicable to the type of Licence held by the Jockey, unless the Jockey requests otherwise; and

30.2a Jockey may request that one day of the suspension takes place before the day it is due to commence.

provided that the request is made before the deadline for Jockey Declarations for the first Race affected by the change

entries.title: Riding suspensions of four days or less
path: Riding suspensions of four days or less
entries.html: (H)31If a suspension is for four days or less, a Jockey may apply to defer one or more days of the suspension for the purpose of to ride at a meeting with a Group 1 or Grade 1 race outside of Great Britain. The application must be made to the BHA by 1pm on the day before the meeting in question.

entries.title: Horses
entries.html: (H)32A horse suspension shall take effect on the day after the time for appealing has lapsed, unless the BHA directs otherwise.

entries.title: Horses
entries.html: (H)33An appeal of a Steward’s decision to suspend a horse may not be withdrawn without the BHA’s permission, which may be granted subject to conditions.

entries.title: Appeals
entries.html:
(H)34The following may appeal a decision of the Stewards:

34.1a Jockey who has ridden in the Race and is affected by a Stewards’ decision;

34.2an Owner or Trainer who has a horse in the Race and is affected by a Stewards’ decision;

34.3any other person that is subject to a disciplinary penalty imposed by the Stewards; and

34.4the BHA.

entries.title: Appeals
entries.html: (H)35The appeal shall proceed in accordance with the Judicial Panel Code.

entries.title: Complaints against Officials
entries.html: (H)36Any complaint against a BHA Official at a Race Meeting must be made to the Stewards or the BHA.

entries.title: General
entries.html: (I)1The BHA may arrange and manage Races and fixtures.

entries.title: General
entries.html:
(I)2If necessary, the BHA may:

2.1order the abandonment of any Race or Race Meeting; and

2.2refuse to allow a horse to run in any Race.

entries.title: General
entries.html: (I)3A horse can only run in one Race per day, unless the first Race was a walk over.

entries.title: The Racing Season
entries.html: (I)4The BHA shall publish the dates for the Flat Season, Winter Flat Season, Jump Season and Hunters’ Steeple Chase Season.

entries.title: Race Conditions
entries.html: (I)5Race Conditions and the programme for a fixture must be approved by the BHA.

entries.title: Race Conditions
entries.html: (I)6Race Conditions shall be published in The Racing Calendar.

entries.title: Race Conditions
entries.html: (I)7The BHA may change any Race Conditions.

entries.title: Cancellation of Races
entries.html: (I)8The BHA may cancel any Race that has too few horses entered or declared to run.

entries.title: Dividing and eliminating Races
entries.html: (I)9A Race may be divided in accordance with the Race Administration Code.

entries.title: Dividing and eliminating Races
entries.html: (I)10Horses may be eliminated from any Race in accordance with the Race Administration Code.

entries.title: Handicapping
entries.html: (I)11No horse may run in a Race unless they meet the previous experience requirements in the Weights and Handicapping Code for the classification of that Race.

entries.title: Handicapping
entries.html: (I)12A horse shall be eligible to receive a Handicap Rating in accordance with the Weights and Handicapping Code.

entries.title: Handicapping
entries.html: (I)13The BHA may refuse to give a Handicap Rating to any horse if, in the BHA’s opinion, it does not have sufficient information to do so.

entries.title: Handicapping
entries.html: (I)14A Handicap Rating which is published on Tuesday of a particular week shall, unless the BHA directs otherwise, apply for Races that Close on that Tuesday through to the following Monday.

entries.title: Handicapping
entries.html:
(I)15A weight may not be altered after it has been published, unless before the relevant deadline, the BHA permits:

15.1a weight to be added where the horse was entered for the race but its name or weight was omitted from the Handicap; or

15.2a correction to be made where an incorrect weight has been published.

entries.title: Handicapping
entries.html:
(I)16No alteration to published weights shall be permitted:

16.1in respect of an Early Closer, after noon on the Friday before the first Scratching Deadline; or

16.2otherwise, after 9am on the day that Declarations to Run are due.

entries.title: Weight Allowances
entries.html: (I)17Weight allowances, penalties and qualifications shall be calculated in accordance with the Weights and Handicapping Code.

entries.title: Claiming and Selling
entries.html: (I)18All Persons must comply with the Claiming and Selling Code.

entries.title: Claiming and Selling
entries.html:
(I)19No Person may

19.1prevent, or seek to prevent, any other person from claiming or bidding for a horse, whether by offering any consideration or guarantee or by means of a threat or otherwise, or

19.2accept or offer to accept any consideration or guarantee or other inducement to refrain from submitting a Claim or bid.

entries.title: Horses Subject to a Lease
entries.html: (I)20A horse which is the subject of a Lease may not be entered into, or run in, a Claiming Race or Selling Race without the written consent of the lessor. If it does run, it shall be disqualified and the BHA may annul the claim or sale of the horse.

entries.title: Horses Subject to a Lease
entries.html: (I)21The lessee of a horse must ensure that the VAT treatment of the horse is correct.

entries.title: Payments
entries.html:
(J)1A Jockey must not accept, agree to accept or solicit, any Consideration in connection with riding in a Race except:

1.1a Professional Jockey may accept, agree to accept or solicit:

1.1.1Consideration stated in the Race Conditions, or the equivalent for a Race run under the rules of a Recognised Racing Authority;

1.1.2Consideration from a Sponsorship Agreement for sponsorship; and/or

1.1.3Consideration from the Owner, Owner’s Representative or Breeder of a horse for riding that horse in a Race,

1.2an Amateur Jockey may accept, agree to accept or solicit, Amateur Expenses.

entries.title: Payments
entries.html:
(J)2A Jockey or Trainer may accept, agree to accept or solicit Consideration for:

2.1the advertising or promotion of goods and / or services; and / or

2.2the provision of views or information for general publication,

except that, where such arrangements are entered into with a Betting Operator, they must provide to the BHA all details of the arrangement, or any changes to the arrangement, as soon as reasonably practicable.

entries.title: Bribes
entries.html: (J)3A Person must not offer or provide or agree to provide a Bribe.

entries.title: Bribes
entries.html: (J)4A Person must not accept, or agree or offer to accept, a Bribe.

entries.title: Prohibition on Betting
entries.html:
(J)5Neither a Jockey nor a Valet may Bet except:

5.1An Amateur Jockey may Bet on Races in which they are not riding.

5.2A Valet may Bet on Races taking place at a Race Meeting where they are not present in their capacity as a Valet.

entries.title: Prohibition on Lay Betting
entries.html: (J)6A Trainer and their Stable Employees must not place a lay Bet on a horse under their care.

entries.title: Prohibition on Lay Betting
entries.html: (J)7Rule (J)6 continues to apply to a Stable Employee for a period of 21 days after they leave the employment of the Trainer.

entries.title: Prohibition on Lay Betting
entries.html: (J)8A Jockey’s Agent must not place a lay Bet on a horse being ridden by a Jockey they represent.

entries.title: Prohibition on Lay Betting
entries.html: (J)9A Listed Person must not place a lay Bet on a horse in which they have any interest.

entries.title: Prohibition on Lay Betting
entries.html: (J)10A Service Provider must not place a lay Bet on a horse owned, trained or ridden by a Person to whom they have provided a service, for the whole of the period in which the service was provided and for 21 days afterwards.

entries.title: Prohibition on Lay Betting
entries.html: (J)11A lay Bet includes a match Bet.

entries.title: Betting Operators
entries.html: (J)12Nothing in these Rules prevents a Betting Operator from Betting in the ordinary course of that Betting Operator’s business.

entries.title: Betting Operators
entries.html: (J)13A Person must ensure that any account with a Betting Operator in their name is not used by any other person.

entries.title: Betting Operators
entries.html: (J)14All Bets placed using an account with a Betting Operator shall be presumed to be for the benefit of the named account holder.

entries.title: Betting Operators
entries.html: (J)15When on Racecourse Property a Professional Jockey or Valet may not communicate directly or indirectly with a Betting Operator or its representative without the consent of the BHA.

entries.title: Inside Information
entries.html: (J)16No Person may communicate Inside Information to any other person unless permitted to do so under these Rules.

entries.title: Inside Information
entries.html: (J)17Except where the Person communicating the Inside Information knows or has reason to know that the Inside Information shall be used for prohibited Betting and/or lay Betting, a Person can communicate Inside Information to a Person who owns, trains or is a service provider or Stable Employee responsible for or engaged in the care and welfare of that horse.

entries.title: Inside Information
entries.html:
(J)18For the purpose of making Inside Information public, a Person can communicate Inside Information to:

18.1the General Public directly;

18.2an accredited journalist for the purposes of publishing the Inside Information to the General Public; or

18.3at a Public Event, provided that the person communicating the Inside Information is paid no more than a reasonable fee for attending the event.

entries.title: Conduct prejudicial to horseracing
entries.html:
(J)19A Person must not engage in conduct which the BHA considers is prejudicial to the integrity, proper conduct or good reputation of horseracing in Great Britain.

19A  Persons must comply with the BHA Code of Conduct. 

         Individuals not bound by the Rules of Racing should be aware that the BHA Code of Conduct also applies to them.

entries.title: Conduct prejudicial to horseracing
entries.html: (J)20A Person must not act in a violent or improper manner.

entries.title: Conduct prejudicial to horseracing
entries.html: (J)21A Person must not abuse a BHA Official, whether verbally or otherwise.

entries.title: Conduct prejudicial to horseracing
entries.html: (J)22Any Person who engages in bloodstock transactions or deals in racehorses (including horses intended for racing), must comply with the Bloodstock Industry Code of Practice (available here).

entries.title: Conduct prejudicial to horseracing
entries.html:
(J)23A Person must not, without the prior written permission of the BHA, associate with the following in connection with horseracing in Great Britain:

23.1a Disqualified Person; or

23.2a person subject to an Exclusion Order.

entries.title: Conduct obstructing the proper administration or control of racing
path: Conduct obstructing the proper administration or control of racing
entries.html:
(J)24A Person must not:

24.1breach any declaration or undertaking given to the BHA;

24.2provide any inaccurate information to the BHA;

24.3omit any relevant information which is requested by the BHA;

24.4fail to comply with a requirement imposed on them by the BHA;

24.5assist, or encourage, or cause another Person to act in contravention of a provision of these Rules; or

24.6mislead or attempt to mislead the BHA or one of its employees or BHA Officials.

entries.title: Involvement in corrupt or fraudulent practices in relation to racing
path: Involvement in corrupt or fraudulent practices in relation to racing
entries.html:
(J)25A person must not:

25.1commit any corrupt or fraudulent practice in relation to horse racing in any jurisdiction; or

25.2conspire with any other person for the commission of such a practice.

entries.title: Conviction of criminal offences connected with racing
path: Conviction of criminal offences connected with racing
entries.html: (J)26A Person must not be convicted of any criminal offence in connection with horse racing in any jurisdiction.

entries.title: Disclosure to the BHA
entries.html:
(J)27A Person must, as soon as reasonably practicable, provide the BHA with full details of any knowledge of:

27.1approach or invitation made to them or any other person which would amount to a breach of these Rules; and

27.2incident, fact or matter which may amount to a breach of the Rules.

entries.title: Unrecognised Meetings
entries.html:
(J)28A Person must not:

28.1own, train or ride a horse at an Unrecognised Meeting; or

28.2act in an official capacity at an Unrecognised Meeting,

entries.title: Application
entries.html:
(K)1The Equine Anti-Doping rules set out below shall apply to any horse that:

1.1is present in Great Britain or has been entered into a Race in Great Britain; and

1.2has been notified to the Stud Book Authority or is registered with a stud book approved by the International Stud Book Committee.

entries.title: Presence of a Prohibited Substance
entries.html:
(K)2The Responsible Person must ensure that:

2.1no Category A Prohibited Substance is present in their horse’s body at any time;

2.2prior to leaving the Racecourse, no Category B Prohibited Substance is present in their horse’s body on a day on which it is engaged to run in a Race; and

2.3prior to leaving the Racecourse, no Category C Prohibited Substance is present in their horse’s body on a day on which it takes a Stalls Test.

entries.title: Use of a Prohibited Method
entries.html:
(K)3The Responsible Person must not use or attempt to use:

3.1a Category A Prohibited Method on their horse at any time; or

3.2a Category B Prohibited Method on their horse on a day on which it is engaged to run in a Race, prior to leaving the Racecourse.

entries.title: Administering Prohibited Substances or applying a Prohibited Method
path: Administering Prohibited Substances or applying a Prohibited Method
entries.html:
(K)4No Person shall: 

4.1administer, attempt to administer, allow the administration, cause the administration or connive in the administration of a Prohibited Substance so that it would be present in a horse’s body in contravention of Rule (K)2; or

4.2apply, attempt to apply, allow the application, cause the application or connive in the application of a Prohibited Method to a horse at a time when application of that Prohibited Method is prohibited.

entries.title: Possession of Prohibited Substances or products allowing for the administration of a Prohibited Method
path: Possession of Prohibited Substances or products allowing for the administration of a Prohibited Method
entries.html:
(K)5No Person shall possess:

5.1subject to Rule (K)16, a Category A Prohibited Substance; or

5.2a Category B Prohibited Substance on the racecourse on a Raceday; or

5.3products, equipment or substances that would allow for the administration of a Prohibited Method when prohibited by Rule (K)3.

entries.title: Availability for Sampling
entries.html: (K)6The Responsible Person must ensure that their horse is made available for a Sample to be taken by the BHA upon request.

entries.title: Whereabouts
entries.html: (K)7The Responsible Person is responsible for ensuring that the BHA always possesses sufficient information to enable the BHA to locate a horse at any time.

entries.title: Trafficking a Category A Prohibited Substance
path: Trafficking a Category A Prohibited Substance
entries.html: (K)8No Person shall traffic or attempt to traffic a Category A Prohibited Substance.

entries.title: Obstruction
entries.html:
(K)9No Person shall:

9.1tamper or attempt to tamper with a Sample;

9.2hinder or attempt to hinder any part of the sample collection process; or

9.3hinder or attempt to hinder an investigation into an Equine Anti-doping Rule Violation.

entries.title: Complicity
entries.html: (K)10No Person shall assist, encourage, aid, abet, conspire in relation to, cover up or engage in any other type of intentional complicity or evasion involving an Equine Anti-doping Rule Violation.

entries.title: Presence of Prohibited Substance in a horse’s body
path: Considerations For Equine Anti-Doping Rule Violations
Presence of Prohibited Substance in a horse’s body
entries.html: (K)11It is not necessary to demonstrate intent, fault, negligence or knowing use to establish a breach of Rule (K)2.

entries.title: Presence of Prohibited Substance in a horse’s body
path: Considerations For Equine Anti-Doping Rule Violations
Presence of Prohibited Substance in a horse’s body
entries.html:
(K)12There shall be no breach of Rule (K)2.2 if:

12.1the Category B Prohibited Substance is administered for genuine therapeutic purposes; and

12.2the horse does not run in a Race on that day; and

12.3the BHA is notified of the administration beforehand or, if urgent, as soon as reasonably practicable.

entries.title: Presence of Prohibited Substance in a horse’s body
path: Considerations For Equine Anti-Doping Rule Violations
Presence of Prohibited Substance in a horse’s body
entries.html:
(K)13The presence of a Prohibited Substance in the following is sufficient evidence of a breach of Rule (K)2.

13.1the horse’s ‘A’ Sample where

(i) the B sample is not analysed; or

(ii) the B Sample is analysed and is found to be compromised;

13.2the horse’s A and B sample;

13.3both portions of the B Sample, where the B Sample is split into two portions as a result of the horse’s A Sample being unavailable or where it is believed to have been compromised.

entries.title: Presence of Prohibited Substance in a horse’s body
path: Considerations For Equine Anti-Doping Rule Violations
Presence of Prohibited Substance in a horse’s body
entries.html:
(K)14The Disciplinary Panel shall impose a penalty on the Responsible Person for a breach of Rule (K)2 unless the Responsible Person establishes:

14.1the precise route as to how the Prohibited Substance entered their horse’s body; and

14.2that they had taken all reasonable precautions to avoid violating Rule (K)2.

entries.title: Use of a Prohibited Method
path: Considerations For Equine Anti-Doping Rule Violations
entries.html: (K)15It is not necessary to demonstrate intent, fault, negligence or knowing use to establish a breach of Rule (K)3.

entries.title: Possession of a Prohibited Substance or PROHIBITED Method
path: Considerations For Equine Anti-Doping Rule Violations
Possession of a Prohibited Substance or PROHIBITED Method
entries.html: (K)16There shall be no breach of Rule (K)5 if the possession of a Category A Prohibited Substance was for legitimate personal use or possessed by a Veterinary Surgeon for legitimate use on animals other than horses subject to Rule (K)1.

entries.title: Possession of a Prohibited Substance or PROHIBITED Method
path: Considerations For Equine Anti-Doping Rule Violations
Possession of a Prohibited Substance or PROHIBITED Method
entries.html: (K)17Only BHA Veterinary Officers or approved Racecourse Veterinary Surgeons may bring Category B prohibited substances onto a racecourse on Raceday.

entries.title: Possession of a Prohibited Substance or PROHIBITED Method
path: Considerations For Equine Anti-Doping Rule Violations
Possession of a Prohibited Substance or PROHIBITED Method
entries.html: (K)18There shall be no breach of Rule (K)5.2 if the Category B prohibited substance is stored in a vehicle under the control of the Responsible Person or their representative.

entries.title: Administration of Category B Prohibited Substances
path: Considerations For Equine Anti-Doping Rule Violations
Administration of Category B Prohibited Substances
entries.html:
(K)19There shall be no breach of Rule (K)4.1 if the Category B Prohibited Substance was administered for genuine therapeutic reasons: and

19.1the horse does not run in a Race or has run already in a Race on that day; and

19.2the BHA is notified of the administration beforehand or, if urgent, as soon as reasonably practicable.

entries.title: General
entries.html: (K)20The BHA may take a Sample from a horse at any time with or without prior notice.

entries.title: General
entries.html: (K)21Where the BHA wishes to take a Sample, the Responsible Person must co-operate with the BHA to make sure that the Sample is taken in a timely manner.

entries.title: General
entries.html: (K)22All Samples obtained from a horse are the property of the BHA and may be used for any purpose as required by the BHA.

entries.title: General
entries.html: (K)23A secure chain of custody shall be maintained for all Samples

entries.title: General
entries.html: (K)24Any departure from Rules or guidance relating to the collection of a Sample that did not cause an Adverse Analytical Finding shall not invalidate the finding.

entries.title: General
entries.html: (K)25If a Person establishes that a departure from Rules relating to the collection of a Sample could have reasonably caused an Adverse Analytical Finding, the burden shall be on the BHA to establish that such departure was not the cause.

entries.title: Sampling
entries.html:
(K)26A Sample shall be collected in such manner as the BHA may direct.

26A A Trainer may request that the BHA take a sample from any horse in their care and for it to be analysed for a Category A Prohibited Substance, providing that:

         26A.1 Any such request is made within 7 days of the horse entering their care; and

         26A.2 The horse has not run during this time; and

         26A.3 They pay the amount outlined in the Fee Code.

26B Where such sample is found to contain a Category A Prohibited Substance the previous Responsible Person will be the person liable under Rule (K)2, unless they can prove otherwise.

entries.title: Sampling
entries.html: (K)27The Responsible Person may observe the Sample being collected. Where they do so, any concerns as to the integrity of the procedure must be raised at that time. If they observe the collection, and do not raise any concerns, they shall be taken to have waived any objection to the integrity of the collection.

entries.title: Sampling
entries.html: (K)28Where the Responsible Person elects not to observe the collection of the Sample, they shall be taken to have waived any objection to the integrity of that procedure.

entries.title: Sample Analysis
entries.html: (K)29A Sample shall only be analysed in Approved Laboratories or using Approved Equipment.

entries.title: Sample Analysis
entries.html:
(K)30Approved Laboratories are presumed:

30.1to have conducted Sample analysis and custodial procedures in accordance with Laboratory Standards; and

30.2to have properly carried out re-sealing and storage procedures of any stored Samples.

entries.title: Sample Analysis
entries.html: (K)31The BHA may instruct an Approved Laboratory to re-seal and store Samples or parts of Samples from any horse.

entries.title: Sample Analysis
entries.html: (K)32If the Responsible Person wants the B Sample to be analysed, they must request such analysis within three working days of being notified of an Adverse Analytical Finding.

entries.title: Sample Analysis
entries.html: (K)33The BHA may also elect to have the B Sample analysed.

entries.title: B Samples
entries.html:
Procedure

(K)34The B Sample shall be analysed at the LGC laboratory, unless the Responsible Person nominates the Laboratorie Des Courses Hippiques (LCH) or the Deutsche Sporthochschule Koln Institut fur Biochemie (DSKIB), or another laboratory with permission from the BHA.

entries.title: B Samples
entries.html: (K)35The Responsible Person may, at their own cost, appoint an appropriately qualified representative to witness the analysis of the B Sample, provided they are available on the designated date.

entries.title: B Samples
entries.html:
(K)36If the Responsible Person elects to have the B Sample analysed at a laboratory other than the LGC laboratory, the Responsible Person shall bear the corresponding costs. In all other cases, a Disciplinary Panel has the power to order that a contribution is made of up to £500 to the costs of the B Sample.

ANALYSIS

entries.title: B Samples
entries.html: (K)37The analysis of the B Sample will be limited to confirming whether the B Sample confirms the findings of the A Sample.

entries.title: B Samples
entries.html: (K)38A copy of the results and any supporting evidence shall be provided to the BHA and the Responsible Person.

entries.title: Endogenous Substances
entries.html: (K)39If an Adverse Analytical Finding involves an endogenous substance, the BHA or the Responsible Person may elect to have further Samples taken or for further examinations of the horse to take place to investigate whether the quantity of the substance found could have been produced naturally by the horse. The costs of analysing any further Samples shall be borne equally by the BHA and Responsible Person.

entries.title: Endogenous Substances
entries.html: (K)40If an Adverse Analytical Finding involves an endogenous substance, the BHA may carry out an investigation prior to notifying the Responsible Person of the finding, save that the BHA shall notify the Responsible Person prior to analysing the B Sample.

entries.title: Endogenous Substances
entries.html: (K)41If samples of food or other substances are removed from the yard or premises, the Responsible Person may appoint a person to observe any analysis of the sample.

entries.title: Endogenous Substances
entries.html:
(K)42Following that analysis, the Responsible Person may arrange for their own tests to be carried out at a laboratory nominated by them. If they do so:

42.1they must make a written request to the BHA for the samples to be released;

42.2the testing must be carried out at an Approved Laboratory; and

42.3if the BHA appoints an analyst to review the laboratory’s processes, the analyst must be given the option of witnessing the analysis of the sample.

entries.title: Provisional Suspensions
entries.html: (K)43The BHA may provisionally suspend the Responsible Person's Licence where there is evidence of an Equine Anti-doping Rule Violation.

entries.title: Provisional Suspensions
entries.html:
(K)44The BHA: 

44.1shall provisionally suspend the horse where there is evidence of an Equine Anti-doping Rule Violation involving a Category A Prohibited Substance or Category A Prohibited Method;

44.2may provisionally suspend the horse where there is evidence of any other Equine Anti-doping Rule Violation.

entries.title: Provisional Suspensions
entries.html:
(K)45If a provisional suspension is imposed, the Responsible Person, or the Owner can apply to the Disciplinary Panel for a preliminary hearing, to be held in accordance with the Judicial Panels Code, to show good reason why the provisional suspension should be lifted.

45A The BHA may lift any provisional suspension that is imposed under Rule (K)43 or (K)44 where there is good reason to do so.

entries.title: Suspension from Racing and Mandatory Stand Down
path: Suspension from Racing and Mandatory Stand Down
entries.html:
(K)46Where a breach of Rule (K)2, Rule (K)3 or Rule (K)4 is proven which involves a Category A Prohibited Substance or a Category A Prohibited Method, the horse shall be suspended from racing for 14 months and shall be subject to a mandatory stand down for 12 months (to run concurrently), save that credit shall be given for any period of provisional suspension imposed.

46A Where the Category A substance is captured by paragraph 6 of the Prohibited List Code the provisions of (K)46 may be revoked upon review of subsequent analysis of further testing.

entries.title: Suspension from Racing and Mandatory Stand Down
path: Suspension from Racing and Mandatory Stand Down
entries.html: (K)47Where a horse tests positive for a Prohibited Substance, it shall be disqualified from all Races from the date of the relevant Sample until the commencement of any provisional suspension.

entries.title: Reinstatement testing
entries.html:
(K)48As a condition of reinstatement:

48.1a Sample shall be collected and analysed at the Owner’s cost;

48.2the Sample must not result in an Adverse Analytical Finding.

entries.title: Banned Substances
entries.html: (K)49A Jockey must ensure that no Banned Substance is present in their body.

entries.title: Banned Substances
entries.html: (K)50It is not necessary to demonstrate intent, fault, negligence or knowing use to establish a breach of Rule (K)49.

entries.title: Banned Substances
entries.html:
(K)51There shall be no breach of Rule (K)49 if the Jockey establishes that the presence of a Banned Substance is attributable to:

51.1use of ordinary medications in normal dosage for a recognised medical purpose other than the treatment of drug addiction or dependency; or

51.2the ingestion of food or other nutritional substances in the ordinary course of dietary nourishment.

entries.title: Notifiable medications
entries.html: (K)52A Jockey must notify the Chief Medical Adviser before they take a Notifiable Medication.

entries.title: Notifiable medications
entries.html: (K)53A Jockey must not ride in a Race with a Notifiable Medication present in their body without the prior written consent of the Chief Medical Adviser.

entries.title: Notifiable medications
entries.html: (K)54It is not necessary to demonstrate intent, fault, negligence or knowing use to establish a breach of Rule (K)53.

entries.title: Alcohol
entries.html: (K)55On a day where a Jockey has riding engagements, they must ensure that the alcohol level present in their body whilst at the Racecourse is not at or above 17 micrograms per 100ml of breath or 54 milligrams per 100 millilitres in urine.

entries.title: Alcohol
entries.html: (K)56If a Jockey’s alcohol level exceeds the threshold in Rule (K)55, the Stewards shall stand the Jockey down from riding in any Race for the remainder of that day.

entries.title: Samples And Results Management
entries.html: (K)57A Sample shall be taken and analysed in accordance with the Jockey Testing Code.

entries.title: Samples And Results Management
entries.html: (K)58The Jockey must comply with the Jockey Testing Code.

entries.title: Samples And Results Management
entries.html: (K)59If a Jockey establishes that a departure from the Jockey Testing Code is capable of invalidating the result of the analysis of a Sample, the burden shall be on the BHA to establish that the departure did not compromise the result of the analysis of the Sample.

entries.title: Evidential Sufficiency
entries.html:
(K)60The presence of a Banned Substance or alcohol in the following is sufficient evidence of a breach of Rule (K)49, (K)53 or, where urine is relied upon, Rule (K)55: 

60.1in the Jockey's A Sample, where (i) the B Sample is not analysed or (ii) the B Sample is analysed and is found to be compromised; 

60.2in the Jockey's A and B sample; or 

60.3in both portions of a B Sample, where the B Sample is split into two portions as a result of the Jockey's A Sample being unavailable or where it is believed to have been compromised.

entries.title: Reinstatement
entries.html: (K)61A Jockey whose Licence has been withdrawn as a result of a Human Anti-doping Rule Violation shall not be reinstated unless they have notified the Chief Medical Adviser of their intention to apply for reinstatement in accordance with the Jockey Testing Code.

entries.title: Investigations
entries.html:
(L)1The BHA has the power to inquire into or investigate any matter in order to monitor compliance with these Rules, irrespective of whether the matter:

1.1arises in Great Britain or elsewhere; or

1.2has been considered by the Stewards.

entries.title: Investigations
entries.html:
(L)2Approved Persons may:

2.1enter premises used for training horses which are owned, controlled or occupied by a Trainer and:

2.1.1inspect the premises;

2.1.2conduct identification and vaccination checks on any horse; and

2.1.3inspect and take copies of any records the Trainer is required to keep under these Rules.

2.2examine horses under the care of a Trainer and take Samples from them for analysis;

2.3require a Person to immediately or by such other time as specified by the Approved Person (or use reasonable endeavours to procure the provision by any third party): 

2.3.1provide the Approved Person with, or access to, objects, information, documents or records (including Listed Information), in such form as the Approved Person may require, and which are held by the Person or within their power to obtain;

2.3.2allow an Approved Person to inspect, copy, image or download any electronic communication and storage devices in the possession or control of the Person (including without limitation mobile telephones, tablets, laptops, smart watches and hard drives);

2.3.3give the Approved Person access to or allow them to download data from any web-based accounts and applications owned, belonging to, in the name of or operated by the Person (including without limitation e-wallets, bank accounts ,applications used for cloud-based storage, communications, financial services (in any type of currency), cryptocurrency, peer-to-peer mediums of value transfer or social media); and

2.3.4provide the Approved Person with passwords, login credentials and other information required to access any item requested pursuant to this Rule (L)2.3, and to not change the provided details until further notice is given by the Approved Person or without permission from the BHA.

2.4require a Person to answer questions at an interview (in such cases, the Person may request a reasonable delay to the interview in order to seek legal advice);

2.5inspect and take custody of any vehicle used in relation to the training of a horse or the transportation of any horse or Person to or from a racecourse;

2.6take samples and custody of any feedstuffs or feed additives or of any other substances or materials;

2.7conduct a search of any Person and take samples or custody of any article or materials found on such Persons; and

2.8take samples from a Jockey including, but not limited to, breath, hair, urine and blood.

entries.title: Compliance with requests of Approved Persons
path: Compliance with requests of Approved Persons
entries.html:
Specific provisions: providing information, documents or records

(L)3The BHA must approve each request made for Listed Information.

entries.title: Compliance with requests of Approved Persons
path: Compliance with requests of Approved Persons
entries.html: (L)4Where an Approved Person makes a request for a telephone billing account, they may require itemised details of all calls made and received during a specified period.

entries.title: Compliance with requests of Approved Persons
path: Compliance with requests of Approved Persons
entries.html:
(L)5Where an Approved Person requires a Person to attend an interview, the Person must:

5.1agree a time and place for the interview within the time specified in the demand; and

5.2attend the interview at the agreed time and place.

Duty to cooperate

entries.title: Compliance with requests of Approved Persons
path: Compliance with requests of Approved Persons
entries.html:
(L)6A Person must cooperate with an Approved Person in the exercise of any of their powers.

Duty to preserve evidence

6A    A Person must:

       6A.1    preserve and not tamper with or hide evidence related to a breach of the Rules; and

       6A.2    not encourage or facilitate any third party to tamper with or hide evidence related to a possible breach of the Rules.

entries.title: Correcting Stewards’ Decisions
entries.html:
(L)7The BHA may quash a decision of, or reduce any sanction imposed by, the Stewards where they have made a clear error, or where it otherwise considers it appropriate. Where the BHA does so:

7.1the affected Person(s) shall be notified of the substituted decision; and

7.2the Person(s) may appeal it in accordance with the Judicial Panels Code.

entries.title: Arabian horse racing and point-to-point Steeple Chases
path: Arabian horse racing and point-to-point Steeple Chases
entries.html: (L)8Any suspension imposed under the Regulations for Point-to-Point Steeple Chases or the Regulations for Arabian Horse Racing shall also have effect under these Rules.

entries.title: Forfeit List
entries.html: (L)9Where a Person is a Disqualified Person due to being on the Forfeit List, they may apply to the BHA to be removed from the Forfeit List and to cease to be a Disqualified Person.

entries.title: Forfeit List
entries.html: (L)10Where a person is a Disqualified Person due to being on a Recognised Racing Authority’s equivalent of the Forfeit List, they may apply to the BHA to cease to be a Disqualified Person.

entries.title: Forfeit List
entries.html: (L)11An application under Rule (L)9 or Rule (L)10 shall be determined by a Disciplinary Panel in accordance with the Judicial Panel Code.

entries.title: Forfeit List
entries.html: (L)12Where an application is made under Rule (L)10, the relevant Recognised Racing Authority may apply to the Disciplinary Panel to be represented at any hearing. Any such application, which shall be at the Recognised Racing Authority’s own expense, shall be determined by the Disciplinary Panel Chairperson.

entries.title: Action taken by the BHA
entries.html:
Exclusion Order

(L)13The BHA may issue an Exclusion Order against any person, whether or not they are subject to the Rules, where it is in the interests of racing to do so. The Exclusion Order may be indefinite, or for such period as the BHA may specify.

Power to prohibit Overseas Jockeys from riding in Races

entries.title: Action taken by the BHA
entries.html: (L)14The BHA may prohibit an Overseas Jockey from taking part in Race(s) for such period as it considers appropriate.

entries.title: Action taken by the BHA
entries.html:
(L)15An Overseas Jockey may appeal the prohibition to a Disciplinary Panel in accordance with the Judicial Panels Code.

Suspension

entries.title: Action taken by the BHA
entries.html:
(L)16Any suspension imposed under the Regulations for Point-to-Point Steeple Chases or the Regulations for Arabian Horse Racing will also have effect under these Rules.

Horse Suspension Grounds

entries.title: Action taken by the BHA
entries.html:
(L)17The BHA may suspend a horse in the following circumstances:

17.1Ground 1: a horse has been the subject of fraudulent practice;

17.2Ground 2: a Sample collected from a horse tested positive under Chapter K;

17.3Ground 3: a horse is the subject of an inaccurate, misleading or fraudulent declaration at the time of registration with the Stud Book Authority or the BHA;

17.4Ground 4: there is a reasonable suspicion that an Equine Anti-doping Rule Violation has been committed;

17.5Ground 5: the horse’s previous performances suggest the horse may be a risk to itself, to another horse or to a Jockey;

17.6Ground 6: there are other welfare concerns;

17.7Ground 7: there has been a failure to pay for the horse in accordance with the Claiming and Selling Code; or

17.8Ground 8: any other circumstances where it would be appropriate to do so.

entries.title: Action taken by the BHA
entries.html: (L)18Where a suspension is issued on the basis of one or more of the Horse Suspension Grounds, the Trainer, Jockey or Owner of the horse may apply to the Disciplinary Panel to lift the suspension.

entries.title: Action taken by the BHA
entries.html: (L)19The Disciplinary Panel shall only lift the suspension where the Trainer, Jockey or Owner of the horse has established good reason for reinstatement.

entries.title: Action taken by the BHA
entries.html:
(L)20Where a horse is suspended in accordance with Ground 5 of the Horse Suspension Grounds, any reinstatement may be subject to such conditions as may be set by the BHA.

Performance-related suspensions

entries.title: Action taken by the BHA
entries.html: (L)21Any horse suspended due to concerns with its jumping ability shall be required to pass a jumping assessment before its suspension is lifted.

entries.title: Action taken by the BHA
entries.html:
(L)22A horse suspended from running three times due to its performance shall be suspended from running, or running in specific types of race, indefinitely

Jockey Suspensions

entries.title: Action taken by the BHA
entries.html: (L)23The BHA may suspend the licence of any Jockey that has returned a Positive Analysis until the conclusion of any Disciplinary Panel proceedings.

entries.title: Action taken by the BHA
entries.html: (L)24The Jockey may apply to the Licensing Committee to lift a suspension impose under Rule (L)23.

entries.title: Action taken by the BHA
entries.html:
(L)25The Licensing Committee shall only lift the suspension where the Jockey has established good reason for reinstatement.

Racecourses

entries.title: Action taken by the BHA
entries.html: (L)26Once a Racecourse Licence has been granted, the BHA may issue fixed penalty notices up to a maximum amount of £500 in respect of a failure to comply with a requirement imposed by these Rules.

entries.title: Disciplinary Panels
entries.html:
(L)27The BHA has the power to take disciplinary action where it considers that there is reason to believe that there has been a breach of the Rules. It shall do so in accordance with the Judicial Panels Code.

Sanction

entries.title: Disciplinary Panels
entries.html:
(L)28Where a Disciplinary Panel finds that there has been a breach of these Rules, the Disciplinary Panel may do one or more of the following, in accordance with the Penalty Guidelines:

28.1impose a caution;

28.2impose a financial penalty not exceeding £75,000;

28.3impose the suspension or withdrawal of a Licence;

28.4declare that a Person is ineligible for a Licence, or other form of registration, under these Rules for such period as it may specify;

28.5declare that a Person is a Disqualified Person for such period as it may specify (including indefinitely);

28.6declare that no application to be employed in racing stables by a Disqualified Person be made for such period as it may specify;

28.7issue an Exclusion Order;

28.8order a Jockey to attend a course in remedial training at the British Racing School or National Horseracing College;

28.9disqualify a horse from one or more Races;

28.10suspend a horse from running in certain Races or for such period of time as it may specify, and subject to any conditions it deems appropriate; or

28.11such other penalty or order as it considers appropriate.

entries.title: Disciplinary Panels
entries.html: (L)29A penalty, or part of it, may be deferred, suspended or be contingent on an event.

entries.title: Applications for permission to be employed in racing stables by Disqualified Persons
path: Applications for permission to be employed in racing stables by Disqualified Persons
entries.html:
(L)30A Disqualified Person may apply for permission to be employed in a racing stable, but not before the later of:

30.1the expiry of the time limit for appealing the disqualification;

30.2any appeal of the disqualification has been determined; or

30.3the expiry of any period set by the Disciplinary Panel before an application can be made.

entries.title: Applications for permission to be employed in racing stables by Disqualified Persons
path: Applications for permission to be employed in racing stables by Disqualified Persons
entries.html: (L)31An application may be heard by a different Disciplinary Panel than the one which imposed the disqualification.

entries.title: Applications for permission to be employed in racing stables by Disqualified Persons
path: Applications for permission to be employed in racing stables by Disqualified Persons
entries.html:
(L)32An application must include:

32.1a full written submission in support;

32.2all evidence and documents on which the applicant wishes to rely; and

32.3a summary of the evidence of any supporting witness.

entries.title: Applications for permission to be employed in racing stables by Disqualified Persons
path: Applications for permission to be employed in racing stables by Disqualified Persons
entries.html:
(L)33Where an application is filed, the BHA shall be asked by the Disciplinary Panel:

33.1whether or not it opposes the application; and

33.2the reasons for any opposition.

entries.title: Applications for permission to be employed in racing stables by Disqualified Persons
path: Applications for permission to be employed in racing stables by Disqualified Persons
entries.html:
(L)34After the BHA’s response has been filed, the Disciplinary Panel Chairperson shall decide how to proceed to determine the application, including whether or not to hold an oral hearing. Such decision shall be final and binding.

Commencement of sanction

entries.html: (L)35Unless otherwise stated, a decision of a Disciplinary Panel shall take effect on the later of the time for an appeal expiring or an appeal being finally determined.

entries.title: Appeals
entries.html: (L)36The Judicial Panels Code sets out those decisions of a Disciplinary Panel that can be appealed to an Appeal Board, and the process that shall be followed.

entries.title: Start date for riding suspensions
entries.html:
(L)37A riding suspension imposed on a Jockey by a Disciplinary Panel shall start on the later of:

37.1eight days after the date of the Disciplinary Panel’s decision; or

37.2the day after an existing suspension ends.

entries.title: Start date for riding suspensions
entries.html: (L)38If a suspension for three months or less is appealed, it shall not take effect until the result of the appeal has been determined.

entries.title: Reciprocal suspensions and disqualifications
entries.html: (L)39Subject to Rule (L)40, the BHA shall reciprocate a suspension or disqualification imposed by another Recognised Racing Authority unless the Recognised Racing Authority requests that it should not be reciprocal.

entries.title: Reciprocal suspensions and disqualifications
entries.html: (L)40A Person may apply to the Disciplinary Panel for an order that the suspension or disqualification should not be reciprocated.

entries.title: Reciprocal suspensions and disqualifications
entries.html: (L)41A Person cannot make an application for the suspension or disqualification not to be reciprocated unless they have exhausted all appeal procedures available to them under the rules of the Recognised Racing Authority.

entries.title: Reciprocal suspensions and disqualifications
entries.html: (L)42Any application must be made in accordance with the Judicial Panel Code, and the suspension or disqualification shall be stayed pending determination.

entries.title: Reciprocal suspensions and disqualifications
entries.html:
(L)43An application must be made within three days of the later of:

43.1the suspension or disqualification being imposed by the Recognised Racing Authority; or

43.2any appeal against the suspension or disqualification under the rules of the Recognised Racing Authority being finally determined.

entries.title: Reciprocal suspensions and disqualifications
entries.html: (L)44The Disciplinary Panel may consider an appeal brought out of time if the applicant can establish that it was not possible to do so in time and that the application was otherwise made as soon as reasonably possible.

entries.title: Reciprocal suspensions and disqualifications
entries.html:
(L)45In hearing an application, the Disciplinary Panel shall only be concerned with whether there was a failure to comply with:

45.1the rules of the relevant Recognised Racing Authority; or

45.2the rules of natural justice in the process that led to the Recognised Racing Authority imposing a suspension.

entries.title: Reciprocal suspensions and disqualifications
entries.html: (L)46Where an application is made, the relevant Recognised Racing Authority may apply to the Disciplinary Panel to be represented at any hearing. Any such application, which shall be at the Recognised Racing Authority’s own expense, shall be determined by the Disciplinary Panel Chairperson.

entries.title: Horse Disqualifications
entries.html:
(L)47A horse shall be disqualified from a Race already run if:

47.1it has been the subject of fraudulent practice;

47.2at the time of the Race, the Jockey was not permitted to ride under these Rules;

47.3at the time of the Race, the horse was subject to a suspension;

47.4a Sample from the horse tests positive for a Prohibited Substance;

47.5the Responsible Person does not comply with the Sample collection provisions of Chapter K;

47.6the requirements for a horse to enter at paragraphs 12 to 20 of the Race Entry Code, and/or the qualifications for a horse to run in the Running Requirements Code have not been complied with;

47.7it carried less than the weight that it should have carried;

47.8it used a different name from that specified in the Register of Horse Names;

47.9it is the subject of a lease and ran in a Selling or Claiming Race without the lessee having obtained the lessor’s prior written consent; 

47.10it was the subject of an inaccurate, misleading or fraudulent declaration at the time of registration with the Stud Book and/or the BHA; or

47.11its Jockey has been found in breach of Rule (F)45 and the number of strikes (excluding those found to be clearly and unequivocally for safety purposes) is 4 or more above the permitted level.

entries.title: Horse Disqualifications
entries.html: (L)48A horse may be disqualified from a Race already run if an Equine Anti-doping Rule Violation has been committed.

entries.title: Horse Disqualifications
entries.html:
(L)49If a horse is disqualified:

49.1it shall not be given a position in the Race;

49.2it is not entitled to any prize; and

49.3except in the case of a stored Sample, the other horses’ positions shall be adjusted accordingly.

entries.title: Horse Disqualifications
entries.html:
(L)50If a horse’s position is adjusted:

50.1it is only entitled to the prize for the adjusted position; and

50.2the other horses’ positions shall be adjusted accordingly.

entries.title: Horse Disqualifications
entries.html: (L)51Other than in exceptional circumstances, if a horse is disqualified because it tested positive for a Prohibited Substance all prize money, other prizes or trophies must be repaid or surrendered as directed by the BHA.

entries.title: Horse Disqualifications
entries.html: (L)52If a horse is disqualified because it tested positive for a Prohibited Substance in a stored sample there shall be no alteration in the placing of any other horse in the Race.

entries.title: Consequences of being a Disqualified Person or made the subject of an exclusion order
path: Consequences of being a Disqualified Person or made the subject of an exclusion order
entries.html:
(L)53A Disqualified Person and anyone made the subject of an Exclusion Order may not:

53.1except where expressly provided by the Disciplinary Panel, be employed by a Trainer;

53.2enter Licensed Premises;

53.3be involved in any way with a horse that has ever been subject to these Rules, unless the BHA directs otherwise;

53.4be a BHA Official;

53.5be an Authorised Agent;

53.6enter, run, train or ride a horse in any Race, subject to any grace period under Chapter B;

53.7be associated with a Licensed equine swimming pool; or

53.8lease, or continue to lease, any horse that he owns to a third party, unless he has the BHA’s approval to do so.

entries.title: Consequences of being a Disqualified Person or made the subject of an exclusion order
path: Consequences of being a Disqualified Person or made the subject of an exclusion order
entries.html:
(L)54Any horse with which a Disqualified Person, or anyone made the subject of an Exclusion Order, has any involvement:

54.1shall be suspended from racing; and

54.2the suspension shall remain in place until the horse has been sold on the open market to someone who has no connection with the Disqualified Person, or the person to whom the Exclusion Order applies, or until the expiry of the disqualification or Exclusion Order.

entries.title: Consequences of being a Disqualified Person or made the subject of an exclusion order
path: Consequences of being a Disqualified Person or made the subject of an exclusion order
entries.html: (L)55A Trainer shall not train a horse owned by a Disqualified Person, or a person the subject of an Exclusion Order, without the BHA’s permission.

entries.title: Aims Of The BHA Safeguarding Function
path: Aims Of The BHA Safeguarding Function
entries.html: (M)1The BHA is committed to ensuring the welfare of Young Persons and Adults at Risk within racing. The BHA expects all Persons to share this commitment and maintain appropriate standards and behaviour in their dealings with Young Persons and Adults at Risk.

entries.title: Aims Of The BHA Safeguarding Function
path: Aims Of The BHA Safeguarding Function
entries.html: (M)2These Safeguarding Rules, incorporating the NSP Rules, establish a procedural framework through which the BHA may investigate matters concerning the harm, or possibility of harm, to Young Persons and Adults at Risk, and through which such matters may be addressed and determined.

entries.title: Aims Of The BHA Safeguarding Function
path: Aims Of The BHA Safeguarding Function
entries.html: (M)3The core aim of these Safeguarding Rules is to ensure the safety and welfare of Young Persons and Adults at Risk. The procedures detailed in these Safeguarding Rules are intended to be fair, straightforward and tailored to the needs of racing.

entries.title: Jurisdiction
entries.html: (M)4These Safeguarding Rules apply to all Persons.

entries.title: Prohibited Conduct And The Protection Of Young Persons And Adults At Risk
path: Prohibited Conduct And The Protection Of Young Persons And Adults At Risk
entries.html:
(M)5No Person may;

  • engage, or attempt or threaten to engage, in conduct that directly or indirectly harms the physical and/or mental welfare and/or safety of one or more Young Persons or Adults at Risk, and/or
  • pose a risk of harm to the physical and/or mental welfare and/or safety of one or more Young Persons or Adults at Risk (‘Prohibited Conduct’).

NOTE:

  •  'Harm' is not a narrow concept, and can mean different things in different contexts. Reference should be made to the BHA Safeguarding Policy.
  • It is not necessary for Prohibited Conduct to take place or arise in the context of racing and/or related activities. For example (and without limitation), in the event that a Person has been convicted or cautioned for, charged with, or arrested for any offence that concerns harm to one or more Young Persons or Adults at Risk (whether or not those Young Persons or Adults at Risk participate in racing), that may form the basis of action under these Safeguarding Rules as a result of that Person posing (or potentially posing) a risk of harm (regardless of whether or not the relevant offence, or alleged offence, took place in the context of racing and/or related activities).
  • The BHA recognises that, as in many activities, sexual relationships can develop within the sport of horseracing. However, an adult in a position of trust – meaning where an adult (1) has contact with a Young Person or Adult at Risk, (2) has a role that carries an expectation of trust, and (3) is in a position to exercise authority, power or control over the Young Person or Adult at Risk (as perceived by the Young Person or Adult at Risk) – must not engage in inappropriate sexual activity with a Young Person or Adult at Risk who they employ, care for, etc. (including not grooming a Young Person or Adult at Risk for sexual activity when that person no longer qualifies as a Young Person or Adult at Risk). A sexual relationship between an adult in a position of trust and someone over whom the adult has (or had) a position of trust will often be a breach of trust and an abuse of the relevant adult’s position. Inappropriate sexual relationships may result in an investigation or proceedings under these Safeguarding Rules, whether or not the relationship results in the commission of a criminal offence.

entries.title: BHA Safeguarding Case Management Group
entries.html: (M)6The BHA shall establish a BHA Safeguarding Case Management Group that (once established) shall be responsible for reviewing and guiding/assisting the work of the BHA and the BHA’s wider safeguarding function in respect of case management pursuant to the Safeguarding Rules. The BHA Safeguarding Case Management Group shall comprise a minimum of three persons, each of whom shall be of suitable experience, and at least one of whom shall be independent of the BHA and have at least ten years’ safeguarding experience drawn from a relevant legal, investigative, social care, risk assessment, and/or offender management background.

entries.title: BHA Safeguarding Case Management Group
entries.html: (M)7The BHA Safeguarding Case Management Group shall meet (1) at least once every two calendar months in order to review and discuss the progress of all active safeguarding cases being handled by the BHA’s safeguarding team - being, at any one time, all cases from the point of considering investigation to the point of the conclusion of any case (including by way of any form of appeal or review proceedings), and (2) as and when requested by the BHA, e.g., to seek guidance/assistance on an urgent matter.

entries.title: BHA Safeguarding Case Management Group
entries.html: (M)8The BHA Safeguarding Case Management Group may recommend and advise actions to be taken by the BHA in respect of any case(s). However, the BHA will retain ultimate responsibility for decisions made in respect of the handling of cases arising under these Safeguarding Rules.

entries.title: The BHA's Powers Of Investigation
entries.html: (M)9Upon the receipt of information from any source that gives the BHA reasonable ground(s) to suspect that a Person has engaged in Prohibited Conduct (including by posing a risk of harm of the kind detailed at paragraph 5(b)), the BHA will be entitled to investigate the matter.

entries.title: The BHA's Powers Of Investigation
entries.html:
(M)1010. In relation to any investigation commenced under these Safeguarding Rules, the BHA may:

10.1investigate the matter itself; and/or

10.2appoint others, including an independent safeguarding expert (or experts), to assist the BHA in relation to its investigation or investigate the matter on the BHA’s behalf.

entries.title: The BHA's Powers Of Investigation
entries.html: (M)11Section L of the Rules also applies to investigations undertaken pursuant to the Safeguarding Rules. The BHA may also require any Person (and request any other persons) to undertake a risk assessment by a suitably qualified person appointed by the BHA in such form as the BHA, at its discretion, considers appropriate (the cost of any such assessment in respect of a Person being risk assessed shall be borne by that Person, unless the BHA considers in the circumstances of an individual case that it is more appropriate for the cost to be borne by the BHA).

entries.title: The BHA's Powers Of Investigation
entries.html:
(M)12In carrying out investigations under these Safeguarding Rules, the BHA will have special regard to and will always take account of:

12.1the risk of harm that may be caused to Young Persons, Adults at Risk and others as a consequence of the investigation, particularly those who might already have been subject to harm; and

12.2how to minimise that risk of harm, balanced against the need to ensure the proper conduct and effectiveness of the investigation.

entries.title: Supporting Provisions
entries.html: (M)13No Person may knowingly employ, engage or otherwise instruct any individual who, in undertaking the activities for which they are employed, engaged or instructed, poses a foreseeable risk of harm to Young Persons or Adults at Risk.

entries.title: Supporting Provisions
entries.html: (M)14Without prejudice to any other obligations set out in the Rules or any other relevant BHA rules, regulations or procedures, Persons must comply with any BHA Disclosure and Barring Service Checks Policy (as may be in force from time to time, and whether as applicant or employee).

entries.title: Supporting Provisions
entries.html: (M)15All Persons subject to investigation under these Safeguarding Rules, or who may otherwise be asked to assist with any such investigation, must co-operate with the investigation.

entries.title: Supporting Provisions
entries.html: (M)16No Person may subject any other Person or other party to any detriment on the ground or belief that that Person or other party has reported a safeguarding concern to the BHA and/or assisted the BHA in any manner in relation to investigations or proceedings brought under these Safeguarding Rules.

entries.title: Supporting Provisions
entries.html: (M)17All Persons must report to the BHA any circumstances of which they are aware that indicate that a Person has engaged in Prohibited Conduct (including by posing a risk of harm of the kind detailed at paragraph 5(b)). A report should be made by the reporting Person using the reporting form made available by the BHA (on its website or otherwise) from time to time.

entries.title: Supporting Provisions
entries.html: (M)18No Person may make a malicious safeguarding report to the BHA, or otherwise act in bad faith in relation to matters covered by these Safeguarding Rules.

entries.title: Supporting Provisions
entries.html:
(M)19If any Person breaches any of the above provisions of this section (paragraphs 13-18), the BHA may take action against him or her under the Rules of Racing or any other applicable rules or regulations of the BHA (whichever is most appropriate in the circumstances).

NOTE:

The BHA wants to be presented with any information, from any source, where there is reason to consider that any Person has presented or presents a risk of harm to one or more Young Persons or Adults at Risk, so that appropriate action may be taken. In order for the BHA's work under the Safeguarding Rules to be effective, the co-operation of all Persons is necessary when requested by the BHA (or those acting on its behalf). The BHA may therefore view a failure to co-operate, or conduct designed at preventing or dissuading others from reporting concerns or co-operating, as a serious disciplinary matter.

In the absence of cogent evidence to the contrary, the BHA will operate on a working presumption that (1) all reports of possible Prohibited Conduct are made in good faith, and (2) all Persons act in good faith in relation to matters covered by these BHA Safeguarding Rules. However, the BHA will also view malicious reporting or acts of bad faith in relation to safeguarding matters seriously (e.g. where a false report is made to pursue a personal vendetta or false information is deliberately provided to an investigation).

entries.title: Provisional Risk Management Orders
entries.html:
(M)20In the absence of cogent evidence to the contrary, the BHA will operate on a working presumption that (1) all reports of possible Prohibited Conduct are made in good faith, and (2) all Persons act in good faith in relation to matters covered by these BHA Safeguarding Rules. However, the BHA will also view malicious reporting or acts of bad faith in relation to safeguarding matters seriously (e.g. where a false report is made to pursue a personal vendetta or false information is deliberately provided to an investigation).

20.1Apply to the Judicial Panel Chair for the imposition of a Provisional Risk Management Order; or

20.2In the circumstances where (a) the Judicial Panel Chair is not available to determine an application made pursuant to paragraph 20.1 (or delegate such determination in accordance with paragraph 31), and (b) the immediate imposition of a Provisional Risk Management Order is deemed necessary by the BHA, impose a Provisional Risk Management Order directly on the Person; or

20.3Agree the terms of a Provisional Risk Management Order to be imposed upon the Person with the consent of that Person. Any such terms will be evidenced in writing between the BHA and the Person (in a form as directed by the BHA) and once evidenced in writing will be deemed to be a Provisional Risk Management Order (despite no form of order being required from the Judicial Panel Chair).

entries.title: Provisional Risk Management Orders
entries.html: (M)21The imposition of Provisional Risk Management Orders pursuant to paragraph 20.2 shall coincide with (or otherwise be followed as soon as possible by) an application by the BHA to the Judicial Panel Chair to ratify the Order at the earliest practicable opportunity.

entries.title: Provisional Risk Management Orders
entries.html: (M)22A Provisional Risk Management Order imposed pursuant to paragraph 20.3 will not require ratification by the Judicial Panel Chair. If either party wishes to withdraw from the Order or amend the terms of the Order without the consent of the other party, an application should be made to the Judicial Panel Chair for the Order to be reviewed at the earliest possible opportunity. The terms of the Order previously agreed will remain in force until the matter can be reviewed.

entries.title: Provisional Risk Management Orders
entries.html: (M)23A Provisional Risk Management Order may prohibit or otherwise restrict a Person from all or any specific racing and/or related activities under the jurisdiction of the BHA, on such terms and conditions as might be reasonable and proportionate to the circumstances of the case.

entries.title: Provisional Risk Management Orders
entries.html:
(M)24A Provisional Risk Management Order shall be imposed only in cases where, and to the extent that, it is reasonable and proportionate. Prior to imposing a Provisional Risk Management Order, the BHA (in liaison with the BHA Safeguarding Case Management Group unless impractical to do so) will consider the following factors:

24.1whether any Young Person or Adult at Risk (or other person) is or may be at risk of harm;

24.2the prospect of any charge(s) made (or that might be made) pursuant to these Safeguarding Rules being upheld (i.e., the stronger the merits of the charge(s), the stronger the justification for a Provisional Risk Management Order);

24.3the seriousness of the alleged Prohibited Conduct (including the seriousness of the risk of harm of the kind detailed at paragraph 5(b)), i.e., the more serious a case is, the stronger the justification for a Provisional Risk Management Order;

24.4whether a Provisional Risk Management Order is necessary or desirable to allow the conduct of any investigation by the BHA, the police, or any other relevant authority to proceed unimpeded;

24.5the opinion of any safeguarding expert (should the BHA choose to seek such an opinion);

24.6the impact (or potential impact) that imposing a Provisional Risk Management Order might have on the Person who may be subject to the Order; and

24.7any other circumstances that might be relevant to the individual case.

NOTE:

The purpose of a Provisional Risk Management Order is to manage any immediate risk whilst investigations, either by a third party (e.g. police or any relevant local authority) or the BHA are ongoing. The purpose is not to resolve any disputes of fact. For risk assessment purposes and the assessment of whether an Order is reasonable and proportionate, the risk should be taken at its highest, meaning the decision-maker should assume the allegations are capable of being proved and assess the risk on that basis.

entries.title: Provisional Risk Management Orders
entries.html:
(M)25Where the Judicial Panel Chair considers an application, an application for ratification or a review in accordance with paragraph 20:

25.1where applicable, the relevant application, and any decision in respect of it, may be made with or without notice being given to the Person;

25.2the procedure for determining the application shall be determined by the Judicial Panel Chair, as appropriate to the circumstances of the application (the procedure shall include, save in exceptional circumstances, seeking representations from the Person);

25.3the Judicial Panel Chair may seek the opinion of an independent safeguarding expert in determining the application (the cost of which shall be borne by the BHA, subject to any later costs order of a BHA Panel or an NSP Tribunal);

25.4the test that the Judicial Panel Chair shall apply when determining the application or review is whether the Provisional Risk Management Order sought or imposed by the BHA is reasonable and proportionate, giving consideration to the factors set out at paragraph 24:

25.4.125.4.1 if the Judicial Panel Chair is satisfied that the Provisional Risk Management Order sought or imposed is reasonable and proportionate, the Judicial Panel Chair shall (as the case may be) impose or ratify the Order; and

25.4.2if the Judicial Panel Chair is not satisfied that the Provisional Risk Management Order sought or imposed is reasonable and proportionate, the Judicial Panel Chair may either (a) not impose or ratify the Order, or (b) impose a Provisional Risk Management Order on such alternative terms and conditions as they consider are reasonable and proportionate in the circumstances.

entries.title: Provisional Risk Management Orders
entries.html:
(M)26When a Provisional Risk Management Order is imposed, the BHA shall ensure that the Person upon whom the Provisional Risk Management Order is imposed is promptly notified of the following matters:

26.1the reasons why the Provisional Risk Management Order has been imposed, unless the BHA decides for good reason otherwise;

26.2the scope of the Provisional Risk Management Order, i.e., which racing and/or related activities the Person is subject to temporary measures in relation to (up to and including all such activities);

26.3such other terms and conditions as have been imposed; and

26.4the date upon which the Provisional Risk Management Order shall take effect (which may be immediate).

entries.title: Provisional Risk Management Orders
entries.html: (M)27The BHA will undertake periodic reviews of Provisional Risk Management Orders imposed on a Person in liaison with the BHA Safeguarding Case Management Group, giving due consideration to the factors set out at paragraph 24. The relevant period will be determined by the BHA with reference to the particular circumstances of the case.

entries.title: Provisional Risk Management Orders
entries.html: (M)28The BHA may at any time (i.e., following periodic review or otherwise) lift or seek to vary the terms of a Provisional Risk Management Order imposed on a Person, giving due consideration to the factors set out at paragraph 24.

entries.title: Provisional Risk Management Orders
entries.html: (M)29A Person who is subject to a Provisional Risk Management Order may, for good cause shown, request permission to apply to lift or vary the terms of the Order from the Judicial Panel Chair. The procedure for determining any request and consequent application shall be determined by the Judicial Panel Chair, who may refer the matter to the NSP in respect of any case proceeding before the NSP. Any application shall only be successful if and insofar as the relevant Person demonstrates the Provisional Risk Management Order imposed is not reasonable and proportionate to the circumstances of their case

entries.title: Provisional Risk Management Orders
entries.html: (M)30For the avoidance of doubt, (1) any steps taken by the BHA concerning Provisional Risk Management Orders shall not serve to preclude the jurisdiction of the NSP (rather than a BHA Panel) to proceed to hear the merits of the charge(s), should the BHA elect to pursue the matter through the procedures under the NSP Rules pursuant to paragraph 32, and (2) Rule 6 of the NSP Rules (Conduct of applications relating to Provisional Suspensions) shall not apply to any applications under these Safeguarding Rules save to the extent an NSP Tribunal may apply it to matters referred to the NSP pursuant to paragraph 29.

entries.title: Provisional Risk Management Orders
entries.html: (M)31The Judicial Panel Chair may in respect of any current or future application made under paragraphs 20-29 delegate their relevant functions to a member of the Disciplinary and Licensing Panel Pool, in which case the above references to the Judicial Panel Chair shall be read instead as references to the designated member of the Disciplinary and Licensing Panel Pool.

entries.title: Notice Of Charge And Response
entries.html:
(M)32If, as the result of an investigation commenced under these Safeguarding Rules, the BHA concludes that the Person has a case to answer, the BHA shall send a written notice of charge to that Person:

32.1confirming that a charge is being issued against the Person under these Safeguarding Rules and that the matter may be referred for determination by a BHA Panel or an NSP Tribunal;

32.2referring to (and attaching) any and all supporting evidence, information and/or documentation that the BHA wishes to rely on;

32.3setting out the risk management measure(s)/order(s) that the BHA considers appropriate if the charge is admitted or upheld; and

32.4requiring the Person’s written response to the charge within 14 days (or, where circumstances so warrant, such shorter or longer period as may reasonably be specified by the BHA).

entries.title: Notice Of Charge And Response
entries.html:
(M)33A charged Person must:

33.1admit the charge and accept the proposed risk management measure(s) (which, absent further direction by the BHA, will constitute an agreement in accordance with paragraph 52); or

33.2admit the charge but:

33.2.1not accept the risk management measure(s) proposed by the BHA; and

33.2.2provide a written response on the appropriate risk management order(s) and refer to (and attach) any supporting evidence, information and/or documentation which the charged Person wishes to rely on, including a written witness statement from any fact or expert witness upon which the charged Person wishes to rely; or

33.3deny the charge (in whole or in part), and:

33.3.1provide a written response setting out why the charge should not be upheld; and

33.3.2refer to (and attach) any and all supporting evidence, information and/or documentation that the charged Person wishes to rely on, including a written witness statement from any fact or expert witness upon which the charged Person wishes to rely.

entries.title: Notice Of Charge And Response
entries.html: (M)34If a notice of charge is sent to a Person who was under the age of 18 years when the relevant Prohibited Conduct is alleged to have occurred or arisen, the BHA may send a copy of the notice of charge to the charged Person’s parent or carer.

entries.title: Notice Of Charge And Response
entries.html: (M)35Following receipt of the Person's response to a written notice of charge, or in the event no such response is received within the period requested pursuant to paragraph 32.4, the BHA may (in their absolute discretion) refer the matter for a hearing before either a BHA Panel or an NSP Tribunal to determine appropriate risk management orders (if any) in accordance with paragraph 47 of these Safeguarding Rules.
