For the avoidance of doubt, no Person may appeal or challenge any aspect of the BHA’s decision as to whether to refer a matter to a BHA Panel or an NSP Tribunal (including whether such a referral is appropriate or as to which body a referral is made).

entries.title: Procedure Before BHA Panels And Nsp Tribunals
path: Procedure Before BHA Panels And Nsp Tribunals
entries.html:
(M)36If, following a notice of charge and any response, the BHA refers a Person to either a BHA Panel or an NSP Tribunal under these Safeguarding Rules, the BHA shall prepare and send a written notice of referral in the name of the BHA to the Person, which shall contain at least the following information:

36.1an outline of the process to be followed in relation to the referral; and

36.2contact details for the BHA Panel or the NSP Tribunal (as appropriate).

entries.title: Procedure Before BHA Panels And Nsp Tribunals
path: Procedure Before BHA Panels And Nsp Tribunals
entries.html:
(M)37The following matters arising under these Safeguarding Rules may be determined by the NSP and NSP Tribunals in accordance with the NSP Rules, as amended from time to time, which are deemed to be incorporated by reference to this paragraph:

37.1any referral to the NSP by the BHA on the basis that a Person has engaged in Prohibited Conduct (including by posing a risk of harm of the kind detailed at paragraph 5(b)); and

37.2any other matter that the BHA may reasonably refer to the NSP for determination in accordance with the NSP Rules.

entries.title: Procedure Before BHA Panels And Nsp Tribunals
path: Procedure Before BHA Panels And Nsp Tribunals
entries.html: (M)38The BHA may, as an alternative to a reference to the NSP under paragraph 37, refer a charge that a Person has engaged in Prohibited Conduct (including by posing a risk of harm of the kind detailed at paragraph 5(b), to a BHA Panel for determination in accordance with relevant parts of the Judicial Panels Code as though the Person were charged with a breach of the Rules of Racing. The Chair of any BHA Panel in such cases may read in such changes to the Judicial Panels Code as might be required and may give such directions as they consider appropriate for the purpose of ensuring a fair and expeditious conduct of the proceedings, with particular regard for the sensitive nature of safeguarding proceedings and the possibility (if appropriate) of adopting one or more of the ‘special measures’, as set out in the NSP Rules. Such ‘special measures’ may also be adopted in respect of the evidence of any witness where appropriate.

entries.title: Procedure Before BHA Panels And Nsp Tribunals
path: Procedure Before BHA Panels And Nsp Tribunals
entries.html:
(M)39In the case of any conflict between these Safeguarding Rules and the Judicial Panels Code, the former shall take precedence. Without limitation, the following provisions of the Judicial Panels Code shall not apply to any matter referred to a BHA Panel under these Safeguarding Rules:

39.1Paragraphs 23 and 24 (Hearings Conducted in the Presence of the Media). (Paragraph 66 of these Safeguarding Rules applies instead).

39.2Paragraphs 33 to 42 (Commencement of Proceedings and Charge Response Form). (Paragraphs 32-35 of these Safeguarding Rules applies instead).

39.3Paragraphs 43 to 48 (Plea Agreement). (Paragraphs 51-57 of these Safeguarding Rules applies instead).

39.4Paragraph 55 (Appeals). (Paragraphs 43-46 of these Rules and the NSP Rules (as amended by Paragraphs 43-46) apply instead).

39.5Part Four (Disciplinary Panels as an Appellate Body) and Part Six (Licensing Committee).

entries.title: Procedure Before BHA Panels And Nsp Tribunals
path: Procedure Before BHA Panels And Nsp Tribunals
entries.html: (M)40In the case of any conflict between these Safeguarding Rules and the NSP Rules that is not specifically provided for by these Safeguarding Rules, the NSP Rules shall take precedence in relation to matters proceeding before the NSP. Otherwise, these Safeguarding Rules shall take precedence.

entries.title: Summary Procedure
entries.html:
(M)41Notwithstanding any of the other provisions of these Safeguarding Rules, the BHA may, having liaised with the BHA Safeguarding Case Management Group, impose any risk management measure(s) on a Person by way of executive decision (i.e., without prior referral to a BHA Panel or NSP Tribunal). The BHA will impose such risk management measures when, and to the extent that, they are considered reasonable and proportionate by the BHA to manage an obvious risk to one or more Young Persons and/or Adults at Risk in light of receipt of the following information (and whether before or after affording the Person concerned the right to address any identified concern(s)):

41.1that the Person has been convicted of, or made the subject of a caution in respect of a criminal offence concerning a Child or Adult at Risk;

41.2that the Person has been found liable in respect of any other form of offence (e.g., a disciplinary or regulatory offence) or civil action; and/or

41.3is included or placed on any statutory barring lists.

entries.title: Summary Procedure
entries.html:
(M)42The BHA shall ensure that the Person upon whom any one or more risk management measure has been imposed is promptly notified of the following matters:

42.1 the reasons why the risk management measure has been imposed, unless the BHA decides for good reason otherwise;

42.2the scope of the risk management measure(s);

42.3such other terms and conditions as have been imposed (including any date(s) at which the risk management measure(s) may be reviewed);

42.4the date upon which the risk management measure(s) shall take effect (which may be immediate); and

42.5the Person’s right to appeal the imposition of the risk management measure(s).

entries.title: Appeals
entries.html:
(M)43The following decisions may be appealed to an NSP Tribunal (acting as an NSP Appeal Tribunal):

43.1a first instance decision of a BHA Panel or an NSP Tribunal issued pursuant to the procedure set out at paragraphs 36-40 of these Safeguarding Rules; and

43.2the imposition of risk management measures imposed by the BHA pursuant to the summary procedure set out at paragraph 41-42 of these Safeguarding Rules;

each to be deemed a first instance decision for the purposes of the NSP Rules.

entries.title: Appeals
entries.html: (M)44The NSP Rules will apply to all appeals, subject to (1) paragraphs 43-46, and (2) mutatis mutandis (i.e., with changes deemed to have been made as required to reflect the different context).

entries.title: Appeals
entries.html:
(M)45In respect of first instance decisions of a BHA Panel or NSP Tribunal, the grounds of appeal available to each of the Person and the BHA shall be that:

45.1the reasons given by the BHA Panel or NSP Tribunal are insufficient to support the decision reached;

45.2there was insufficient material on which the BHA Panel or NSP Tribunal could have made the decision in question;

45.3the BHA Panel or NSP Tribunal failed to hold a fair hearing;

45.4the BHA Panel or NSP Tribunal misconstrued, failed to apply or wrongly applied these Safeguarding Rules (or any other relevant rules or regulations);

45.5the order or risk management measure is so disproportionate that no reasonable BHA Panel or NSP Tribunal could have decided upon it; and/or

45.6there is evidence available for the appeal that was not available or obtainable at first instance but which, had it been available at first instance, would have caused the BHA Panel or NSP Tribunal to reach a materially different decision.

entries.title: Appeals
entries.html:
(M)46Save (1) in cases of appeals against the imposition of risk management measures imposed by the BHA pursuant to the summary procedure, or (2) where an NSP Tribunal orders otherwise as a consequence of exceptional circumstances, an appeal shall not be de novo and shall instead be by way of review of materials considered at first instance and any such additional evidence, except that:

46.1oral submissions will be permitted; and

46.2oral evidence will only be permitted if permission to introduce new evidence has been granted.

entries.title: Risk Management Orders
entries.html:
(M)47BHA Panels, the BHA acting under the Summary Procedure set out above, and NSP Tribunals may impose such risk management orders and/or risk management measures as they see fit. However, the BHA envisages that the following range of risk management orders are appropriate where, on the balance of probabilities, a BHA Panel or an NSP Tribunal concludes that a Person has engaged in Prohibited Conduct (including by posing a risk of harm of the kind detailed at paragraph 5(b)):

47.1guidance as to future conduct;

47.2an order requiring the Person to undertake specified training/education;

47.3a reprimand;

47.4a warning as to future conduct;

47.5an order requiring the Person to be monitored in specific matters and/or for a specified period of time (up to and including indefinitely) by a specified person or entity (which monitoring may be ordered to be at the Person’s cost);

47.6the suspension of, withdrawal of, or the imposition of conditions on, any licences, permits and/or registrations held by the Person, either temporarily or permanently;

47.7a period of suspension or disqualification for a specific period of time (up to and including indefinitely) from involvement in any racing and/or related activities under the jurisdiction of the BHA on such terms and conditions as considered appropriate; and/or

47.8an order excluding the Person from any premises licensed by the BHA for a specific period of time (up to and including indefinitely).

entries.title: Risk Management Orders
entries.html:
(M)48In determining the appropriate management order(s), BHA Panels and NSP Tribunals may take into account:

48.1the seriousness of the Prohibited Conduct and/or risk of harm;

48.2the impact of any relevant conduct on any affected Young Person or Adult at Risk;

48.3the context of the particular situation (including whether there is a pattern of inappropriate behaviour or misconduct and the age(s) and/or other circumstances of the persons involved);

48.4whether the Prohibited Conduct in question was deliberate, reckless and/or negligent;

48.5any continuing risk a Person may pose;

48.6the enforceability of any risk management order in practical terms; and

48.7any ‘aggravating’ or ‘mitigating’ factors that exist (in the opinion of the BHA Panel or NSP Tribunal) in the context of the particular circumstances.

entries.title: Risk Management Orders
entries.html: (M)49BHA Panels and NSP Tribunals may choose to suspend all or part of any risk management order it has imposed.

entries.title: Publication
entries.html: (M)50The BHA may publish and/or share details of risk management orders and risk management measures, including Provisional Risk Management Orders or any other interim measures, on a ‘need to know’ basis in such form and manner, and to such extent, as it deems necessary for the purposes of enforcement and/or compliance. The BHA may also take such administrative steps as it deems necessary or appropriate in order to give effect to risk management orders and risk management measures, including Provisional Risk Management Orders or any other interim measures imposed by the BHA, BHA Panels and NSP Tribunals (i.e., such risk management orders will not require any further act of ratification by any other body).

entries.title: Conclusion Of Cases Other Than By Determination By A BHA Panel Or Nsp Tribunal Or Summary Procedure
path: Conclusion Of Cases Other Than By Determination By A BHA Panel Or Nsp Tribunal Or Summary Procedure
entries.html: (M)51If, at any stage prior to a referral under paragraph 36, the BHA concludes that (1) there is insufficient evidence to charge/proceed with a charge, and/or (2) a referral would not further the aims of these Safeguarding Rules, and/or (3) there is any other bona fide reason for the BHA not to refer the matter, then the BHA may take such other action as it considers appropriate in all the circumstances of the case. For example, without limitation, the BHA may inform a Person that they have no case to answer under these Safeguarding Rules, provide a Person with guidance as to their future conduct, or refer the matter to another body (where the BHA is satisfied that other body will deal with the matter effectively).

entries.title: Conclusion Of Cases Other Than By Determination By A BHA Panel Or Nsp Tribunal Or Summary Procedure
path: Conclusion Of Cases Other Than By Determination By A BHA Panel Or Nsp Tribunal Or Summary Procedure
entries.html: (M)52Notwithstanding any of the other provisions of these Safeguarding Rules, at any time prior to the commencement of deliberations by a BHA Panel or an NSP Tribunal, it will be open to a Person to agree with the BHA on the appropriate risk management measure(s) (including in respect of Provisional Risk Management Orders or any other interim measures) to be imposed upon him/her in order to avoid the need for a determination by a BHA Panel or an NSP Tribunal.

entries.title: Conclusion Of Cases Other Than By Determination By A BHA Panel Or Nsp Tribunal Or Summary Procedure
path: Conclusion Of Cases Other Than By Determination By A BHA Panel Or Nsp Tribunal Or Summary Procedure
entries.html: (M)53Any such discussions between the BHA and the relevant Person may take place on a “without prejudice” basis and in such manner that they will not delay or in any other way interfere with an investigation or any proceedings.

entries.title: Conclusion Of Cases Other Than By Determination By A BHA Panel Or Nsp Tribunal Or Summary Procedure
path: Conclusion Of Cases Other Than By Determination By A BHA Panel Or Nsp Tribunal Or Summary Procedure
entries.html: (M)54Any resulting agreement will be evidenced in writing between the BHA and the relevant Person (in a form as directed by the BHA) and set out the risk management measure(s) imposed on the relevant Person.

entries.title: Conclusion Of Cases Other Than By Determination By A BHA Panel Or Nsp Tribunal Or Summary Procedure
path: Conclusion Of Cases Other Than By Determination By A BHA Panel Or Nsp Tribunal Or Summary Procedure
entries.html: (M)55In reaching an agreement under paragraph 52 of these Safeguarding Rules, the BHA will have due regard to the range of risk management orders set out at paragraph 47 of these Safeguarding Rules, but it may agree any measure(s) appropriate to the case at hand.

entries.title: Conclusion Of Cases Other Than By Determination By A BHA Panel Or Nsp Tribunal Or Summary Procedure
path: Conclusion Of Cases Other Than By Determination By A BHA Panel Or Nsp Tribunal Or Summary Procedure
entries.html: (M)56If an agreement is reached, determination by a BHA Panel or an NSP Tribunal will not be required.

entries.title: Conclusion Of Cases Other Than By Determination By A BHA Panel Or Nsp Tribunal Or Summary Procedure
path: Conclusion Of Cases Other Than By Determination By A BHA Panel Or Nsp Tribunal Or Summary Procedure
entries.html: (M)57A Person who agrees to resolve proceedings in accordance with paragraph 52 of these Safeguarding Rules will waive their right to appeal against or otherwise challenge any aspect of the agreed outcome.

entries.title: Exceptional Material
entries.html: (M)58In considering any Provisional Risk Management Orders, or any charge, appeal or other matter brought pursuant to these Safeguarding Rules, the relevant decision-makers may not in the ordinary course of events consider any evidence provided by either the BHA or the relevant Person that the other party has not seen and had a reasonable opportunity to respond to. Exceptionally however, the BHA or the relevant Person may make an application for permission to submit evidence that has not been provided to the other party where the BHA or the relevant Person considers that such evidence should not be provided to the other party because revealing it (or the identity of, or anything which might reveal the identity of, any individual within such evidence) to the other party may (1) create a risk of harm to any person, and/or (2) be unlawful, and/or (3) prejudice an ongoing investigation (by the BHA, the police, or any other relevant authority). Applications under this paragraph should be lodged with the Judicial Panel Chair or (following a referral to the NSP) the NSP President as soon as possible.

entries.title: Exceptional Material
entries.html: (M)59Where either the BHA or the relevant Person makes an application for permission to submit exceptional material to any relevant decision-maker, the applicant party shall provide reasonable advance notice to the other party, unless the applicant party considers that such written notice itself may (1) create a risk of harm to any person, and/or (2) be unlawful, and/or (3) prejudice an ongoing investigation. Any reply from the other party must be provided alongside any application.

entries.title: Exceptional Material
entries.html: (M)60The Judicial Panel Chair or NSP President will appoint an appropriate person from the Disciplinary and Licensing Panel Pool or the NSP to determine any application brought under paragraph58, and the appointed person shall otherwise have no involvement in the proceedings. The appointed person will issue such directions as they consider appropriate to determine the application, and they may allow or reject the application in whole or in part. In making their decision, the appointed person may seek the opinion of an independent expert.

entries.title: Exceptional Material
entries.html: (M)61If the appointed person allows the evidence to be submitted to the relevant decision- maker but withheld from the other party, the appointed person shall consider whether a redacted version of the evidence and/or a summary of the evidence should be provided to the other party as an alternative.

entries.title: Miscellaneous
entries.html: (M)62These Safeguarding Rules are to be interpreted and applied by reference to their core aim of ensuring the safety and welfare of Young Persons and Adults at Risk. Such interpretation and application shall take precedence over any strict legal or technical interpretations that may otherwise be proposed. The BHA's Safeguarding Policy and any related documents that may be published by the BHA from time to time may be referred to as interpretative aids.

entries.title: Miscellaneous
entries.html: (M)63In the event that any incident or other matter occurs that is not provided for in these Safeguarding Rules (whether it relates to conduct, jurisdiction, investigation, procedure, sanction or otherwise), then the BHA, Judicial Panel Chair, BHA Panel Chair (following a referral to a BHA Panel), or (following a referral to the NSP) the NSP President or any appointed NSP Tribunal may take such action as considered appropriate in the circumstances, taking into account the specific circumstances of the individual case and the principles of natural justice and fairness.

entries.title: Miscellaneous
entries.html: (M)64Minor practical or technical points will not serve to invalidate the procedure or any decisions or findings made under these Safeguarding Rules, so long as the principles of natural justice and fairness are not infringed.

entries.title: Miscellaneous
entries.html: (M)65In the event that any matter or conduct falling under these Safeguarding Rules also falls under any other part(s) of the Rules of Racing or any other relevant BHA rules, regulations or procedures (as may from time to time be in force), or is subject to investigation by the police or other public authority (or analogous body, such as another sports governing body), or is subject to any other legal/regulatory/disciplinary process, then the BHA, Judicial Panel Chair, BHA Panel Chair (following a referral to a BHA Panel), or (following a referral to the NSP) the NSP President or any appointed NSP Tribunal, may at any point temporarily suspend the procedure under these Safeguarding Rules. For the avoidance of doubt, in the event that any matter or conduct falling under these Safeguarding Rules also falls under any other part(s) of the Rules of Racing or any other relevant BHA rules or regulations, the BHA expressly reserves its right to bring proceedings under those other rules or regulations (regardless of whether proceedings are also brought under these Safeguarding Rules).

entries.title: Miscellaneous
entries.html: (M)66Save to the extent that disclosure and/or publication is provided for in these Safeguarding Rules, or is otherwise in accordance with the law, all matters considered under these Safeguarding Rules, will, so far as practicable, be regarded as confidential.

entries.title: Miscellaneous
entries.html: (M)67These Safeguarding Rules are governed by English law.

entries.title: Miscellaneous
entries.html: (M)68If any part of these Safeguarding Rules (including the NSP Rules) is ruled to be invalid, unenforceable or illegal for any reason, that part will be deemed deleted, and the rest of these Safeguarding Rules will remain in full force and effect.

entries.title: Miscellaneous
entries.html: (M)69Neither the BHA, nor any person employed by or appointed to assist the BHA, will be liable to any party for any act or omission unless it is actuated by malice or bad faith

entries.title: Miscellaneous
entries.html: (M)70These Safeguarding Rules have an effective date of 1st January 2019. The substantive provisions of these Safeguarding Rules shall not apply retrospectively to matters arising before that date (but, for the avoidance of doubt, a Person may be considered to pose a risk of harm as a consequence of conduct or circumstances that took place prior to the effective date).

entries.title: Miscellaneous
entries.html: (M)71These Safeguarding Rules were last amended on 20 May 2026 with such amendments coming into effect on that date, save that proceedings pending as at that date shall continue to be governed by the Safeguarding Rules as in force at the time the proceedings were brought (unless the parties to the proceedings agree otherwise).

entries.title: Miscellaneous
entries.html: (M)72The BHA may further amend these Safeguarding Rules from time to time. Such amendments will come into effect on the date specified by the BHA.

entries.title: General
entries.html:
1Failure to comply with this Code may result in:

1.1a Claim or bid for the winning horse being declared void;

1.2a prohibition on future participation in Claiming Races or Selling Races;

1.3inclusion on the Forfeit List, in the event of non-payment of an amount due;

1.4a suspension on the horse from running; and

1.5disciplinary action being taken.

entries.title: Submitting a Claim
path: Claiming in a Claiming Race or Selling Race
entries.html: 2The BHA may refuse any Claim.

entries.title: Submitting a Claim
path: Claiming in a Claiming Race or Selling Race
entries.html:
3A Claim must be submitted using the Telephone Claiming Line.

Timing

entries.title: Submitting a Claim
path: Claiming in a Claiming Race or Selling Race
entries.html:
4A Claim must be submitted:

4.1on the day of the Race; and

4.2not later than 15 minutes after the start of the Race.

entries.title: Submitting a Claim
path: Claiming in a Claiming Race or Selling Race
entries.html:
5A Person that contacts the Telephone Claiming Line and is placed in a queue before the deadline in paragraph 4 will be permitted to submit a Claim.

Process

entries.title: Submitting a Claim
path: Claiming in a Claiming Race or Selling Race
entries.html:
6The following information must be provided when submitting a Claim:

6.1the security code of the Person submitting the Claim;

6.2the name of the horse that is the subject of the Claim;

6.3whether the Claim is a Reclaim or a Third Party Claim;

6.4the name of the Person submitting the Claim and, if different, the name of the Person on whose behalf the Claim is submitted;

6.5payment details; and

6.6contact telephone number.

entries.title: Submitting a Claim
path: Claiming in a Claiming Race or Selling Race
entries.html:
7A Claim may only be submitted by:

7.1an Owner;

7.2an Owner’s Representative;

7.3a Trainer or Trainer’s Authorised Agent; or

7.4in respect of a Reclaim, by the Owner, Trainer or an Authorised Agent.

Publication of claimants

entries.title: Submitting a Claim
path: Claiming in a Claiming Race or Selling Race
entries.html: 8The BHA shall publish the names of anyone who submits a Claim.

entries.title: Premiums on successful Claims
path: Claiming in a Claiming Race or Selling Race
entries.html: 9A premium may be added to the advertised price, as determined by the Racecourse and recorded in the Race Conditions.

entries.title: Premiums on successful Claims
path: Claiming in a Claiming Race or Selling Race
entries.html: 10There shall be no premium payable in the case of a Reclaim where no other Claim was submitted.

entries.title: Prohibition on multiple Claims by the same Person
path: Claiming in a Claiming Race or Selling Race
Prohibition on multiple Claims by the same Person
entries.html: 11No Person may submit or have any involvement in the submission of more than one Claim per horse.

entries.title: Withdrawing or altering a Claim
path: Claiming in a Claiming Race or Selling Race
entries.html: 12A Claim may only be withdrawn or altered to avoid a breach of these Rules.

entries.title: Determining the successful Claim
path: Claiming in a Claiming Race or Selling Race
entries.html: 13No Claim for the winning horse shall be determined until the result of the Race has been announced.

entries.title: Determining the successful Claim
path: Claiming in a Claiming Race or Selling Race
entries.html: 14If one Person submits a Claim, they shall be successful. If two or more Persons submit a Claim, a ballot shall be conducted to determine the successful claimant.

entries.title: Notification of the successful claimant and payment of the Claim Purchase Price
path: Claiming in a Claiming Race or Selling Race
Notification of the successful claimant and payment of the Claim Purchase Price
entries.html:
15Once a Claim has been determined, the Racing Calendar Office shall telephone:

15.1the successful claimant; and

15.2the Clerk of the Scales who shall inform the existing Trainer of the horse.

entries.title: Notification of the successful claimant and payment of the Claim Purchase Price
path: Claiming in a Claiming Race or Selling Race
Notification of the successful claimant and payment of the Claim Purchase Price
entries.html:
16Following the determination of a Third Party Claim, the successful claimant:

16.1must pay the Claim Purchase Price to the Stakeholder immediately, unless the claimant is a Trainer in which case payment must be made within two working days; and

16.2may not sell or transfer title in the horse until the Claim Purchase Price is paid.

entries.title: Notification of the successful claimant and payment of the Claim Purchase Price
path: Claiming in a Claiming Race or Selling Race
Notification of the successful claimant and payment of the Claim Purchase Price
entries.html: 17Following the determination of a Reclaim, the claimant must pay any premium due within 12 days of the Race.

entries.title: Notification of the successful claimant and payment of the Claim Purchase Price
path: Claiming in a Claiming Race or Selling Race
Notification of the successful claimant and payment of the Claim Purchase Price
entries.html: 18Subject to paragraph 19, a Claim shall be void if the Racing Calendar Office is unable to contact the claimant or payment is not made on time. If this happens, and there was more than one claimant, the next claimant in the ballot shall be selected.

entries.title: Notification of the successful claimant and payment of the Claim Purchase Price
path: Claiming in a Claiming Race or Selling Race
Notification of the successful claimant and payment of the Claim Purchase Price
entries.html:
19A Claim shall not be void if:

19.1payment could not be made due to a technical failure by the BHA or the Racing Calendar Office; or

19.2the BHA exercises its discretion to pay the Claim Purchase Price and to recover the Claim Purchase Price from the successful claimant.

entries.title: Notification of the successful claimant and payment of the Claim Purchase Price
path: Claiming in a Claiming Race or Selling Race
Notification of the successful claimant and payment of the Claim Purchase Price
entries.html:
20If a Claim is void, and the only other Claim was a Reclaim, the horse shall remain with the Owner.

Payment methods

entries.title: Notification of the successful claimant and payment of the Claim Purchase Price
path: Claiming in a Claiming Race or Selling Race
Notification of the successful claimant and payment of the Claim Purchase Price
entries.html:
21Unless the claimant is a Trainer, payment for a Third Party Claim must be made by one of the following methods:

21.1using available funds in the claimant’s invoice account with the BHA; or

21.2by charge, credit or debit card supported by Amex, VISA or MasterCard.

entries.title: Disputes concerning a Claim
path: Claiming in a Claiming Race or Selling Race
entries.html: 22Any dispute concerning the selection of a successful Claim or collection of payment of the Claim Purchase Price shall be determined by the Stakeholder.

entries.title: Consequences of a Claiming Race being declared void
path: Claiming in a Claiming Race or Selling Race
Consequences of a Claiming Race being declared void
entries.html: 23The claiming process shall be void if a Claiming Race is declared void.

entries.title: Prohibitions following a Claiming Race
path: Claiming in a Claiming Race or Selling Race
entries.html:
24For 6 months following a Claiming Race, a claimed horse:

24.1may not be sold or transferred back to the Owner in whose name it ran, or to any Person who submitted a Claim for that horse, except where:

24.1.1the Claim was a Reclaim; or

24.1.2within that 6-month period, the horse has been:

(a) claimed in a subsequent Claiming Race or Selling Race;

(b) sold in a Selling Race; or

(c) sold in a public auction.

24.2may not return to the care of the Trainer in whose care it was in when it raced, except where:

24.2.1paragraphs 24.1.1 or 24.1.2 apply; or

24.2.2only one Claim was submitted for the horse.

entries.title: Minimum Selling Price and VAT
path: Sale of the winner in a Selling Race
entries.html:
25The Race Conditions for a Selling Race shall state:

25.1the minimum selling price for the auction; and

25.2the method of distribution for any amount by which the successful bid exceeds the minimum price.

entries.title: Minimum Selling Price and VAT
path: Sale of the winner in a Selling Race
entries.html: 26The Owner or Trainer of the winning horse in a Selling Race must advise the auctioneer if the horse is to be sold subject to any VAT.

entries.title: Disqualification, change of placing or delayed announcement of the winner
path: Sale of the winner in a Selling Race
Disqualification, change of placing or delayed announcement of the winner
entries.html:
27The winner of a Race shall be offered for sale by auction immediately after the Race, unless:

27.1the winner is disqualified or its placing altered; or

27.2the announcement of the Race result is delayed;

in which case the time for the sale shall be announced by the Stewards.

entries.title: Prohibition on coordinated bidding
path: Sale of the winner in a Selling Race
entries.html:
28In respect of any Selling Race, no Person may:

28.1prevent or seek to prevent by any means any other person from bidding for the winner; or

28.2accept, agree to accept or solicit any benefit whatsoever.

entries.title: Racecourse guarantee for the Sale Price
path: Sale of the winner in a Selling Race
Racecourse guarantee for the Sale Price
entries.html: 29The Racecourse must guarantee the winner’s sale price.

entries.title: Mandatory terms of contract
path: Terms of Contract, Premiums and VAT
entries.html: 30A person who submits a Claim or bid for the winner in a Claiming Race or Selling Race accepts the horse in the condition it is in when that Claim or bid is submitted. The Claim Purchase Price or bid price must be paid and shall  not be returned, irrespective of the condition of the horse.

entries.title: Vat
path: Terms of Contract, Premiums and VAT
entries.html:
Pre-race requirements

31Before the start of a Claiming Race or Selling Race, each Owner and Trainer must:

31.1check that the Owner’s VAT status is correctly stated on the list in the weighing room; and

31.2inform the Clerk of the Scales if the Owner’s VAT status is not correctly stated.

VAT payable on a Claim or successful bid

entries.title: Vat
path: Terms of Contract, Premiums and VAT
entries.html: 32In a Claiming Race or Selling Race, a successful claimant is liable to pay VAT save where the horse is successfully claimed or bid for by its current Owner.

entries.title: Vat
path: Terms of Contract, Premiums and VAT
entries.html: 33In a Selling Race, any VAT payable on the winning horse shall be calculated on the bid price or a portion of it if the horse is only partly owned by a person or company registered for VAT.

entries.title: Responsibility for a horse following a Claiming Race or Selling Race
path: Responsibility for a horse following a Claiming Race or Selling Race
entries.html: 34Horses that ran in a Claiming Race or Selling Race must not be removed from Racecourse Property for at least 60 minutes following the weigh in, except by the successful claimant or bidder.

entries.title: Responsibility for a horse following a Claiming Race or Selling Race
path: Responsibility for a horse following a Claiming Race or Selling Race
entries.html:
35After a Claim or sale of the winner is confirmed:

35.1the Trainer:

35.1.1must immediately lodge the horse’s Passport with an Equine Welfare Integrity Officer;

35.1.2shall remain responsible for the horse until any examination ordered by the BHA is complete.

35.2the purchaser:

35.2.1shall be immediately responsible for the horse, subject to any examination ordered by the BHA;

35.2.2must within three hours of the last Race:

(a) remove the horse from the Racecourse Stables; or

(b) make arrangements with the Racecourse Managing Executive for the care of the horse until it is collected, for which the Racecourse may charge a reasonable fee.

entries.title: Void Claims and sales of the winner
path: Void Claims and sales of the winner
entries.html:
36The BHA may void a Claim or sale of the winner if the horse has been disqualified on the following grounds:

36.1fraud or substitution;

36.2the horse ran at any Unrecognised Meeting;

36.3a Sample taken from the horse has tested positive for a Prohibited Substance; and / or

36.4the sex of the horse was wrongly recorded on the Racing Administration Website and the BHA are satisfied  that at the time of the Claim or sale of the winner the new Owner would not have been aware of the error.

entries.title: Void Claims and sales of the winner
path: Void Claims and sales of the winner
entries.html: 37Except as provided in paragraph 36, a Claim or sale of the winner following a Claiming Race or Selling Race shall not be affected by any change to the result after ‘Weighed In’ has been announced.

entries.title: Making the draw
entries.html:
1The draw for a Race shall be undertaken after:

1.1Declarations to Run have been submitted; and

1.2where applicable, the Race has been divided or the number of runners has been reduced.

entries.title: Making the draw
entries.html: 2Where a reserve horse is to run, the BHA shall allocate the draw order for that horse in accordance with the conditions of the Race.

entries.title: Changes to the draw order
entries.html:
3The BHA may change the draw order:

3.1in the circumstances set out in paragraphs 4 to 5; or

3.2if otherwise appropriate.

entries.title: Adding horses to a Race
entries.html:
4Where a horse is added to a Race:

4.1if it results in the elimination of another horse, the added horse shall take the saddle cloth number and draw position of the eliminated horse; or

4.2if it does not result in the elimination of another horse:

4.2.1if it is added before 2pm on the day of the deadline for Declarations to Run, the added horse shall take the next highest saddle cloth number and shall be allocated a random draw position; or

4.2.2if it is added after 2pm on the day of the deadline for Declarations to Run, the added horse shall take the next highest saddle cloth number and shall be allocated the highest number in the draw.

Where more than one horse is to be added to a Race

entries.title: Adding horses to a Race
entries.html: 5Where more than one horse is added to a Race, paragraph 4 shall apply to each added horse in an order determined by random ballot. If elimination is necessary for some of the added horses, those horses shall be added in accordance with the elimination sequence.

entries.title: General
entries.html: 1No equipment may be used in a Race unless it has been approved by the BHA.

entries.title: General
entries.html:
2The Stewards may:

2.1prohibit a Jockey from using any whip; and/or

2.2order the seizure and destruction of any body protector which does not meet the requirements of paragraphs 27 to 30.

entries.title: Headgear
entries.html: 3A horse cannot run in a Race wearing a garment fitted over its head or ears other than Headgear.

entries.title: Headgear
entries.html:
4The following are prohibited:

4.1any form of attachment to Headgear;

4.2the use of blinding Hoods; and

4.3modification of a Visor by covering the holes cut in the cowls.

entries.title: Requirement to declare Headgear or a Tongue Strap
path: Requirement to declare Headgear or a Tongue Strap
entries.html:
5Any Headgear or Tongue Strap to be worn by a horse in a Race must: 

5.1be declared when submitting a Declaration to Run; and

5.2not be the colour specified for the purposes of paragraph 14.

entries.title: Requirement to declare Headgear or a Tongue Strap
path: Requirement to declare Headgear or a Tongue Strap
entries.html:
6A Trainer may add or remove Headgear and/or a Tongue Strap after the Declaration to Run if they make a request to the BHA to do so and:

6.1the request is received within two hours of the deadline for Declarations to Run; and

6.2they pay the fee stated in the Fee Code.

entries.title: Requirement to declare Headgear or a Tongue Strap
path: Requirement to declare Headgear or a Tongue Strap
entries.html:
7A Trainer may substitute Headgear that has been declared for another piece of Headgear if they make a request to the BHA to do so and:

7.1the request is received prior to weighing out for the Race; and

7.2they pay the appropriate financial penalty.

entries.title: Requirement to wear Headgear or a Tongue Strap that has been declared
path: Requirement to wear Headgear or a Tongue Strap that has been declared
entries.html: 8The Headgear that has been declared must be worn by the horse on the way to the start and during the Race. If any Headgear that has been declared is not worn on the way to the start the horse will be withdrawn.

entries.title: Requirement to wear Headgear or a Tongue Strap that has been declared
path: Requirement to wear Headgear or a Tongue Strap that has been declared
entries.html:
9If a Tongue Strap is used, the Veterinary Officer must be satisfied:

9.1with the material of the Tongue Strap; and

9.2with the way in which it is fitted.

entries.title: Requirement to wear Headgear or a Tongue Strap that has been declared
path: Requirement to wear Headgear or a Tongue Strap that has been declared
entries.html: 10A Tongue Strap that comes loose may only be refitted by the horse’s Jockey or Trainer.

entries.title: Requirement to wear Headgear or a Tongue Strap that has been declared
path: Requirement to wear Headgear or a Tongue Strap that has been declared
entries.html:
11If a Jockey or Trainer cannot fit the Tongue Strap:

11.1the horse may still run; but

11.2if it does not, the financial penalty for non-runners will not apply.

entries.title: Requirement to wear Headgear or a Tongue Strap that has been declared
path: Requirement to wear Headgear or a Tongue Strap that has been declared
entries.html: 12If a horse declared to run with a Tongue Strap arrives at the start without it, the horse will be allowed to run but the Trainer will be subject to a financial penalty.

entries.title: Wearing Headgear or a Tongue Strap that has not been declared
path: Wearing Headgear or a Tongue Strap that has not been declared
entries.html:
13Subject to paragraph 14, if a horse arrives at the start with undeclared headgear or tongue strap, it must be removed, and the horse shall be allowed to run

13A    Any horse from which it is not possible to remove the undeclared headgear or tongue strap will be withdrawn by the Starter.

entries.title: Wearing Headgear or a Tongue Strap that has not been declared
path: Wearing Headgear or a Tongue Strap that has not been declared
entries.html:
14A Trainer may request permission for a horse to wear a hood of a specified colour on the way to the start, which must be removed:

14.1before the horse is loaded into the stalls; or

14.2before the horses are called in by the Starter,

14A    Any horse from which it is not possible to remove the hood will be withdrawn by the Starter.

entries.title: Shoes
entries.html:
15The following types of shoes are prohibited:

15.1shoes with studs;

15.2American type toe-grab plates; 

15.3shoes with a sharp flange;

15.4shoes with a trailered heel

15.5shoes with nail heads protruding more than 2mm from the Fuller Groove on the solar surface.

15.6shoes with exposed shoe edges that protrude beyond the hoof wall;

entries.title: Shoes
entries.html:
16Horses running in Flat Races conducted on turf must enter the parade ring fully shod except where:

16.1the BHA has consented before the Declaration to Run is submitted; or

16.2in exceptional circumstances the Stewards give permission.

entries.title: Nasal dilators, supports or bells
entries.html: 17A horse must not wear nasal dilators, supports or bells in the parade ring or in a Race.

entries.title: Lip Chains
entries.html: 18Lip Chains must not be used on a horse on Racecourse Property unless the chain is covered and connected to a lead rope which is under the control of a handler on the ground, except a French lip chain which may be worn without being connect to a lead rope, but must be removed before the horse goes to the Start.

entries.title: Bits
entries.html: 19A horse must not run in a bitless bridle.

entries.title: Bits
entries.html: 20All bits must be approved by a Veterinary Officer.

entries.title: Jockey Equipment
entries.html: 21Jockeys must keep their equipment in good condition and any modifications to Safety Equipment must only be undertaken by the manufacturer.

entries.title: Jockey Equipment
entries.html: 22A Jockey must present Safety Equipment for inspection when requested.

entries.title: Helmets and Body protectors
entries.html: 23Any Person who rides a horse on Racecourse Property must wear an approved helmet and body protector which are in good condition.

entries.title: Helmets and Body protectors
entries.html:
24A Trainer is responsible for ensuring that any Apprentice Jockey, Conditional Jockey, Stable Employee or other person who rides a horse under their care wears an approved helmet and body protector which are in good condition.

Helmets

entries.title: Helmets and Body protectors
entries.html:
25A helmet must comply with two different international testing standards, one from Group A and a different standard from Group B

Group AGroup B
British standard PAS 015 2011 and any subsequent updates.British standard PAS 015 2011 and any subsequent updates.
European standard (EN): UKCA and/or CE marked products referencing harmonised standard EN1384:2023.European standard (EN) UKCA or CE marked products referencing harmonised standard EN1384:2023.

American ASTM F1163: 2015 and any subsequent updates.
American Snell E2016 and any subsequent updates

25A    A helmet must contain the corresponding quality testing label.

entries.title: Helmets and Body protectors
entries.html:
26Helmets must be correctly fastened and adjusted.

Body Protectors

entries.title: Helmets and Body protectors
entries.html:
27Body protectors must:

27.1comply with certified safety standard (BS) EN 13158: 2018

27.2be at least Level 2

27.3have passed quality testing for the standard.

entries.title: Helmets and Body protectors
entries.html:
28Body protectors must not be:

28.1modified in any way, except those undertaken by the manufacturer; or

28.2attached to the horse or any equipment carried by the horse.

entries.title: Helmets and Body protectors
entries.html: 29No Person shall bring a body protector that has been modified by anyone other than the manufacturer onto Racecourse Property

entries.title: Helmets and Body protectors
entries.html: 30A Jockey must wear the same approved body protector during weighing out, the Race and weighing in.

entries.title: Whips
entries.html:
31A Jockey must carry an approved whip that meets the following specifications:

31.1for a Flat Race:

31.1.1the maximum length (including flap) is 70 centimetres; and

31.1.2there must be no binding within 17 centimetres of the end of the flap;

31.2for a Jump Race:

31.2.1the maximum length (including flap) is 68 centimetres; and

31.2.2there must be no binding within 23 centimetres of the end of the flap;

31.3the minimum diameter for a whip is 1 centimetre;

31.4the overall weight must not exceed 160 grams;

31.5the contact area of the shaft must be smooth, with no protrusion or raised surface, and covered by shock absorbing material throughout its circumference such that it gives a compression factor of at least 6 millimetres;

31.6the only additional feature that may be attached to a whip is a flap, which if attached must comply with the following requirements:

31.6.1the maximum length of the flap from the end of the shaft is 10 centimetres;

31.6.2the maximum width of the flap is 4 centimetres, with a minimum width of 2 centimetres;

31.6.3the flap from the end of the shaft must not contain any reinforcements or additions;

31.6.4the flap must have similar shock absorbing characteristics to that of the contact area

entries.title: Whips
entries.html: 32Other than adjustments to the handle or grip, a Jockey must not carry a modified whip.

entries.title: Other equipment
entries.html:
33A Jockey must:

33.1not ride in a Race wearing spurs;

33.2not ride in a Race wearing spectacles;

33.3where applicable, ride using soft contact lenses;

33.4ensure that all blindfolds have been removed from the horse before the ‘Off’; and

33.5not remove a horse’s ear plugs during a Race.

entries.title: Riding Fees And Prize Money
entries.html:
GENERAL

1A Jockey is not entitled to any riding fee, and the Owner is not liable for any riding fee, in respect of a Race where the Jockey is found in breach of:           

1.1Rule (F)34 (Dangerous Riding); or

1.2Rule (G)9 (failure to present themselves to be weighed in); or 

1.3Rule (F)45 (misuse of the whip) and their horse is disqualified under Rule (L)47.11

entries.title: Riding Fees And Prize Money
entries.html:
2A riding fee becomes payable:

2.1once the signal to mount is given, or

2.2if permission has been given for a horse to proceed to the start early, once the Jockey has mounted.

entries.title: Riding Fees And Prize Money
entries.html:
3Where a riding fee is payable, the Owner of the horse must pay an additional sum of: 

3.16% of the riding fee to the Trustees of the Professional Riders Insurance Scheme for application under the trusts of the Scheme; and

3.2£4.00 into the Professional Riders Career Ending Insurance (CEI) Scheme.

entries.title: Riding Fees And Prize Money
entries.html: 4An additional fee shall be payable where the Jockey has been substituted following weighing out.

entries.title: Riding Fees And Prize Money
entries.html:
5If VAT is payable, it must be paid in addition to the fee unless the Jockey is an Apprentice Jockey or Conditional Jockey (in which case the fee paid shall be inclusive of VAT where applicable). 

Flat Races

entries.title: Riding Fees And Prize Money
entries.html: 6The riding fee payable to a Professional Jockey for a Flat Race is £173.54.

entries.title: Riding Fees And Prize Money
entries.html:
7In respect of an Apprentice Jockey, any riding fee, payable under this Fee Code, and any Prize Money, payable to the Jockey under the Stakes and Prize Money Code, shall be split by the Apprentice Jockey and their employer as follows:

Riding FeesPrize Money
ClaimApprentice Jockey %Trainer %ClaimApprentice Jockey %Trainer %
7lbs80207lbs8020
5lbs80205lbs8020
3lbs/no claim80203lbs/no claim9010

For the avoidance of doubt, the Apprentice Jockey shall not be entitled to claim any expenses or contributions to any insurance premiums under the Apprentice Jockey’s Agreement with the Trainer.

entries.title: Riding Fees And Prize Money
entries.html:
8Where a riding fee is payable to an Apprentice Jockey, the Apprentice Jockey must pay an additional sum of 7.2% of the fee to the BHA for the purposes of industry training. 

Jump Races

entries.title: Riding Fees And Prize Money
entries.html: 9The riding fee payable to a Professional Jockey for a Jump Race is £235.90.

entries.title: Riding Fees And Prize Money
entries.html:
10In respect of a Conditional Jockey, any riding fees, payable under the Fee Code, and any Prize Money, payable to the Jockey under the Stakes and Prize Money Code, shall be retained by the Conditional Jockey.

For the avoidance of doubt, the Conditional Jockey shall not be entitled to claim any expenses or contributions to any insurance premiums under the Conditional Jockey’s Agreement with the Trainer.

entries.title: Riding Fees And Prize Money
entries.html: 11Where a riding fee is payable to a Conditional Jockey, the Conditional Jockey must pay an additional sum of 5.4% of the fee to the BHA for the purposes of industry training.

entries.title: Riding Fees And Prize Money
entries.html: 12Subject to paragraph 13, no fee is payable to an Amateur Jockey for a Jump Race.

entries.title: Riding Fees And Prize Money
entries.html:
13Where an Amateur Jockey:

13.1rides in a Race that is not confined solely to Amateur Jockeys; 

13.2has had more than 75 rides in Great Britain in races open to Professional Jockeys; and

13.3rides a horse in the Race that is not the sole property of that Amateur Jockey and/or one or more of their Family Members,

a fee is payable to the BHA for a Jump Race of £235.90.

Physical Therapy

entries.title: Riding Fees And Prize Money
entries.html:
14Where a fee is payable to a Professional Jockey, the Jockey shall pay the additional sum of:

14.10.5% in respect of a Flat Race; or

14.20.65% in respect of a Jump Race

to the BHA for the provision of on-course physical therapy services.

Valets

entries.title: Riding Fees And Prize Money
entries.html:
15A Valet shall be paid a daily attendance entitlement from the Jockeys’ Valets’ Attendance Fund in relation to each occasion that they attend and provide services at a Race Meeting, and the rate shall be determined by the BHA.

Non-Runners

entries.title: Riding Fees And Prize Money
entries.html:
16Any Professional Jockey who has been declared to ride a horse by the deadline for Declaration of Jockeys, but whose horse is subsequently made a non-runner will receive a fee of £86.77 (Flat) and £117.95 (Jump), unless;

16.1the Professional Jockey is substituted onto another horse in the race in accordance with paragraph 64 of the Race Entry Code, whereupon the fee will be transferred to that substituted rider, provided that they were due to receive a riding fee; or

16.2the reason for the horse being declared a non-runner was due to the Professional Jockey becoming unavailable to ride and there was no suitable replacement available.

entries.title: Riding Fees And Prize Money
entries.html: 17No fee is payable where the Race Meeting or Race is abandoned or made void.

entries.title: Riding Fees And Prize Money
entries.html: 18No additional payments or deductions are applicable to either fee.

entries.title: Riding Fees And Prize Money
entries.html: 19The fee in paragraph 16 will not be due to any Jockey who is declared after the deadline for Declaration of Jockeys.

entries.title: Riding Fees And Prize Money
entries.html: 20No fee is payable to a Jockey who has been declared to ride a horse that is a non-runner in a Race that has been nominated as the Second Preference Race.

entries.title: Application to register a name for a horse
path: Application to register a name for a horse
entries.html:
1Except where the BHA directs otherwise, an application to register a horse’s name will only be accepted if:

1.1the horse’s identity is verified;

1.2the horse has been implanted with an identifying microchip;

1.3the horse has been accepted for inclusion in:

1.3.1the Stud Book;

1.3.2a Stud Book approved by the International Stud Book Committee;

1.3.3the Non-Thoroughbred Register, or

1.3.4the AQPS Register.

1.4the proposed name of the horse:

1.4.1complies with this Code; and

1.4.2has not been reserved under Rule (C)31.

1.5the horse, and its sire and dam, are each a product of a Natural Service or Covering and that, during breeding the horse had a full natural gestation in the body of the mare in which it was conceived.

entries.title: Application to register a name for a horse
path: Application to register a name for a horse
entries.html:
2An application to register a name for a horse foaled outside of Great Britain, Ireland or the Channel Islands must be accompanied by:

2.1the horse’s Passport if available;

2.2a statement from a Veterinary Surgeon that the horse has been implanted with an identifying microchip, unless such evidence is already contained in the horse’s Passport; and

2.3an Age and Markings Certificate.

entries.title: Application to register a name for a horse
path: Application to register a name for a horse
entries.html: 3The Veterinary Surgeon that signs an Age and Markings Certificate must be independent of the Owner and Trainer of the horse.

entries.title: Application to register a name for a horse
path: Application to register a name for a horse
entries.html:
4The BHA shall reject an application to register a name if:

4.1there is a discrepancy between the Age and Markings Certificate and the markings first recorded in the Stud Book or the Export Certificate; and

4.2the horse’s identity cannot be verified by a blood or a DNA test.

entries.title: Prohibited names
entries.html:
5A horse cannot be registered with any of the following names:

5.1a name already in the Register of Horse Names, unless paragraph 7 applies;

5.2a name followed by a number;

5.3a name designated as a protected name;

5.4a name of more than 18 characters, including signs or spaces;

5.5a name made up entirely of initials, or ones that include figures, hyphens, full-stops, commas, signs, exclamation marks, inverted commas, forward or backward slash, colon and semi-colon;

5.6a name that starts with a sign other than a letter;

5.7a name containing more than seven syllables; or

5.8a name which the BHA considers offensive or inappropriate.

entries.title: Names that may be registered subject to specific conditions being met
path: Names that may be registered subject to specific conditions being met
entries.html:
6A horse may be registered with:

6.1the name of a well-known person, if the person gives permission;

6.2a name of commercial significance if the BHA consents; or

6.3a name of a prominent company, product or trade if:

6.3.1the relevant person consents; or

6.3.2the BHA is satisfied that the name has an alternative common meaning.

entries.title: Names already in the Register of Horse Names
path: Names already in the Register of Horse Names
entries.html:
7A name in the Register of Horse Names shall become available for registration to a different horse as follows:

7.1a name registered to a broodmare, the earlier of:

7.1.110 years after the mare's death;

7.1.210 years after the last recorded year in which the mare was covered or produced a foal; or

7.1.3when the mare reaches 30 years of age.

7.2a name registered to a stallion, the earlier of:

7.2.115 years after the stallion's death;

7.2.215 years after the last recorded year in which the stallion covered one or more mares; or

7.2.3the year when the stallion reaches 35 years of age.

7.3a name registered to any other horse, the earlier of:

7.3.15 years after the horse's death; or

7.3.2the year when the horse reaches 20 years of age.

entries.title: Names already in the Register of Horse Names
path: Names already in the Register of Horse Names
entries.html: 8The BHA may allow a name in the Register of Horse Names to become available earlier than set out in paragraph 7 if the horse never raced.

entries.title: Order of priority for names claimed simultaneously
path: Order of priority for names claimed simultaneously
entries.html: 9The Racing Calendar Office shall determine by lot the order of priority for two or more horses that claim the same name simultaneously.

entries.title: General
path: Part One - Disciplinary Panel and Appeal Board Composition
entries.html:
Selection of Disciplinary Panel and Appeal Board members

1The Judicial Panel Chairman shall select members of:

1.1a Disciplinary Panel or Licensing Committee from the Disciplinary and Licensing Panel Pool, one of whom shall be selected as chairperson, in accordance with the Disciplinary Panel Terms of Reference or the Licensing Committee Terms of Reference; and

1.2an Appeal Board from the Appeal Board Pool, one of whom shall be selected as chairperson, in accordance with the Appeal Board Terms of Reference.

entries.title: General
path: Part One - Disciplinary Panel and Appeal Board Composition
entries.html:
2Each member of a Disciplinary Panel, Licensing Committee or Appeal Board must declare if they have a conflict or an interest in a case. If they do, they must either:

2.1recuse themselves; or

2.2obtain the consent of the parties to stay on the Disciplinary Panel, Licensing Committee or Appeal Board (as applicable).

entries.title: General
path: Part One - Disciplinary Panel and Appeal Board Composition
entries.html:
3Where a conflict or an interest in a case is declared, and the member neither recuses themselves in accordance with paragraph 2.1, nor obtains the consent of the parties in accordance with paragraph 2.2;

3.1the Disciplinary Panel Chairperson, Licensing Committee Chairperson or Appeal Board Chairperson (as applicable) shall determine whether the panel member shall remain on the panel; or

3.2where the panel member in question is the Disciplinary Panel Chairperson, Licensing Committee Chairperson or Appeal Board Chairperson (as applicable), the Judicial Panel Chairperson shall decide whether the panel member shall remain on the panel.

entries.title: General
path: Part Two - Procedural rules applicable to Judicial Panels
entries.html:
4Paragraphs 5 to 32 shall be referred to as the Procedural Rules. The Procedural Rules shall cover:

4.1Disciplinary Panels as a first instance body;

4.2Disciplinary Panels as an appellate body; and

4.3Appeal Boards

entries.title: General
path: Part Two - Procedural rules applicable to Judicial Panels
entries.html: 5Judicial Panels shall have the power to regulate their own procedure. The chairperson of the panel will normally determine procedural matters alone and, where submissions from the parties are required, such submissions will normally be requested in writing and without a hearing.

entries.title: General
path: Part Two - Procedural rules applicable to Judicial Panels
entries.html: 6Any breach of procedure by a Judicial Panel, or a failure by them to follow any direction given (including any time limit), shall not invalidate the proceedings or its outcome unless the breach is such as to seriously and irredeemably prejudice the position of the parties.

entries.title: General
path: Part Two - Procedural rules applicable to Judicial Panels
entries.html: 7Judicial Panels are disciplinary, rather than arbitral, bodies. In the interests of achieving a just and fair result, procedural and technical considerations must take second place to the paramount object of being just and fair to all parties.

entries.title: General
path: Part Two - Procedural rules applicable to Judicial Panels
entries.html:
8Judicial Panels shall have the power, where the subject matter or facts are sufficiently linked and where appropriate for the efficient disposal of proceedings, to consolidate proceedings so that they are conducted together and determined at a joint hearing. The circumstances in which the power may be exercised include:

8.1where breaches are alleged to have been committed in the same Race or at the same meeting; or

8.2where there is common evidence.

entries.title: General
path: Part Two - Procedural rules applicable to Judicial Panels
entries.html:
9The chairperson of the panel will give such directions as they consider appropriate for the fair and expeditious conduct of the case to include, but not limited to:

9.1lengthening or shortening any time limit;

9.2adapting or dispensing with any procedural steps; and

9.3holding a preliminary hearing.

entries.title: General
path: Part Two - Procedural rules applicable to Judicial Panels
entries.html: 10A party may apply to the Judicial Panel Chairman where it wishes to have a preliminary matter determined by a separate Judicial Panel.

entries.title: Standard of proof
path: Part Two - Procedural rules applicable to Judicial Panels
entries.html: 11Where any fact or matter has to be established to the satisfaction of a Judicial Panel, the standard of proof shall be the balance of probabilities.

entries.title: Evidence
path: Part Two - Procedural rules applicable to Judicial Panels
entries.html: 12A Judicial Panel is not obliged to follow the strict rules of evidence and may admit such evidence, and accord it such weight, as it sees fit.

entries.title: Evidence
path: Part Two - Procedural rules applicable to Judicial Panels
entries.html: 13A Judicial Panel may draw an inference from the failure of a Person or witness to provide evidence or answer a question as it considers appropriate.

entries.title: Adjournment and non-attendance
path: Part Two - Procedural rules applicable to Judicial Panels
entries.html: 14A Judicial Panel may adjourn a hearing for such period and upon such terms as it considers appropriate.

entries.title: Adjournment and non-attendance
path: Part Two - Procedural rules applicable to Judicial Panels
entries.html:
15A Judicial Panel may require a person to:

15.1attend a hearing; and / or

15.2produce any relevant documents.

entries.title: Adjournment and non-attendance
path: Part Two - Procedural rules applicable to Judicial Panels
entries.html: 16If a person fails to attend a hearing when required to do so, the Judicial Panel may proceed with the hearing in such manner as it considers appropriate, including proceeding to make findings and to issue sanctions.

entries.title: Legal representation
path: Part Two - Procedural rules applicable to Judicial Panels
entries.html: 17A party to proceedings has a right to be legally represented. As soon as reasonably practicable the BHA must be notified of the representative.

entries.title: Legal representation
path: Part Two - Procedural rules applicable to Judicial Panels
entries.html: 18A party to proceedings must state the address to which communications should be sent.

entries.title: Confidentiality
path: Part Two - Procedural rules applicable to Judicial Panels
entries.html: 19Subject to paragraphs 20 to 22, all written representations, submissions, evidence, transcripts and documents created in the course of proceedings shall be treated as being confidential and cannot be further disclosed or otherwise used outside of those proceedings.

entries.title: Confidentiality
path: Part Two - Procedural rules applicable to Judicial Panels
entries.html:
20The BHA may publish information regarding a case at any time. Such information may include, but is not limited to:

20.1details of any steps taken against any respondent or appellant, including any charges brought, appeals or facts alleged in support;

20.2any representations, submissions, evidence and/or documents created in the course of the proceedings; or

20.3any direction or finding made or sanction imposed.

entries.title: Confidentiality
path: Part Two - Procedural rules applicable to Judicial Panels
entries.html: 21The BHA may disclose information concerning a case to any person in circumstances where the BHA considers that such disclosure may assist the initiation, conduct or defence of any criminal or quasi-criminal investigation or proceeding, or the regulatory or disciplinary process of any trade profession or sport whether in the UK or elsewhere.

entries.title: Confidentiality
path: Part Two - Procedural rules applicable to Judicial Panels
entries.html: 22The BHA may use and rely upon any representations, submissions, evidence, recordings, transcripts and documents created or provided in the course of any proceedings for the purpose of carrying out its regulatory functions, to include but not limited to monitoring compliance with the Rules.

entries.title: Hearings conducted in the presence of the media
path: Part Two - Procedural rules applicable to Judicial Panels
Hearings conducted in the presence of the media
entries.html: 23Hearings will be open to representatives of the media unless the chairperson of the panel directs otherwise.

entries.title: Hearings conducted in the presence of the media
path: Part Two - Procedural rules applicable to Judicial Panels
Hearings conducted in the presence of the media
entries.html: 24When attending a hearing, the media must respect paragraph 19 above. The chairperson of the panel may direct that certain matters arising during the course of a hearing may not be published.

entries.title: Recordings
path: Part Two - Procedural rules applicable to Judicial Panels
entries.html: 25Subject to paragraph 26, a person must not record a hearing.

entries.title: Recordings
path: Part Two - Procedural rules applicable to Judicial Panels
entries.html:
26Hearings shall be recorded by the BHA and any such recording shall be:

26.1owned by the BHA; and

26.2confidential.

entries.title: Recordings
path: Part Two - Procedural rules applicable to Judicial Panels
entries.html:
27Subject to paragraph 60 and paragraph 81, no person shall have the right to compel the production of a recording or any copy or transcript:

27.1except as required by law; and

27.2subject to payment of the BHA’s costs of production.

entries.title: Deliberations
path: Part Two - Procedural rules applicable to Judicial Panels
entries.html: 28Deliberations of Judicial Panels shall take place in private.

entries.title: Decision
path: Part Two - Procedural rules applicable to Judicial Panels
entries.html: 29Judicial Panel decisions shall be reached by simple majority.

entries.title: Decision
path: Part Two - Procedural rules applicable to Judicial Panels
entries.html: 30Judicial Panels may refer to any evidence or submissions as it considers necessary in its written decision, notwithstanding that such decision may be published.

entries.title: Decision
path: Part Two - Procedural rules applicable to Judicial Panels
entries.html:
31A decision of a Judicial Panel to:

31.1withdraw or suspend a Licence for a period of 3 months or more; or

31.2declare a Person to be a Disqualified Person,

shall take effect immediately on the announcement of the decision, unless the BHA or a Judicial Panel directs otherwise.

entries.title: Decision
path: Part Two - Procedural rules applicable to Judicial Panels
entries.html:
32Any decision not covered by paragraph 31 shall become effective

32.1after the time for bringing an appeal has expired, or

32.2if an appeal is brought, from 12.01 a.m. the day after the date on which the appeal:

32.2.1is finally determined by an Appeal Board;

32.2.2is abandoned; or

32.2.3fails by reason of non-prosecution,

unless the Appeal Board directs otherwise.

entries.title: Commencement of proceedings
path: Part Three - Disciplinary Panels as a first instance body
entries.html:
33Where the BHA considers that there has been a breach of the Rules, it may commence disciplinary proceedings by serving on a person (hereafter a Respondent):

33.1details of the alleged breach(es), to include a summary of the case against them;

33.2a copy of the documents relied upon including witness statements; and

33.3a copy of the Charge Response Form.

entries.title: Commencement of proceedings
path: Part Three - Disciplinary Panels as a first instance body
entries.html: 34The BHA may bring new charges against a Respondent notwithstanding that it has served the items listed in paragraph 33.

entries.title: Charge Response Form
path: Part Three - Disciplinary Panels as a first instance body
entries.html:
35Each Respondent must complete the Charge Response Form by stating:

35.1whether they admit or deny each alleged breach;

35.2their response to the evidence against them, irrespective of whether they admit or deny the charges;

35.3where the breaches are admitted, any representations on sanction;

35.4the name of any witness they intend to call to give oral evidence at the hearing, together with a witness statement or summary of the witness’ proposed oral evidence; and

35.5where they deny each alleged breach or make partial admissions, and where the BHA relies on witness evidence, any witnesses they want to question at the hearing (for the avoidance of doubt, where a Respondent does not notify of a wish to question a witness called by the BHA, that witness’ evidence shall be deemed to be accepted).

entries.title: Charge Response Form
path: Part Three - Disciplinary Panels as a first instance body
entries.html: 36The Charge Response Form must be accompanied by copies of all evidence, documents and written submissions upon which the Respondent intends to rely unless the BHA agrees to an extension of time to the period stated on the form.

entries.title: Charge Response Form
path: Part Three - Disciplinary Panels as a first instance body
entries.html: 37The Charge Response Form must be served on the BHA within the period stated on the form, unless the BHA agrees to an extension of time or such other time as the Disciplinary Panel chairperson orders..

entries.title: Charge Response Form
path: Part Three - Disciplinary Panels as a first instance body
entries.html:
38If a Respondent introduces evidence late, the Disciplinary Panel may:

38.1allow or refuse the admission of that evidence; or

38.2adjourn a hearing.

entries.title: Charge Response Form
path: Part Three - Disciplinary Panels as a first instance body
entries.html: 39Where a hearing is adjourned in accordance with paragraph 38.2 the Disciplinary Panel may make an order for costs against the Respondent.

entries.title: Charge Response Form
path: Part Three - Disciplinary Panels as a first instance body
entries.html: 40The BHA may offer the Respondent the opportunity to enter into the fast track process in accordance with the Fast Track Protocol.

entries.title: Charge Response Form
path: Part Three - Disciplinary Panels as a first instance body
entries.html: 41Upon review of the Charge Response Form and the accompanying materials, the BHA may provide the Respondent with any further evidence or material on which it intends to rely. The Respondent will be given an opportunity to respond to that evidence or material.

entries.title: Charge Response Form
path: Part Three - Disciplinary Panels as a first instance body
entries.html: 42The Disciplinary Panel may make an interim decision affecting a penalty or award, order or other sanction.

entries.title: Plea agreements
path: Part Three - Disciplinary Panels as a first instance body
entries.html:
43The BHA and the Respondent may attempt to agree:

43.1that the Respondent admits a charge in return for a reduced sanction;

43.2that the Respondent admits one or more charges in return for others not being pursued by the BHA; and / or

43.3some or all of the facts relating to the charge,(a Plea Agreement).

(a Plea Agreement).

entries.title: Plea agreements
path: Part Three - Disciplinary Panels as a first instance body
entries.html: 44If a Plea Agreement is sought by the Respondent, they should request discussions at an early stage.

entries.title: Plea agreements
path: Part Three - Disciplinary Panels as a first instance body
entries.html:
45A Plea Agreement is always subject to the approval of the Disciplinary Panel so it can assess whether the agreement:

45.1accurately and appropriately reflects the available evidence; and

45.2is fair and in the interests of justice.

entries.title: Plea agreements
path: Part Three - Disciplinary Panels as a first instance body
entries.html:
46If a Plea Agreement is agreed the Disciplinary Panel must be provided with:

46.1full details of the Plea Agreement; and

46.2the facts of the case which should, where possible, be agreed.

entries.title: Plea agreements
path: Part Three - Disciplinary Panels as a first instance body
entries.html: 47If agreement is reached on certain issues, but not others, the BHA and the Respondent may agree to seek directions from the Disciplinary Panel as to how to proceed.

entries.title: Plea agreements
path: Part Three - Disciplinary Panels as a first instance body
entries.html: 48The Disciplinary Panel will not be informed of discussions if they do not result in agreement. However, the Disciplinary Panel and any other party to the proceedings may be informed of any relevant documents or information referred to during those discussions that is not already before the Disciplinary Panel, including any admissions made.

entries.title: Hearings
path: Part Three - Disciplinary Panels as a first instance body
entries.html:
49The chairperson of the Disciplinary Panel shall ensure a fair procedure, as part of which a Respondent shall be given the opportunity to put their case and question witnesses.

Owner’s rights

entries.title: Hearings
path: Part Three - Disciplinary Panels as a first instance body
entries.html:
50If a hearing concerns the possible disqualification or suspension of a horse, or the possible alteration of places, the Owner or Owner’s Representative will:

50.1be given notice of the hearing,

50.2upon request, be provided with all documents relied upon by the BHA; and

50.3on notice to the BHA, be permitted to attend the hearing with legal representation and to question witnesses and make submissions.

entries.title: Hearings
path: Part Three - Disciplinary Panels as a first instance body
entries.html: 51If a horse is owned by more than one Person, only one of them may attend a hearing as a representative of the Owners.

entries.title: Disciplinary Panel Decision
path: Part Three - Disciplinary Panels as a first instance body
entries.html: 52The Disciplinary Panel shall have the power to impose any one or more of the sanctions set out in Chapter L.

entries.title: Disciplinary Panel Decision
path: Part Three - Disciplinary Panels as a first instance body
entries.html: 53The Disciplinary Panel shall provide written reasons for its decision within 20 working days of the conclusion of the hearing (except in exceptional circumstances, where further time may be required). The written reasons shall include sufficient detail to allow the parties to understand the Disciplinary Panel's decision and which material facts have been relied upon.

entries.title: Costs
path: Part Three - Disciplinary Panels as a first instance body
entries.html: 54Except where otherwise provided, a Disciplinary Panel shall have the power to make such order as to costs against a Person as it considers appropriate.

entries.title: Appeals
path: Part Three - Disciplinary Panels as a first instance body
entries.html: 55A party to proceedings may appeal a decision of a Disciplinary Panel to an Appeal Board within 7 days of receipt of the full written reasons.

entries.title: Standing
path: Part Four - Disciplinary Panels as an appellate body
entries.html:
56The following decisions can be appealed to a Disciplinary Panel:

56.1subject to Rule (H)34, a decision of a Stewards Enquiry;

56.2a substituted decision of the BHA in accordance with Rule (L)7;

56.3a decision to prohibit an Overseas Jockey from taking part in any Race(s) in accordance with Rule (L)14; 

56.4a decision of the BHA to issue an Exclusion Order in accordance with Rule (L)13 and / or

56.5a decision of the Whip Review Committee

entries.title: Commencing an Appeal
path: Part Four - Disciplinary Panels as an appellate body
entries.html:
57An appeal is commenced by lodging a notice of appeal with the BHA within seven days of notice of the relevant decision, except where:

57.1the decision of the Stewards relates to a breach of Rule (F)37; or

57.2a Jockey has been suspended from riding,

in which case the appeal must be commenced within two working days of notice of the decision.

entries.title: Commencing an Appeal
path: Part Four - Disciplinary Panels as an appellate body
entries.html: 58The notice of appeal must state the grounds of appeal in general terms.

entries.title: Commencing an Appeal
path: Part Four - Disciplinary Panels as an appellate body
entries.html:
59A notice of appeal will be invalid unless it is accompanied by a deposit of:

59.1in the case of an appeal by an Apprentice Jockey, a Conditional Jockey or Amateur Jockey:

59.1.1£110, where a financial penalty not exceeding £500 was imposed; or

59.1.2£250 otherwise;

59.2in any other case:

59.2.1£220, where a financial penalty not exceeding £500 was imposed; or

59.2.2£500 otherwise.

entries.title: Commencing an Appeal
path: Part Four - Disciplinary Panels as an appellate body
entries.html:
60Where a Person appeals a decision of the Stewards, the BHA will provide a transcript of the Stewards Enquiry to the Person as soon as practicable.

Determination on written submissions

entries.title: Commencing an Appeal
path: Part Four - Disciplinary Panels as an appellate body
entries.html:
61An Appellant can request that the appeal is considered on the papers. Where the Appellant does so, the Disciplinary Panel may require that they submit a signed witness statement or summary of evidence.

Procedure

entries.title: Commencing an Appeal
path: Part Four - Disciplinary Panels as an appellate body
entries.html:
62The Disciplinary Panel shall set directions as required for the conduct of the appeal.

Consideration by the Disciplinary Panel and Decision

entries.title: Commencing an Appeal
path: Part Four - Disciplinary Panels as an appellate body
entries.html:
63The Disciplinary Panel may confirm or reverse or otherwise vary the decision appealed and may:

63.1where the appeal is made from a decision of a Stewards Enquiry; or

63.2where the appeal is made from a substituted decision of the BHA in accordance with Rule (L)7, impose any one or more of the sanctions that would have been available to the Stewards.

entries.title: Commencing an Appeal
path: Part Four - Disciplinary Panels as an appellate body
